articleTitle: Lightweight CNN for Sorghum Plant Counting: A Patch-Wise Approach
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Decision Aid Sciences and Applications (DASA)
abstract: Agriculture plays a vital role in the economies of developing nations, serving as both a subsistence and a source of wealth. To mitigate the risks of insufficient production and food scarcity, numerous agricultural output forecasting techniques have been developed. While traditional methods often rely on satellite data, recent advancements in deep learning and UAV (Unmmaned Aerial Vehicle) technology have opened new avenues for plant phenotyping. Early-stage plant counting is a key strategy for yield forecasting. However, manual crop counting is a time-consuming and labor-intensive task. To address this, high-throughput, automated plant counting methods are essential. This study proposes an approach for plant counting in sorghum crops using aerial images. Our method employs a patch-wise approach, where each image is divided into smaller patches. A complexity-optimized DCNN model is then applied to each patch to estimate the number of plants. By utilizing a regression layer, the model predicts the plant count for each patch. Our proposed method outperforms solutions based on known CNN architectures on the same dataset, achieving a lower Mean Absolute Error (MAE) with fewer parameters. This demonstrates the effectiveness of our approach in accurately counting plants in agricultural fields.

articleTitle: Method to Optimize Space Function Distribution in FM by Employing BIM
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Decision Aid Sciences and Applications (DASA)
abstract: The research paper presents a method to employ building information modelling (BIM) in facilities management (FM) to optimize space function distribution. The research paper provides insights into the use of BIM (7D model) in FM strategies, aiming to enhance FM operations overall and, more specifically, space function distribution. The methodology bridges the gap in FM processes through two complementary analyses: mathematical analysis and 7D model-based analysis. A mall case study is employed to highlight the method effectiveness. This research opens up new avenues for the application of FM processes, utilizing real-time data and 7D BIM models.

articleTitle: Detection and Classification of Corn Plant Diseases Using Computer Vision
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Decision Aid Sciences and Applications (DASA)
abstract: The goal of this paper is to create a sophisticated computer vision model that is especially intended for the automatic identification and categorization of diseases affecting corn plants. The study uses cutting-edge deep learning architectures like ResNet50, VGG16, MobileNet, and Xception to improve disease identification in maize crops in terms of both efficiency and accuracy. The study includes a thorough analysis of existing approaches, with an emphasis on modifying these strategies to address the unique difficulties presented by maize pathology. Advanced image processing techniques will be used to carefully curate and compile a high-quality image dataset of maize plants exhibiting various illnesses. By incorporating the chosen model into an intuitive platform, the goal is to close the knowledge gap between cutting edge AI technology and useful agricultural solutions. This program aims to improve crop management methods by providing a dependable and effective way to detect diseases, which will ultimately lead to higher agricultural output and sustainability. The paper aims to establish a new benchmark in the use of deep learning for agricultural disease management through ongoing improvement and validation.

articleTitle: The Medina of Al Hoceima (Morocco): Seismic Risk Assessment of Architecturally Irregular Buildings
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Decision Aid Sciences and Applications (DASA)
abstract: Assessing seismic vulnerability is of crucial importance in establishing the degree of resilience of existing buildings to earthquakes. Unfortunately, the northern region of Morocco has witnessed several devastating earthquakes in recent years, resultant in loss of life and considerable material damage. Al Hoceima is in an area characterized by intense seismic activity, where the terrain displays slopes ranging from 10 % to 40 %, in this context, the major objective of the present study is to strengthen our understanding of the inherent seismic vulnerability of irregular architectural structures when subjected to seismic loads.

articleTitle: Arabic Sign Language Recognition Chatbot for Decision Making in Healthcare
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Decision Aid Sciences and Applications (DASA)
abstract: This paper presents the development of a healthcareoriented chatbot system designed to facilitate communication for hearing-impaired individuals by recognizing Arabic sign language (ArSL). To identify the most effective deep learning model for this application, we conducted a comparative analysis of four widely used pretrained image classifiers-VGG16, ResNet50, InceptionV3, and EfficientNetB0-on the RGB Arabic Alphabet Sign Language Dataset (AASL). Through extensive experimentation, we selected the best model based on accuracy for integration into the chatbot system, which will process sequences of ArSL gesture images, translate them into sentences, and enable real-time, accessible interactions in healthcare settings. This approach underscores the potential of deep learning to enhance healthcare accessibility, providing a practical, AI-driven communication solution for hearing-impaired individuals.

articleTitle: Detecting Emergent Behaviors with an Expert System in Complex System
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Decision Aid Sciences and Applications (DASA)
abstract: The notion of emergence is one of the most discussed topics in the world today, understanding the causes of emergent behavior in terms of system components, their attributes, and their interactions is critical in order to influence the appearance of desired emergent properties and the reduction of any undesired effects. However, the inability to predict and control emergent phenomena prevents us from exploring its full potential. In addition, the article explores how interactions can be used as a metric to identify emergent behaviors in the Boids model and outlines the initial effects of a four step process: (1)representation and acquisition of simulation data and human knowledge, (2)Rule-based transformation of the data,(3)Building of the inference engine, (4)Learning process and emergence detection. Furthermore, the update of the rule base with new rules when a new unknown behavior appears. Since this is a part of ongoing research, future direction is also discussed.

articleTitle: Factors Influencing Foreign Direct Investment In Oman
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Decision Aid Sciences and Applications (DASA)
abstract: We investigate the factors that affect foreign direct investment in Oman. The research provides an empirical evidence of how various factors including economic factors, political factors, regulatory factors and free economic zones impact foreign direct investment in Oman. The research is quantitative in nature in which researchers collected numerical data from research participants who are economic experts in Oman. The sample size for this research is 47 which was selected through random sampling method. The findings revealed that economic, political, regulatory and free economic zones are the factors that have positive and significant impact on foreign direct investment in Oman.

articleTitle: Optimizing Activation Functions for Intrusion Detection Systems Using Evolutionary Algorithms
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Decision Aid Sciences and Applications (DASA)
abstract: This paper explores the importance of activation functions in enhancing the performance of intrusion detection systems (IDSs) using deep learning. Traditional activation functions such as ReLU, Sigmoid, and Tanh face issues like vanishing gradients and information loss. To address this, the authors propose a Genetic Algorithm (GA)-based framework to evolve new activation functions tailored for IDS. Tested on two datasets NSL-KDD and CICIDS 2017, these optimized functions improved detection accuracy by up to 3% and reduced false positives, demonstrating the effectiveness of evolutionary optimization to strengthen IDS in cybersecurity.

articleTitle: What is the Role of Governments in Achieving the SDGS? Empirical Evidence from EU Countries
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Decision Aid Sciences and Applications (DASA)
abstract: This research aimed to examine the role of governments in achieving sustainable development goals in EU nations from 2010 to 2021. The Autoregressive Distributed Lag (ARDL) approach was used to analyze the relationship between government spending on environmental protection, human development, energy consumption, and environmental innovations between 2010 and 2020. The study aimed to identify the main issues affecting government spending and environmental protection rates. The research also explored measures to help European nations establish growth and develop in a green environment without financial spending. The results showed a strong negative association between financial development, green energy consumption, consumption, scientific innovations, human capital, and the acceleration rate of government spending on environmental protection. However, the positive association was confirmed with fossil fuel consumption. The research aimed to understand the factors motivating European nations to achieve long-term development goals.

articleTitle: Exploring Machine Learning Classifiers for Identifying Gestational Diabetes Mellitus
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Decision Aid Sciences and Applications (DASA)
abstract: Gestational diabetes mellitus (GDM) is a con-dition in which a hormone produced by the placenta disrupts the body's ability to use insulin efficiently. Early diagnosis of GDM risk is essential since it can lead to more effective treatments and less cumulative effects. The purpose of this study aims to investigate an efficient model for early identification of GDM using commonly accessible parameters to enable early intervention. The project aims to use prediction algorithms in locations where more thorough assessments are unavailable. Multiple classifiers are created that function well in diagnosing GDM having accuracies ranging from 93% to 90.5%. KNN and XGB classifiers achieved 95% accuracy, which is the best among all classifiers. This suggests employing these classifiers to create a GDM detection system.

articleTitle: Decision Support for Building Thermal Comfort Monitoring with a Sustainable GenAI System
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Decision Aid Sciences and Applications (DASA)
abstract: Staff expenses can account for up to 70% of business costs, with indoor conditions playing a critical role in employee health, behavior, and productivity. Optimal thermal comfort, typically around 21°C with 40-70% humidity, maximizes productivity. However, effective monitoring requires comprehensive data, particularly as energy regulations push for smarter building management. Although Building Information Modeling (BIM, a digital representation of a building's physical and functional characteristics) and sensor integration support facilities management, many existing systems are proprietary, expensive, and inflexible. To address these challenges, this study introduces ThermalComfortBot, a sustainable Generative Artificial Intelligence (GenAI)-powered Chatbot designed as an advanced Information System (IS). Utilizing Large Language Models (LLMs, AI models for natural language understanding) and Retrieval-Augmented Generation (RAG, a method that combines data retrieval with LLMs-generated insights), ThermalComfortBot integrates data from BIM, sensors, and other relevant sources. Built on open-source technology, it is cost-effective and fully customizable, allowing users to tailor datasets to their needs. The Chatbot delivers actionable insights through a Question-Answering (QA) interface, enabling data-driven decisions on thermal comfort to improve workplace conditions and enhance operational efficiency.

articleTitle: Expert-Decision-Based Scheduling Strategies for Construction Projects Management
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Decision Aid Sciences and Applications (DASA)
abstract: This paper presents an alternative methodology to the traditional Project Evaluation and Review Technique (PERT) by introducing the Dempster-Shafer theory of evidence into project scheduling. The evidence theory provides a flexible and robust framework for managing subjective beliefs, extending beyond PERT's rigid assumptions regarding activity durations and aligning more closely with the inherent uncertainties of real-world project environments. The proposed evidential reasoning approach enhances flexibility in estimating activity durations by leveraging expert judgment rather than relying on fixed probability distributions. Unlike PERT, which strictly assumes a beta distribution and fixed percentages for optimistic, most likely, and pessimistic estimates, this approach enables experts to adjust these percentages dynamically based on real-time project conditions. Through a detailed case study on a bridge construction project, this paper demonstrates the advantages of evidential reasoning in addressing limitations of traditional PERT. A comparative analysis validates the Dempster-Shafer theory's effectiveness, showing improved scheduling outcomes and adaptability.

articleTitle: Innovative Energy Management in Renewable Systems Through the application of Multi-Stage Thermal Energy Storage in Solar Power Plant
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Decision Aid Sciences and Applications (DASA)
abstract: This study presents a detailed investigation into thermal energy storage (TES) systems, with a focus on multi-stage phase change materials (PCMs) in concentrated solar power (CSP) plants. The novelty of the research lies in demonstrating how multi-stage PCM configurations can optimize both energy storage and release by capturing a broader temperature range, enhancing the efficiency and dispatchability of renewable energy systems. By addressing the interplay between natural convection and heat transfer mechanisms in PCM arrangements, the paper offers insights into improving TES performance. This work is significant for future renewable energy applications, particularly for stabilizing grids and increasing the reliability of solar power integration.

articleTitle: Hybrid Deep Convolutional Neural Networks Combined with Autoencoders and Augmented Data to Predict the Look-Up Table 2006
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Decision Aid Sciences and Applications (DASA)
abstract: Lookup tables derived from empirical research contain limited data for critical heat flux (CHF). Machine learning techniques can be employed to create CHF prediction models by training them with existing experimental-based CHF lookup tables. Consequently, these models can generate CHF look-up tables that provide expected CHF values for a wider variety of scenarios. This study presents a novel predictive method integrating auto-encoders with deep convolutional neural networks (DCNN). The purpose is to obtain precise and reliable predictions for CHF retrieval. The accuracy of these models was evaluated utilizing the coefficient of determination (R<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sup>), Nash-Sutcliffe efficiency (NSE), mean absolute error (MAE), and normalized root-mean-squared error (NRMSE). The findings demonstrate that the suggested hybrid model reveals an important degree of accuracy.

articleTitle: Deformable Convolutional Networks-Based Instance-Specific Coefficients of On-tree Mango Segmentation
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Decision Aid Sciences and Applications (DASA)
abstract: This research does provide an approach for the detection of mangoes on trees with the use of deformable convolutional networks concentrating on imaging at nighttime. The method used in the mango detection and segmentation is YOLACT++ which is critical in estimating the sizes of fruits in remote sensing applications. The evidence from experiments shows the effectiveness of the proposed model in various lighting conditions. Despite this, it means that this model yields high detection accuracy particularly at night where confidence scores are above 0.90 for light and noise. During the daytime, images capture by the model show better segmentation accuracy and detection probabilities of the model. The average precision of detection (AP) for bounding boxes is in the 53.45 – 79.67 range, with AP exceeding 80% at lower Intersection over Union (IoU) values (0.5–0.7). However, the localization of the mangoes has remained a task when correctly estimating them using higher IoU thresholds of 0.75 to 0.95. These achievements further confirm that YOLACT++ can perform mango instance segmentation and suitable for real-life uses, including agricultural surveillance and fruit measurement.

articleTitle: Management Decision Strategies in Commercial Spaceflight Tourism: Exploring Stakeholder Attitudes and Environmental Implications of Suborbital and Orbital Travel
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Decision Aid Sciences and Applications (DASA)
abstract: Commercial suborbital and orbital travel present a promising opportunity for the sustained advancement of outer space exploration and the popularisation of the Commercial Spaceflight Tourism (CST) phenomenon. But, despite the optimistic outlook space exploration carries for humanity and science, CST trips have left their mark on the Earth's atmosphere and outer layers in several ways, raising questions and doubts among the program's stakeholders about such initiatives' environmental implications and placing emphasis on how this can affect these key players attitude towards space travel in a way that may impede the long-term growth of the CST market. Therefore, this study extends the knowledge of the past few decades of scholarly work on stakeholder theory, while correlating it with the notion of space flight missions, the launch phases, and the detrimental effects they yield. This work also uncovers the conceptual relation of stakeholders and thus determines how different environmental factors can shift the attitudes and power attributes of the sector's stakeholders.

articleTitle: Personalized Shopping Experiences: Leveraging Big Data Analytics in E-commerce for Enhanced Customer Engagement
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Decision Aid Sciences and Applications (DASA)
abstract: E-commerce systems have integrated big data analytics (BDA) as a core element, enabling personalized shopping experiences, crucial for customer loyalty and satisfaction. This research explores how intentional use of data analytics impacts customers and signals the combined effect of technology and market data in tailoring customer needs through innovation. We developed unique data mining processes from e-commerce archives to uncover patterns in customer behavior, aiming to simplify consumer analysis and identify factors influencing purchasing and loyalty barriers. Our research also tests personalization strategies on sample data to improve key performance indicators like conversion rates, average order value, and customer retention. Ethical data use and privacy are prioritized, ensuring trust and transparency between e-commerce platforms and consumers. This study is innovative, demonstrating the power of analytics to revolutionize e-commerce by prioritizing customer needs and sustainable growth.

articleTitle: Combination of Blockchain and Machine Learning for the Improvement of Decision Making and Secure Supply Chain Authentication Management
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Decision Aid Sciences and Applications (DASA)
abstract: This justifies the feature of blockchain in decision-making where companies predominantly use data processing and managing methods or have intricate supply chains demanding authenticity and relying on blockchain technology. This study is motivated by increasing convolutions and demands for secure speedy supply chain system as it is important in nurturing trustworthiness and accountability during commercial transactions, so it focuses on showing why current supply chain authentication methods are inefficient and unreliable leading to potential frauds and mistrust. This research starts by reviewing existing supply chain authentication methods and their shortcomings. The Basics of Blockchain refer to How Decentralized and Secure it really is, explaining what blockchain technology is. This blog post discusses how blockchain can be used to enhance decision-making processes, providing an unchangeable, auditable way to keep track of and authenticate the supply chain, and briefly covers various use cases of blockchain in supply chains and explains how they are transforming the security and efficiency of operations. The objective of this study is to suggest a structure that combines blockchain and machine learning for better supply chain decisions and authentication systems. It makes use of decentralized system architecture from methodological point of view by which the immutability aspect of blockchain and machine learning analytics can be integrated together in forecasting of demand while at the same time ensuring safety for transactions. Overall, blockchain technology enables significant disruption in supply chain authentication by helping partner systems and organizations make better decisions and reinforcing security requirements between partners. Combined with blockchain, RFIDs provide improved transparency and cost savings and ensure data is secure and trustworthy, thereby greatly enhancing supply chain networks. Indeed, the findings have shown clearly that coherent use of these technologies in supply chain management yields tangible improvements in such areas as fraud prevention, operational efficiency and even customer trust.

articleTitle: Literary Analysis: Disruptive Technologies and Digital Transformation in Residential Real Estate
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Decision Aid Sciences and Applications (DASA)
abstract: Digital transformation has become essential for organizations of all sizes as they navigate the complexities of an increasingly digital landscape. This paper explores the implementation of disruptive technologies within the real estate industry, particularly in the areas of leasing and property management for both new rentals and renewals. It reviews current trends and innovations that are reshaping the industry, such as blockchain for transparent transactions, artificial intelligence for predictive analytics, and smart building technologies for enhanced property management. The necessity of digital transformation is highlighted as a means to achieve competitive advantage in today's fast-paced market, where consumer expectations are continually evolving. By adopting these technologies, real estate firms can improve operational efficiency, enhance customer experiences, and better position themselves against competitors. The findings underscore the critical importance of embracing digital transformation to thrive in the modern real estate landscape.

articleTitle: Green Growth and Financial Development in OECD Economics
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Decision Aid Sciences and Applications (DASA)
abstract: The paper investigates the banking system's effect on green economics in OECD economics. It investigates the relationship among factors such as sustainable energy utilization, human capital, sustainable energy technologies, financial expansion, ecological footprint, and green growth during 2010–2020. The study employs the three ARDL models containing;[PMG; MG; DFE]. Finally, Dumitrescu and Horlin causality test was used to see the causal relationship between the variables. The results suggest that human capital, financial development, renewable energy, and technologies promote green economic growth. The causality test results demonstrate that human capital development and FD have a bidirectional causal link with green economics.

articleTitle: A Comprehensive Overview of Formal Methods and Deep Learning for Verification and Optimization
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Decision Aid Sciences and Applications (DASA)
abstract: Formal approaches, which have their roots in logic and mathematics, offer reliable guarantees of the accuracy of software systems. Many strategies have been developed, including model checking, deductive verification, and static analysis. These methods attempt to overcome issues such as undecidability and scalability, which are brought to light by Rice's Theorem and restrict our capacity to develop instruments that can consistently ascertain the correctness of a program. In deductive verification, the work by Floyd, Hoare, and Naur, check program requirements are using logic; nevertheless, further annotations are frequently needed for tractability. Model checking is beneficial for hardware verification and evaluates correctness using temporal logic, but it has trouble with infinite-state systems. By understanding programs at an abstract level, static analysis and abstract interpretation provide completely automated, scalable solutions that detect possible flaws without running the code. In order to overcome the challenge of demonstrating modern architectures like convolutional neural networks (CNNs), the paper also investigates the application of formal approaches to neural networks. The neural network features like resilience and safety against adversarial assaults are verified using techniques like SMT-based approaches and abstract interpretation frameworks like AI<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sup>, DeepZ, and DeepPoly. These tools demonstrate the growing importance of formal techniques in ensuring the security and reliability of neural networks, which are being used in more important systems.

articleTitle: Enhancing Tuberculosis Diagnosis with DenseNet121 and Grad-CAM: A Deep Learning Approach for Accurate and Interpretable Chest X-ray Analysis
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Decision Aid Sciences and Applications (DASA)
abstract: In this paper, GradCAM has been used with a DenseNet121 architecture for classifying Tuberculosis. The model was trained and evaluated over the dataset of 420 chest X-ray images for the classification of TB-positive versus TB-negative cases. Performance metrics denote an overall accuracy of 90.48%. This is with a precision of 90% and a recall of 100% for the TB negative class, and a precision of 100<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">%</sup> with a recall of 43 % for the TB positive class. The corresponding f1-scores for these classes are 0.95 and 0.60, respectively. The macro average f1-score stands at 0.77, thereby showing that on the whole, there is a fair amount of balance in performance across both classes. The weighted average f1-score Metropolitan: 0.89, indicating good overall performance but disparity in recall between classes. GradCAM visualizations enable a look at the areas of interest that the model focuses on while making predictions, providing insight into the decision-making process of DenseNet121. The study epitomizes both the potential and limitation of DenseNet121 on the classification of TB, pointing out a future road map for improvements in sensitivity toward TB-positive cases.

articleTitle: OptImal Resource Allocation Strategies in Engineering Projects Using Modern Algorithms
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Decision Aid Sciences and Applications (DASA)
abstract: Efficient resource allocation in engineering projects is a challenging task, especially under budget constraints and tight deadlines. Improper resource management can lead to cost overruns or significant delays in project completion. This study proposes approaches to optimizing financial decisions based on modeling and modern optimization algorithms. The problem lies in finding a balance between minimizing costs and reducing project completion time. To address this issue, a genetic algorithm and an ant colony algorithm were employed, demonstrating their effectiveness in resource allocation and cost reduction. The conducted experimental studies confirmed that the proposed approaches can significantly enhance the efficiency of managing engineering projects.

articleTitle: Purposing the Improvement Strategy of Distributing Ornamental Fish Based on SCOR 12.0 and AHP
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Decision Aid Sciences and Applications (DASA)
abstract: Ornamental fish is unique and a commodity in the fisheries sector in high demand. The distribution system often has shortcomings that cause physiological stress due to shocks and changes in conditions, water quality, oxygen capacity, temperature, and longer distribution times. Fish mortality is the main obstacle that impacts distributors, and the supply chain performance must be enhanced. Therefore, an assessment is needed to evaluate whether the business meets the required standards. This study aims to determine the value of reliability performance attributes at the distributor. The method used was quantitative. Data was obtained from ornamental fish distributors in Mina Restu Ornamental Fish Market, Banyumas Regency. The data was obtained by conducting observations and interviews, which refers to using the supply chain performance measurement (SCOR) 12.0 and analytical hierarchy process (AHP) approaches. The result shows some underperforming KPIs. This happens because there is a problem with the KPI, such as the make-and-deliver process. The make process is yield, and the deliver process is the percentage of orders delivered in full, damage-free, and defect-free conformance. The improvement for the distributor can be enhanced by implementing good handling practices and improving workforce performance by providing some training to handle the fish. The excellent handling practice can consider internal factors such as packaging conditions and external factors such as weather. The distributor can train the workforce to follow customer requirements and minimize the risk.

articleTitle: A Virtual Reality Face Recognition System for Revolutionizing Attendance Tracking
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Decision Aid Sciences and Applications (DASA)
abstract: Nowadays, taking attendance is crucial in classrooms. Participation in teaching and learning sessions is a key predictor of student achievement and commitment to academic pursuits. However, traditional manual methods in universities are often slow and prone to errors. To address the problem, this project introduces Vista Attend, a VR face recognition attendance system designed to streamline attendance recording. Using a VR device like Meta Quest with Vista Attend, lecturers can scan students' faces, automatically recording attendance in real-time. A database stores students' facial profiles and basic information, which can be accessed in Augmented Reality through the VR headset, enabling lecturers to view student profiles, including matric numbers, names, and faculties. This feature allows lecturers to familiarize themselves with their students visually and is beneficial for personal academic interaction since most lecturers cannot recognize their students. This system will be developed using Unity as the platform, and an application was crafted to operate optimally on a VR device. Vista Attend will significantly enhance the speed and reliability of attendance recording. Also, it will replace traditional methods and become a major method in the future. Compared to traditional methods, this application offers a more streamlined and user-friendly experience, and users can significantly reduce attendance fraud and avoid the absence of accurate attendance reports. In summary, this research presents a practical integration of face recognition and VR technology for the educational sector, suggesting that universities might benefit from adopting such advancements to modernize students' attendance tracking procedures.

articleTitle: The Influence of Using Statistical Software on Educational Decision Making in Jordan Private Universities
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Decision Aid Sciences and Applications (DASA)
abstract: This study aims to examine the influence of using Statistical Software (SPSS) on the educational decision-making processes of private universities in Jordan, as perceived by students. Additionally, the objective is to measure the relationships among the dimensions of Statistical Software, specifically focusing on Education & Training, and Facilities & Financial Support. The research utilized a quantitative methodology. The researcher designed the questionnaire to comprehensively cover all the variables under examination. The researcher selected a sample size of 60 students from private universities in Jordan using a simple random sample. The researcher employed SPSS version 27 for statistical analysis, which included descriptive analysis such as calculating the mean and standard deviation. Additionally, the inferential analysis encompassed regression analysis, Pearson correlations, and Cronbach's alpha. The findings show that Education & Training, Facilities & Financial Support have a significant influence on educational decision-making. In addition, the SPSS software's results showed a strong correlation between each statistical software dimension and other dimensions.

articleTitle: Role of Artificial Intelligence Applications on Engineering Decision Making: Mediation Effects of Value Co-Creation
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Decision Aid Sciences and Applications (DASA)
abstract: To enhance decision making processes among engineering industries, the main objective of this research is to explain the role of AI-Enabled applications on decision making processes rely on the mediation effect of value co-creations determinants within engineering companies in Jordan. Based on a quantitative design, the target sample were asked to provide their perspectives in accordance with a questionnaire approach. The results of this study retrieved based on Structural Equation model method. The outcomes show that AI-Enabled applications confirm a positive influence on value co-creation determinants. Moreover, the results uncover that value co-creation determinants conform a considerable influence on decision-making processes. Furthermore, the outcomes discover that value co-creation determinants strongly mediate the relationship between AI-Enabled applications and decisionmaking processes. Lastly, the findings of this study provide new insights for managers and top management of engineering companies that investing in AI tools have an ability to offer various benefits and take attention toward reinforcing value co-creation as a strategic resource.

articleTitle: Multi-Seasonal Modeling of Energy Consumption in a Building: Integration of Sub-Models with Switching
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Decision Aid Sciences and Applications (DASA)
abstract: This paper introduces a novel approach for predicting electric energy consumption in buildings throughout the year using meteorological variables such as outdoor temperature, indoor temperature, atmospheric pressure, and outdoor humidity. Specifically, the method involves the development of a comprehensive seasonal Random Forest (RF) model that dynamically adjusts to different seasons-winter, summer, spring, and autumn-based on the calendar date. Furthermore, the sub-models demonstrate robust performance; for instance, the summer model achieves a root mean square error (RMSE) of 59 Wh during testing, while the winter model reaches a coefficient of determination (R2) of 95 % and 61 % in the training and testing phases respectively. Ultimately, this multi-input modeling approach provides significant improvements in reconstructing seasonal energy consumption patterns. To evaluate the performance and effectiveness of the proposed approach, we employed cross-validation, ensuring a comprehensive analysis of our sub-models across all data samples. This method led to reliable results across the four folds for all seasons, with an R2 of 65% and 60% in fold 4 for the winter and autumn seasons, respectively.

articleTitle: Identity Recognition Using Wavelet-Based Neural Networks: Review and Comparative Study
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Decision Aid Sciences and Applications (DASA)
abstract: Wavelet neural networks are a unique combination of wavelet analysis and neural network architectures, thus providing the benefits of advanced signal processing. Unlike traditional methods, WNNs offer a multi-resolution approach that outshines for nonstationary signals; therefore, these are very useful in applications related to areas such as biomedical signal analysis, image processing, and time-series forecasting. Architecture of WNNs enables the replacement of activation functions with wavelet functions for the extraction of localized features, making both processing and interpretation of data much more efficient. Some of the recent improvements in designing WNNs improve its computational efficiency to suit the requirements of real-time applications and also to incorporate it into deep learning frameworks, but still, one of the main challenges faced in WNNs such as computational complexity and scalability need to be addressed. As the historical development, core contributions, and evolving architecture of WNNs is done, this paper represents those along with filling up certain existing research gaps. This research paper addresses future directions regarding hybrid models that combine synergies of CNNs with RNNs as well as WNNs and therefore posits opening its way for enhanced performance across various domains. Researching such an area ensures and guarantees further expansion of applications in WNNs besides strengthening their importance in signal processing in the modern arena.

articleTitle: Artificial Neural Network (ANN) Model for the Prediction of Shear Strength of Exterior RC Beam-Column Joints: A Conceptual Model
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Decision Aid Sciences and Applications (DASA)
abstract: One of Machine Learning (ML) techniques that can be used for engineering applications is Artificial Neural Network (ANN). In this paper, Machine Learning (ML) - Artificial Neural Network (ANN) has been utilized to predict the shear capacity of reinforced concrete (RC) beam-column joint (BCJ). In this study, data sets needed for the ANN model have been generated using Finite Element Analysis (FEA) software ABAQUS. ANN prediction model is proposed depending on 4320 total BCJ samples: (70<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">%</sup>) used for training, (15<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">%</sup>) for testing, and (15<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">%</sup>) for validation of the ANN model. The proposed model showed 95.6% accuracy in its prediction for shear capacity of RC BCJ testing data of 648 samples.

articleTitle: Endorsing Trust in Digital Engineering: Accredited Electronic Certificate and Their Reliability in Engineering Transactions
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Decision Aid Sciences and Applications (DASA)
abstract: This study aims to evaluate the trust certificate service providers emerged, as a neutral party mediating between the competent administrative body that grants the license and accreditation to the provider, and the public dealing with these electronic means, or what are called subscribers, so it was necessary to search in depth into the legal organization of the trust certificate service provider in light of the Electronic Communications and Transactions Law of 2018. The main findings of this study revealed that the legislator in the Electronic Communications and Transactions Law stipulated that trust service providers must obtain the necessary license from the competent administrative authority before practicing the activity, while the UNCITRAL Model Law on Electronic Signatures did not stipulate this. The legislator has recognized the validity of the authentication certificate issued by the trust service provider as long as it meets the requirements specified by a decision issued by the competent authority. This study recommends to include allows trust certificate service providers to disclose personal or financial information if there is written consent or in implementation of the provisions of the law.

articleTitle: Impact of Roof Thermal Insulation on Energy Performance in Buildings
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Decision Aid Sciences and Applications (DASA)
abstract: This research emphasizes the critical role of energy analysis in the early stages of architectural design. By focusing on roof insulation, a key factor influencing building energy performance, the research aim is to optimize energy consumption and enhance sustainable design practices. Three villas from a housing project in Bahrain serve as case studies to explore the impact of different roof insulation strategies. Through energy modelling and analysis, energy saving potential associated with various insulation configurations will be quantified. By analysing the results, energy-efficient design strategies will be established. This research contributes to a deeper understanding of the relationship between roof insulation and building energy performance, substantially leading to more sustainable and energy-efficient buildings.

articleTitle: Towards a Software Factory for Developing Recommender Systems and Decision Support Systems for Smart Tourism
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Decision Aid Sciences and Applications (DASA)
abstract: The development of smart systems is fundamental to improve the competitiveness of tourist destinations, by exploiting technologies such as Recommender Systems (RS) and Decision Support Systems (DSS). In this article, we propose an approach based on Model-Driven Engineering (MDE) for the creation of a software factory dedicated to the design of RS and DSS for tourism destination managers. This software factory is based on two main assets: a Domain-Specific Language (DSL) for recommendation systems and another DSL for decision support systems. The main aim of this approach is to reduce the complexity and development time of this type of application.

articleTitle: Multi-Criteria Decision Analysis to Assess the Efficacy of Cold Chain Technologies for Safeguarding the Quality of Temperature-Sensitive Products
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Decision Aid Sciences and Applications (DASA)
abstract: Cold Chain logistics (CCL) refers to the meticulous handling of food items that are temperature-sensitive from the point of production to the point of consumption. Furthermore, the CCL services ensure that the perishable items are stored and transported at predetermined temperatures to prevent microbial growth and to preserve the freshness/quality of the items. Conversely, ineffective and inefficient management of CCL services, might lead to safety and quality problems, such as pathogenic contamination, dehydration, excessive ripening, and discoloration, reducing the shelf life and appeal of the food items. Moreover, within today's landscape characterized by globalization, increased food miles, and ever evolving consumer needs to taste non-local foods, the CCL services are further obligated to safeguard the quality, towards providing healthy, and nutritious food to customers across the globe. In this pursuit, Cold Chain technologies such as Internet of Things (IoT), Block Chain (BCT) Systems, Integrated BCT and IoT systems, Intelligent Packaging (IP) Systems, Hyperspectral Imaging Systems (HIS), Digital Twin (DT) technologies etc., play a crucial role in optimally handling the food items from source to sink. However, the selection of the appropriate technology to safeguard the quality of food depends on diverse criteria. Consequently, research has been undertaken to identify the vital criteria for technological deployment within CCL's operating within developing nations. In this context, a few studies also concentrated on defining the selection criteria for each of the technological solutions. Nonetheless, a dearth of research is observed with regards to identifying a comprehensive list of criteria to comparatively assess the efficacy of the cold chain logistics technologies for safeguarding the quality of temperature-sensitive products within developing nations. Hence, this study aims at employing a hybrid multi-criteria decision-making approach for estimating the criteria weights in order to compare and evaluate the viability of cold chain technological alternatives for sustaining food quality.

articleTitle: The Role of IoT in Optimizing Urban Infrastructure in Smart Cities
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Decision Aid Sciences and Applications (DASA)
abstract: This research explores the role of the Internet of Things (IoT) in optimizing urban infrastructure in smart cities. Specifically, it examines how IoT enhances energy management, waste management, and public safety through real-time data collection and automated systems. The study adopts a descriptive-analytical approach, assessing existing smart city applications across several cities globally and their implications for improving urban services. The paper concludes that while IoT can transform urban environments, national-level strategies must consider local contexts to address infrastructure limitations, legal challenges, and privacy concerns. Recommendations are provided for developing a national IoT strategy tailored to specific urban needs.

articleTitle: Evaluating Machine Learning Classifiers for Predicting Liver Disease Outcomes
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Decision Aid Sciences and Applications (DASA)
abstract: The increasing prevalence of liver disease necessitates the development of accurate predictive models to aid in early diagnosis and treatment. This study investigates the effectiveness of several machine learning classifiers, Random Forest, Gradient Boosting, AdaBoost, Support Vector Machine (SVM), and Logistic Regression, in predicting liver disease outcomes based on clinical and biochemical features. Each model's performance was rigorously evaluated using multiple metrics, including F1-score, accuracy, root mean square error (RMSE), mean absolute error (MAE), precision, recall, and cross-validation ROC-AUC scores. The Random Forest Classifier emerged as the most effective model, achieving a perfect accuracy of 100% and an F1-score of 1.00, suggesting its robustness in handling complex, high-dimensional data. The Gradient Boosting Classifier also demonstrated commendable performance with an accuracy of 89% and an F1-score of 0.85, indicating its efficacy in capturing the underlying patterns of liver disease. Conversely, Logistic Regression and SVM exhibited lower performance metrics, pointing to potential limitations in their ability to model the intricacies of liver disease data effectively. The insights from this study not only enhance our understanding of liver disease prediction using machine learning but also emphasize the need for further research to validate these models in diverse clinical populations. This study contributes to the growing body of literature advocating for the integration of machine learning techniques in clinical decision-making processes, ultimately aiming to improve patient outcomes in liver disease management.

articleTitle: Dynamics of Climate-Related Financial Risks on Financial Stability: Evidence from OECD Countries
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Decision Aid Sciences and Applications (DASA)
abstract: The study examines the impact of climate change on the financial sector, focusing on the relationship between environmental taxes and financial stability in OECD nations. Results show a strong positive association between environmental taxation and financial stability, suggesting that raising environmental taxes can lead to financial sustainability. However, the study also highlights the negative trend in OECD nations' ability to adjust to natural disasters, which negatively affects their financial stability. The adaptive capacity dimension measures a country's ability to deal with disasters, considering government efforts, organized official activities, and existing infrastructure. The study found that OECD countries successfully established systems to handle calamities, thereby enhancing their financial stability.

articleTitle: MuSeRAN: Multimodal Sentiment Analysis with Recurrent Attention Networks
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Decision Aid Sciences and Applications (DASA)
abstract: This paper introduces a novel Multimodal Aspect-Based Sentiment Analysis (MABSA) methodology by creating a Multimodal Sentiment Analysis model utilizing Recurrent Attention Networks (MuSeRAN). The proposed framework uses the synergy between textual and visual data to improve sentiment classification. We use BERT and Bottom-Up Attention (BUA) models as encoders for text and images to guarantee efficient feature extraction. The primary innovation resides in the interactive fusion module, which amalgamates semantic representations at the token level and employs GRU cells to eliminate noise from the image data. Our iterative attention mechanism enhances aspect-specific sentiment features, facilitating progressive learning for improved classification efficacy. We assessed the proposed model using the Twitter-17 dataset with the Twitter-15 dataset, attaining results surpassing leading baselines. Findings demonstrate that multimodal models, including ours, surpass single-modal methods, significantly depending on text-based attributes for precise sentiment prediction. The T-test verifies the enhancements' statistical significance, affirming our model's robustness. This research underscores the importance of multimodal fusion methodologies in enhancing sentiment analysis applications.

articleTitle: Optimizing Outdoor Thermal Comfort with Pedestrian-Based Urban Greenery Planning: A Microclimate Simulation Study
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Decision Aid Sciences and Applications (DASA)
abstract: This study evaluates outdoor thermal comfort in Labban Square, El Mina, Lebanon, using ENVI-met, a microclimate simulation tool designed to support urban planning and outdoor environmental design. A pedestrian flow analysis was conducted to identify the primary walking path through the square, which guided the redesign of the urban greenery layout. The study includes a comparative assessment of thermal comfort before and after implementing the redesigned greenery plan. Results demonstrate the significant influence of urban greenery on improving the thermal comfort of the square, providing valuable insights into the role of vegetation in mitigating urban heat and enhancing outdoor spaces for pedestrians. By integrating pedestrian movement data with microclimate simulation, this research highlights the importance of green infrastructure in creating more livable and comfortable urban environments, especially in areas with hot climates. The findings also offer urban planners and landscape designers' practical guidance for optimizing outdoor thermal comfort through pedestrian-based urban greenery planning.

articleTitle: Engineering Decision Making: Impact of Digital Transformation on Administrative Procedures Development at the Ministry of Information in Bahrain
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Decision Aid Sciences and Applications (DASA)
abstract: This research aims to identify the impact of re-engineering the production processes of television programs in light of digital transformation (IT infrastructure, digital skills, strategy culture, leadership, competition and change) on the development of administrative procedures at the ministry of information in the Kingdom of Bahrain. Two hundred and sixty-seven employees were surveyed through a simple random sampling method. The analysis is based on the outcome of the questionnaire survey that was given out to a representative sample of the employees at the ministry in question. The researchers hypothesized that there is a significant impact for the re-engineering the production processes of television programs in light of digital transformation (IT infrastructure, digital skills, strategy culture, leadership, competition and change) on the development of administrative procedures at the ministry of information in the Kingdom of Bahrain. The results indicated that this hypothesis was accepted. Moreover, the results showed that there were no significant differences relating the impact of re-engineering the production processes of television programs in light of digital transformation with its dimensions in question on the development of administrative procedures at the ministry in question due to the demographics (gender, age, qualification, and years of experience), while there were differences due to the demographic (position).

Author Keywords: Re-engineering the Production Process of Television Programs

articleTitle: Gender in Governance: Essential or Outdated? A Bibliometric Analysis
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Decision Aid Sciences and Applications (DASA)
abstract: This study analyses whether gender research in corporate governance is still relevant. This paper presents a comprehensive literature review that focuses on the role and existence of gender in corporate governance through various global perspectives published in reputable international journals until 2024. Vosviewer software was used to analyze the data after the author used a variety of literature review approaches, such as content analysis to examine previous research. The collected manuscripts comprise 2500 papers published from 2014 to 2024, categorized into various research topics. The results of data mapping show that the topics have been widely researched are gender, education, woman, leadership, diversity, firm and performance in the 2021-2022 period. Meanwhile, research topics likely to be future research opportunities are gender equity, violence, discrimination, empowerment, degree, SDGs, government, and household.

articleTitle: Integrating Hierarchical Clustering and Stochastic Multi-Objective Decision-Making for Optimized Decision Processes
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Decision Aid Sciences and Applications (DASA)
abstract: Under uncertain business conditions, it might be challenging to manage the sustainable supplier selection challenge. This work is focused on applying a hybrid hierarchical cluster-stochastic optimization strategy to tackle the problem while considering robust and sustainable criteria. Initially, we recommend grouping high-dimensional supplier data using a hierarchical clustering algorithm. We created a stochastic goal programming model in the following phase to incorporate these factors into the decision-making procedure. The examination of the data reveals that the use of clustering algorithms improves supplier segmentation efficiency. The hybrid strategy that has been recommended is a helpful tool that reduces complexity, has the ability to be easily implemented, and elevates businesses' sustainable insights.

articleTitle: England: General Population Health Landscape
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Decision Aid Sciences and Applications (DASA)
abstract: This paper explores the population health of those living within England. With the health of the population facing changes, such as global aging, life expectancies and retirement ages have subsequently increased. Ethnic minorities have been found to be more susceptible to poorer health than their Caucasian counterparts, with minorities developing chronic diseases and disabilities. Therefore, this research delves into health, ethnicity, age and disability data, obtained from the 2021 UK Census, as well as the weekly Coronavirus datasets provided by the Mayor of London. Prior to conducting any analysis, all datasets were cleaned and transformed to exclude any data related to the Welsh population. The datasets were then visualised into graphs, such as bar, line and pie charts to display any relationships, but also frequencies of health across as-point Likert Scale: Very Good, Good, Fair, Bad and Very Bad. Overall, the research concluded that the majority of England's population have very good to good health, thus may be considered as healthy. Those living in the capital (London) are relatively healthier than those that live outside. But the health landscape has slightly adjusted since the onset of Coronavirus, with population health marginally decreasing as a consequence. Moreover, the paper possesses an opportunity to delve into the effects of Long Covid on England's population.

articleTitle: Machine Learning-Based Fault-Tolerant Inertial Navigation System for Micro Tunnel Boring Machines
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Decision Aid Sciences and Applications (DASA)
abstract: Underground tunneling poses a navigation challenge as Micro Tunnel Boring Machines (mTBMs) operate in GPS denied environments. In such settings, Inertial Measurement Units (IMUs) offer an alternative navigation solution. However, faults in mTBM operation caused by various environmental and operational factors lead to inaccuracies in IMU data. This paper presents a machine learning-based fault tolerance system for IMU based mTBM navigation. IMU data corresponding to four specific mTBM faults: vibration, high temperature, magnetic interference and mTBM precession were collected under rigorous testing in a lab environment. Support Vector Machine (SVM) was applied to classify these faults and predict the mTBM's operational state based on the IMU readings. The results demonstrate the effectiveness of the SVM model in identifying and classifying the faults, thereby enhancing the reliability and safety of mTBM operations in challenging environments.

articleTitle: Simulation and Analysis of TCP Tahoe on Wireless Sensor Network for Building Structure Condition Monitoring Topology
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Decision Aid Sciences and Applications (DASA)
abstract: Simulation and performance analysis of TCP Tahoe on WSN for building structure condition monitoring topology is important to understand the behavior of this protocol in complex wireless environments. By conducting simulations, we can evaluate the performance of TCP Tahoe in sending data with the parameters used, such as throughput, delay, and packet loss ratio. Analysis of simulation results can provide insight into the effectiveness of TCP Tahoe in ensuring reliable and efficient data delivery, as well as help identify areas that require further improvement or optimization. This study aims to evaluate the performance of the Transmission Control Protocol (TCP) Tahoe protocol in a wireless sensor network (Wireless Sensor Network/WSN) used for building structure condition monitoring. This study uses a quantitative method by collecting data from simulations and analysis of TCP Tahoe on a wireless sensor network for building structure condition monitoring topology. The type of research conducted is experimental research. In this study, experiments were conducted through simulations to test the performance of the TCP Tahoe protocol in terms of throughput, delay, and packet loss ratio. This research is expected to contribute to the development and optimization of communication protocols for WSN in building structure condition monitoring applications.

articleTitle: Addressing Legal and Ethical Considerations of Electronic Trust Certificates in Validating Engineering Projects
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Decision Aid Sciences and Applications (DASA)
abstract: The objective of this study is to investigate the basic elements regarding the electronic authentication certificate, which is issued by the electronic authentication service provider, who collects personal information directly from the person concerned, and may obtain it from a third party after obtaining the written or electronic consent of this person. The results of this analytical study revealed that legislator in the Electronic Communications and Transactions Law stipulated that trust service providers must obtain the necessary license from the competent administrative authority before practicing the activity, while the UNCITRAL Model Law on Electronic Signatures did not stipulate this. The legislator recognized the validity of the authentication certificate issued by the trust service provider as long as it meets the requirements specified by a decision issued by the competent authority. The trust certificate service provider is liable for tortious liability, whenever its elements of error, damage and a causal relationship between them are present. It arises when there is no contractual relationship between the trust certificate service provider and the non-affected parties. The description of a third party here includes any person who is not directly linked to a contract with the trust service provider.

articleTitle: Optimization of Seaport Operations Using Decision Support Methods and Simulation Modeling
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Decision Aid Sciences and Applications (DASA)
abstract: The study focuses on optimizing seaport operations using modeling methods and decision support systems. The main emphasis is placed on the implementation of digital technologies and process automation aimed at improving the efficiency of port operations. Based on simulation modeling conducted using the AnyLogic platform, various port operation scenarios were analyzed, bottlenecks were identified, and measures for their elimination were proposed. The research results showed that increasing the number of terminals and pilots significantly reduces vessel waiting times and enhances the port's throughput capacity. The introduction of modern technologies enables managers to make data-driven decisions, contributing to improved productivity and the competitiveness of ports in the international arena.

articleTitle: GIS and Ant Colony Optimization for Hazardous Medical Waste Management in Tunisia
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Decision Aid Sciences and Applications (DASA)
abstract: This study examines the issues of managing hazardous medical waste management by combining Geographic Information Systems (GIS) with Ant Colony Optimization (ACO) to tackle complex routing problems, particularly the Capacitated Vehicle Routing Problem (CVRP). A case study in Tunisia illustrates how this integrated approach enhances the collection of hazardous medical waste collection across the GIS-identified sites and 174 public hospitals in Tunisia, reducing travel distances and improving vehicle efficiency. The findings indicate that the CVRPACO method effectively optimizes hazardous medical waste collection routes while ensuring vehicle capacity constraints and distance reduction across 174 public hospitals and five treatment centers.

articleTitle: Streamlit Application for Helmet Detection Based on YOLOS: Case Study Indonesia
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Decision Aid Sciences and Applications (DASA)
abstract: Traffic violations are still the biggest problem in the development of traffic in Indonesia. The three biggest violations are (1) running a red light, accounting for 42% of violations, (2) not wearing a helmet, accounting for 23% of violations, and (3) violating traffic signs, accounting for 9% of violations. The violation of not wearing a helmet is the second largest violation in Indonesia, which is due to the lack of awareness of safety while driving. Additionally, the supervision carried out by the security forces is also somewhat inadequate. Supervision is only conducted in certain areas, leading to a high number of violations. To address these issues, the YOLOS (You Only Look at Once Sequence) model, using Vision Transformer and Pytorch, was developed with the assistance of the AI City Challenge 2023 dataset. This model, trained for 200 epochs, is capable of detecting riders who wear helmets and those who do not. It achieves average precision and average recall values for objects with large area coverage in the precision and recall curves (large area), namely 38.8% and 57.2%, and on average precision with an IoU parameter of 0.5, obtaining a value of 63.5%. The implementation of the model in the Streamlit framework to create a system that can be used for detection was successfully completed. The system is capable of performing detection on a single image, webcam video, and video from RTSP CCTV.

articleTitle: Enhancing Energy Consumption in Business through Data Analysis
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Decision Aid Sciences and Applications (DASA)
abstract: This paper investigates how data analytics and machine learning can optimize energy consumption in business operations. It explores the integration of predictive analytics, big data, and smart technologies in energy systems to reduce waste, enhance sustain ability, and lower operational costs. By analyzing real-time energy data, businesses can implement efficient strategies, from predictive maintenance to smart energy grids. Case studies from various industries demonstrate significant energy savings and operational improvements. However, challenges remain regarding data privacy, the high cost of infrastructure, and the need for skilled personnel to manage these technologies.

articleTitle: Reshaping Accounting Professionals: AI Influence and the Path to Comprehensive Qualification
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Decision Aid Sciences and Applications (DASA)
abstract: This study seeks to explore the consequences of AI on the accounting staff, with the view of improving their skills and making them all-round professionals. The authors used the narrative overview method in reviewing related literature such as published books and journals. It is anticipated that accounting will be one of the areas that will be greatly affected by AI in the future, in that there will be less manual work and traditional jobs while efficiency, accuracy, and productivity will be enhanced. The increasing reliance on AI raises ethical concerns regarding privacy, bias, transparency, and accountability, the ethical risks associated with AI, including data privacy breaches, biased decision-making, lack of transparency, and accountability issues. The fourth industrial revolution, which includes the era of big data and development of block chains, upheaves several insights in the world. Therefore, it is necessary to adopt regulations that emphasize the need to prepare specialists with higher level programming and analytic capabilities imbued with big data awareness. All parts of the society; that is: the universities, the government and other educational institutions should pursue this development goal. Professional organizations also need to rethink the training and development procedures for professionals.

articleTitle: A Lightweight Convolutional Neural Network for Face Recognition
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Decision Aid Sciences and Applications (DASA)
abstract: This paper presents a lightweight Convolutional Neural Network (CNN) model for face recognition. The network structure has three convolutional layers, three pooling layers, one flattening layer and two fully connected layers, the pooling layer uses average pooling, the back propagation process uses the Adam model, and the training set used for network training is the FERET face database. The single-layer or two-layer convolutional neural network is widely used for simple image recognition. This structure expands the convolutional layer and the pooling layer to three layers, which makes the network capable of recognizing face images and has a high recognition accuracy rate, which can reach over 98%. Compared with large-scale deep neural networks, this network has a simpler structure, takes less time to train, and is easy to implement in hardware.

articleTitle: Analyzing User Prompt Quality: Insights From Data
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Decision Aid Sciences and Applications (DASA)
abstract: This research investigates the quality of user prompts in Large Language Models (LLMs), such as Chat-GPT, focusing on the impact of user experience and prompt characteristics on model performance. For this research, we prepared an online survey consisting of questions to collect data and, involving a total of 91 observations, took part in this research over 15 days. The study reveals that month of user experience and prompt satisfaction significantly enhance the ROUGE F1 scores, indicating better alignment between prompts and generated outputs. However, factors such as user background and output satisfaction show no significant impact. Responses were pre-processed and analyzed using statistical packages in Python. The findings underscore the importance of designing longer, well-structured prompts to optimize LLM performance, contributing to improved interactions and outputs in artificial intelligence applications.

articleTitle: Implementation of Convolutional Neural Network for Sentiment Analysis on Hotel Customer Reviews
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Decision Aid Sciences and Applications (DASA)
abstract: The hotel industry is a business that provides a place to stay for a short period of time. Online reviews provide information about the impressions, evaluations and experiences of hotel customers. The purpose of this study is to classify positive and negative reviews using Convolutional Neural Network method and analyse review sentiments to determine customer perceptions of 6-star hotels in Pekanbaru City based on 8 aspects, namely facilities, rooms, prices, food, services, location, safety and cleanliness. The data source used as a reference is reviews on the Google Maps platform. As a result, the classification using Convolutional Neural Network on customer review data Hotel A for data splitting (60:40), (70:30) and (80:20) has an accuracy of 97%, 98% and 90%. Hotel B has accuracies of 81%, 87% and 85%. Hotel C has an accuracy of 90%, 83% and 88%. Hotel D has an accuracy of 8%, 81% and 89%. Hotel E has an accuracy of 96%, 97% and 98%. Hotel F has an accuracy of 80%, 82% and 81%. The room aspect is the aspect with the most ratings in each hotel rating. The safety aspect is the best aspect in every hotel review, as it is dominated by positive reviews. While the room aspect in every hotel contains many negative reviews and is a material for evaluation, the room aspect in every hotel needs improvement.

articleTitle: Design Considerations for Hybrid Underwater Target Tracking: Integrating Particle Filters and Deep Learning for Enhanced Decision
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Decision Aid Sciences and Applications (DASA)
abstract: This paper delves into the key characteristics of Autonomous underwater vehicle (AUV) design, highlighting considerations such as hull structure, hydrodynamics, propulsion systems, and sensor integration. The main contribution of this paper is the tracking of underwater dynamic targets, distinguishing between reactive and deliberative tracking levels by proposing a novel hybrid tracking approach, the Multiple Model Particle Filter (MMPF), that integrates deep learning to predict dynamic target trajectory. Finally, a few simulations are delivered to demonstrate the efficiency of the proposed approach in tracking underwater maneuvering targets under different trajectory scenarios.

articleTitle: Robot With Vision Guidance System for Unscrewing Operation
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Decision Aid Sciences and Applications (DASA)
abstract: This work consists in identifying screws along a section of a metal beam, using a camera. Subsequently, the robot moved to the screws with tool (screwdriver) oriented and aligned with the screws, unscrewing them completely automatically. To detect the screws, a dataset of images contextualized with the application was created for personalized training of a neuronal network model. With this solution it is possible to detect and distinguish any type of screw, as the model can be continuously trained and optimized, following the logic of a scalable solution for the following phases of this development.

articleTitle: Impact of Psychological Capital on Organizational Identify on Technical Firms
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Decision Aid Sciences and Applications (DASA)
abstract: This research aims to identify the impact of psychological capital (self-efficacy, hope, optimism, and perseverance) on the organizational identity of customs affairs in the Kingdom of Bahrain. Two hundred and fifty-eight employees were surveyed through a simple random sampling method. The analysis is based on the outcomes of the questionnaire survey given to a representative sample of the employees at the headquarters in question. Researchers hypothesized that psychological capital (self-efficacy, hope, optimism, and perseverance) significantly positively impacts organizational identity in the customs affairs in the Kingdom of Bahrain. The findings indicated that this hypothesis was accepted. Moreover, results indicated that there were no significant differences relating to the impact of psychological capital with its dimensions in question on the organizational identity at the headquarters in question due to the demographic (age, qualification, and years of experience), while there were differences due to (position).

articleTitle: AI-Augmented Software Development: Boosting Efficiency and Quality
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Decision Aid Sciences and Applications (DASA)
abstract: Software developer's approaches to coding, testing, and deployment are changing due to the incorporation of Artificial Intelligence (AI) into software development. AI-Augmented Software Development Tools simplify repetitive activities, boost productivity, and lessen the cognitive load on developers by utilizing machine learning, natural language processing (NLP), and other AI techniques. These tools support several development phases, including DevOps optimization, testing automation, problem discovery, and code generation. For example, AI-driven systems find flaws and inefficiencies in the code, while AI-powered code generation tools like GitHub Copilot help with code suggestion and completion. Additionally, AI automates debugging and test case creation, ensuring the scalability and dependability of software systems. Artificial intelligence (AI) improves quality assurance in complex contexts such as microservices and APIs by maximizing test coverage and identifying abnormalities. Additionally, AI-powered assistants help guide engineers through code inspections, security checks, and performance optimization. Notwithstanding these advantages, there are drawbacks to using AI tools, such as privacy issues and an excessive reliance on automation. With continued development, these tools have the potential to not only expedite development but also redirect the developer's attention towards more complex problem resolution, thereby transforming software engineering methodologies. [7]

articleTitle: The Influence of ChatGPT on Decision-Making: A Theoretical Approach
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Decision Aid Sciences and Applications (DASA)
abstract: The paper analyzes the potential impacts of ChatGPT on decision-making processes across different fields, focusing on ethical aspects such as discrimination, transparency, and responsibleness. With the growth of ChatGPT use, understanding the effects it has on decision-making becomes important. Some of these challenges include issues specific to the competing actors in healthcare, finance, telecommunications, and tourism sectors. It highlights the need for developing sector-specific ethical frameworks and even governance measures for ethical AI.

articleTitle: Sustainable Decision-Making in Urban Design: Softscape Solutions for Mitigating Urban Heat Island Effects in Hot-Arid Climates
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Decision Aid Sciences and Applications (DASA)
abstract: This paper examines the contribution of softscape elements to UHI mitigation in outdoor urban spaces, focusing on walkway treatments as an influencing factor on outdoor thermal comfort and microclimate conditions. Pedestrian paths represent an important area in cities and are often associated with the intensification of the UHI effect since they are directly exposed to sunlight and through the types of materials used in their construction. This study compares how three different softscape treatments would affect the thermal characteristics of such urban walkways. In each treatment, efficiency was analyzed regarding the lowering of surface and ambient temperatures within the context of UHI mitigation with the help of ENVI-met, a currently widely used simulation tool for microclimatic and environmental modeling in urban studies. These simulation results indicate that all three treatments reduced the temperature from the untreated base case; however, the one yielding the highest reduction in temperature became the most effective strategy to mitigate UHIin the current study. Although there was no statistically significant difference among the three softscape element types in their overall performance in mitigating the UHI effect, each of the treatments did result in a significant improvement in thermal conditions when compared to an untreated walkway. This result implies that any of these softscape elements could be introduced into the design of urban walkways for large benefits in the mitigation of urban heat, therefore allowing flexibility in urban planning and landscape design decisions for the improvement of outdoor thermal comfort and reduction of the UHI effect in city environments.

articleTitle: Analysis of Field Measurement Data for Domestic Water Demand and Diurnal Consumption
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Decision Aid Sciences and Applications (DASA)
