Our model SP-Net incorporates several layers including convolutional, dropout, max pooling, and fully connected layers. The results demonstrate that SP-Net achieved a highest test accuracy of 97.76% when it was trained using the SGD optimizer. Moreover, this model trained with the best optimizer outperformed the existing state-of-the-art techniques on comparison.

articleTitle: Unveiling Generative AI Abilities to Support Project Teams
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Decision Aid Sciences and Applications (DASA)
abstract: The practical application of generative artificial intelligence in project teams has tremendous potential for achieving outstanding outcomes. However, little has been discovered in the literature about generative artificial intelligence abilities for enhancing project teams. Thus, the purpose of this study is to explore the abilities of generative artificial intelligence to enhance the performance of project teams and achieve project success. By conducting semi-structured interviews with 10 artificial intelligence professionals, the study reveals 37 abilities of generative artificial intelligence. The study applies the Hierarchical Clustering Algorithm of Machine Learning to group similar abilities, followed by the Silhouette plot. Consequently, the study determines 34 abilities of generative artificial intelligence that belong to 12 main clusters under themes. This study contributes to the domain of Generative Artificial Intelligence by determining its abilities and significance in project teams.

articleTitle: lIoT-Enabled Smart Wearables for Improved Visual Impairment Navigation
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Decision Aid Sciences and Applications (DASA)
abstract: This study introduces a novel Internet of Things (IoT) assistive technology designed to increase the mobility and self-sufficiency of visually impaired people. Over 40 million individuals, including over 1.6 million children, are visually impaired in India, and getting around in daily life is still exceedingly difficult. Walking canes and other traditional aids are not always effective in identifying hazards at different heights and angles. The suggested system integrates smart shoes and spectacles with buzzers, microcontrollers, and ultrasonic sensors. The smart glasses recognise obstructions at head height by extending detection beyond the level of the shoes, which continuously monitors the ground for obstacles. The system ensures better spatial awareness by alerting users in real-time with audio when an obstacle is spotted. The IoT-enabled communication between shoes and smart glasses is a significant innovation since it enables synchronized obstacle identification and reaction. With its all-encompassing coverage, this integrated strategy enhances user mobility and safety. The system is lightweight, ergonomically sound, dependable, and made for everyday use. Future additional improvements might include GPS integration for accurate navigation and machine learning for anticipatory obstacle identification. This study demonstrates how people with visual impairments can live much better thanks to wearable Internet of Things devices.

articleTitle: Management Decisions Based on Comparative Numerical Analysis of Latent Thermal Energy Storage Using Multi-Stage and Single-Stage Phase Change Materials
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Decision Aid Sciences and Applications (DASA)
abstract: This study investigates the performance of a multi-stage latent thermal energy storage (LHTES) system utilizing three distinct phase change materials (PCMs) compared to a single-stage system using only Stearic Acid. Employing computational fluid dynamics (CFD) simulations., we reveal that the multi-stage system exhibits a 15.5% reduction in melting time and a 6.9% increase in efficiency during the charging phase. The findings highlight the impact of spatial thermal energy distribution on melting rates., along with stable temperature profiles that minimize thermal shock. This research underscores the potential of integrating diverse organic PCMs to enhance efficiency and sustainability in concentrated solar power applications.

articleTitle: Instance Segmentation of Damaged Insulators for Power System Inspection and Maintenance
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Decision Aid Sciences and Applications (DASA)
abstract: This paper introduces a novel approach for power system inspection using Mask-RCNN, an advanced model for instance segmentation. The accuracy of our model in identifying and diagnosing damaged low- to medium-voltage insulators is exceptional, as evidenced by its Mean Average Precision (mAP) score of 98.7<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">%</sup>• Throughout the training process, the model exhibited minimal loss metrics, indicating its proficiency in predicting bounding boxes precisely, segmenting, classifying, and aligning masks. The model exhibited consistent reliability in distinguishing between undamaged and damaged components during the inference process, as seen by its consistently high detection rates for both “normal intact” and “damaged broken” insulators. The results demonstrate the practical usefulness of the model and offer promising prospects for enhancing power system maintenance and inspection protocols. The model's consistent and accurate identification of damaged insulators has the potential to significantly enhance the safety and efficiency of power systems, thereby revolutionizing the industry.

articleTitle: Particle Swarm Optimization-Based Deep Neural Network vs Whale Optimization Algorithm-Based Deep Convolutional Neural Networks for Critical Heat Flux Prediction
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Decision Aid Sciences and Applications (DASA)
abstract: Critical heat flux (CHF) denotes the thermal limit at which a phase change occurs during heating, that causes a significant decline in heat transfer efficiency and eventual localized overheating of the heating surface. This study applies two hybrid deep learning models: a Deep Convolutional Neural Network (CNN) optimized with the Whale Optimization Algorithm and a Deep Neural Network (DNN) optimized with Particle Swarm Optimization, to predict Critical Heat Flux (CHF). The results show that the latter model outperforms the former in terms of performance, simplicity, and computation efficiency in the CHF prediction task.

articleTitle: A Group Decision-Making Approach Based on HFL MCDM Methods: Sustainable Supplier Selection
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Decision Aid Sciences and Applications (DASA)
abstract: Selecting a supplier is a common Multi-Criteria Decision-Making (MCDM) problem; however, choosing a sustainable supplier involves considering economic, environmental, and social factors simultaneously. Therefore, selecting the most suitable supplier gains more importance, especially for businesses that adopt the understanding of sustainability in their supply chain processes. This study aims to provide a Group Decision-Making (GDM) approach based on Hesitant Fuzzy Linguistic (HFL) MCDM methods to select the most sustainable supplier. The literature, industry reports, and expert comments provide a sustainable supplier selection methodology in this setting. The HFL technique addresses expert opinions' reluctance and uncertainty, and the assessment process's partiality is addressed by a GDM approach using aggregation operators. The impacts of the evaluation factors are identified using the HFL Simple Additive Weighting (SAW) approach. The HFL Complex Proportional Assessment (COPRAS) method evaluates sustainable suppliers. To demonstrate the potential of the suggested method, an application of this MCDM problem is given. Lastly, the application results and outlook for the future are provided.

articleTitle: A Decision Support System for Enhancing Transportation Services Using Aspect-Based Sentiment Analysis
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Decision Aid Sciences and Applications (DASA)
abstract: This paper proposes an innovative decision support system based on sentiment analysis, specifically designed for the transportation sector. The system employs an aspect-based sentiment analysis approach, which accurately identifies and classifies customer opinions on key transportation service aspects such as comfort, driver behavior, punctuality, and vehicle condition. By integrating the BERT model, known for its advanced natural language processing capabilities, our system provides an in-depth and reliable analysis of customer sentiments. This analysis enables managers and decision-makers to better understand the strengths and weaknesses of the provided transportation services and to precisely target areas that require improvement. By offering actionable insights, our approach aims to enhance the user experience, improve service quality, and increase overall customer satisfaction.

articleTitle: A Metamodel for a DSL to Design Decision Support Systems in Smart Tourism
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Decision Aid Sciences and Applications (DASA)
abstract: The development of Decision Support Systems (DSS) for several companies operating in sectors such as tourism, healthcare, or others, presents significant challenges due to the nature of their multi-component architecture. A typical DSS consists of a data component, a model component incorporating machine learning and deep learning techniques, and a user interface component, each one requires diverse technologies. This complexity increases development time and effort, hindering the efficient design of DSS tailored to specific domains like tourism, where real-time decision-making is essential. One promising approach to overcome these challenges is the use of Domain-Specific Languages (DSLs). DSLs allow developers to model and generate code more efficiently by providing high-level abstractions suited to the domain. By leveraging DSLs, it is possible to simplify the design process and automate the generation of code or parts of the DSS, thereby reducing the overall complexity and time required for development. This paper proposes a metamodel for designing DSS, specifically for the Smart Tourism sector. The metamodel serves as a foundation for the creation of DSL. The goal is to provide a solution to facilitate the development of DSS for the demands of tourism. The paper outlines the key concepts, approach, and results, presenting the first element of the proposed DSL which is the metamodel capturing the essential components and relationships for DSS in Smart Tourism.

articleTitle: Robustness Comparison of TOPSIS, VIKOR, and PROMETHEE II for Prioritizing Switching Device Placement in Power Distribution Networks
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Decision Aid Sciences and Applications (DASA)
abstract: This paper continues previous research on the prioritization of switching device placement in power distribution networks. The aim of this study is to evaluate the robustness of three different multi-criteria decision-making approaches. The criteria considered include Energy Not Served (ENS), feeder length, network availability, System Average Interruption Duration Index (SAIDI), and System Average Interruption Frequency Index (SAIFI). Through conducting a sensitivity analysis on the weightings of the criteria, the robustness of each method is assessed. Robustness is measured using standard deviation, range, and Spearman correlation. The results demonstrate that PROMETHEE II is the most robust method. From 30 feeder alternatives, the top 10 feeders are identified, with ULP Kanopan receiving the highest allocation of LBS units, totaling three units, consistent with previous findings.

articleTitle: Fish Waste-Based Organic Fertilizer Formulation with Taguchi Design of Experiment Approach
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Decision Aid Sciences and Applications (DASA)
abstract: This study aims to improve the utilization of fish waste as a raw material in the production of solid organic fertilizers rich in macronutrients, such as nitrogen (N), phosphorus (P), and potassium (K). Experimental research methods utilizing the Taguchi Design of Experiment (DoE) technique to determine the optimal formulation of several main ingredients, namely fish waste, rice bran, EM-4, and bromelain. The decomposition process was carried out aerobically for 37 days, followed by laboratory testing to measure the levels of N, P, and K in each sample. The test results showed that each variation of the formulation produced nutrient levels that met the SNI 19-7030-2004 standard, with the highest composition in the sample containing 1 kg of rice bran and 300 ml of EM-4, which reached a phosphorus content of 7.0874%. The increase in the content of fish waste and bromelain in the composition contributed to a significant increase in nitrogen and potassium levels. The conclusion of this study emphasizes that the formulation based on fish waste and additional materials can be optimized to produce quality organic fertilizers that meet standards, supporting sustainable agricultural efforts.

articleTitle: Integrating Job Crafting Into HR Decision Models: Implications for Psychological Well-Being in Engineering Organizations
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Decision Aid Sciences and Applications (DASA)
abstract: The aim of this research is to identify the impact of job crafting (increase of job structural resources, reduce of obstacles to job requirements, increase of job social resources and increase of challenging job requirements) on psychological well-being of employees at Aladliya contracting establishment in Bahrain. Two hundred and twenty-four employees were surveyed through a simple random sampling method. The analysis is based on the outcome of the questionnaire survey that was given to a representative sample of employees at the company in question. The researchers hypothesized that there is a significant impact for job crafting (increase of job structural resources, reduce of obstacles to job requirements, increase of job social resources and increase of challenging job requirements) on well-being of employees. The findings revealed that this hypothesis was accepted. Moreover, results indicated that there were no significant differences with regard to the impact of job crafting with its dimensions in question on psychological well-being of employees at the company in question due to the demographics (gender, years of experience and position), while there were differences relating to the demographics (age and qualification).

articleTitle: Advanced Staging of Alzheimer's Disease via ResNet152V2: A High-Precision Approach Using MRI Data
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Decision Aid Sciences and Applications (DASA)
abstract: Alzheimer's disease is a neurodegenerative disorder that sustains the loss of neuronal function and connectivity, culminating in cognitive decline and dementia. In such a scenario, it becomes imperative to diagnose and stage Alzheimer's accurately with a view to managing and probably slowing down the progression of the disease. While no cure has been found, early diagnosis by brain imaging with reasonably good accuracy-like through Magnetic Resonance Imaging (MRI)- plays a very essential role in patient management. MRI can point out brain abnormalities linked to different stages of cognitive impairment, such as mild cognitive impairment and Alzheimer's disease. This paper presents a new technique for classifying the stages of Alzheimer's disease from MRI images using the ResNet152V2 architecture, which is very prominent in deep residual learning in a convolutional neural network. The deployed algorithm categorized the MRI images into four different categories: “Mild Demented,” “Moderate Demented,” “Non-Demented,” and “Very Mild Demented.” Model evaluation is done through precision, recall, F1-scores, and accuracy metrics. Results show very high accuracy and robustness in the classification of different stages of dementia, with an overall accuracy of 97.31 % and strong performance for all metrics of classification. Deep learning techniques may more likely add great value to the improvement of diagnostic accuracy and the establishment of a clinical decision-making workflow in Alzheimer's disease management.

Index Terms: Role In The Management Of Patients

articleTitle: Wind Turbine Blades Fault Diagnosis Based on Vibration Signals Utilizing Convolutional Neural Network
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Decision Aid Sciences and Applications (DASA)
abstract: Wind energy is a key contributor to renewable energy production, with wind turbines playing a critical role in its generation. However, the operational efficiency of wind turbines is often compromised by blade faults, leading to reduced performance, expensive maintenance, and potential safety hazards. Traditional methods of diagnosing faults in wind turbine blades are limited in both accuracy and efficiency. This study proposes a novel fault diagnosis approach using Convolutional Neural Networks (CNNs), a powerful deep learning technique for data analysis. The dataset comprises four sets of vibration signals representing both healthy and faulty wind turbine blades, covering fault conditions such as blade cracks, surface degradation, imbalance, and blade twist. Our proposed CNN-based method aims to accurately detect and classify these faults, enabling proactive maintenance and improving the overall reliability and efficiency of wind energy systems.

articleTitle: Enhancing Software Engineering with AI: Key Insights from ChatGPT
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Decision Aid Sciences and Applications (DASA)
abstract: Artificial intelligence (AI) is currently a prominent topic in the field of software engineering. AI has greatly transformed software engineering by providing advanced tools that may boost the effectiveness and efficiency of various stages of the system development life cycle. In this paper, we examine the role of AI by focusing primarily on ChatGPT, an OpenAI language model. The research explores how ChatGPT can assist in software engineering tasks such as code generation, bug fixing, and documentation development. Through an analysis of real-world scenarios, the case study highlights the benefits and challenges of using AI tools in these three areas. The findings show that although AI can accelerate the output and simplify processes, its application must be carefully considered because it has issues in terms of lack of context awareness regarding performance considerations, project-specific requirements, its inability to access real-time logs or inspect environments, and its tendency to produce documentation that doesn't capture the necessary details for complex systems.

articleTitle: A Severity Grading Framework for Diabetic Retinopathy Detection using Transfer Learning
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Decision Aid Sciences and Applications (DASA)
abstract: Diabetic retinopathy is one of the primary reasons of blindness among individuals. It is a threatening visual disorder that affects delicate blood vessels present within the retina. Early identification of this condition is beneficial for preserving vision and managing it effectively. Detecting diabetic retinopathy manually takes great amount of time and is susceptible to errors. This research aims to propose an automated and efficient framework for grading the severity of diabetic retinopathy with higher accuracy using transfer learning techniques. For this purpose, we have used 3 distinct diabetic retinopathy datasets; Messidor-1, Messidor-2 and IDRiD, containing fundus images. Preprocessing techniques including cropping, denoising, CLAHE, and image resizing are applied to each dataset. Data augmentation is used to tackle class imbalance issues in order to avoid biased results. The dataset was split into three subsets for training, validation, and testing, using a split of 70:10:20. Pre-trained model EfficientNetB5 is fine-tuned and hyper-parameters are adjusted. This model is used to train and test each dataset separately. Results show that our model attained test accuracies of 98.43% for Messidor-1, 97.36% for Messidor-2, and 97.67% for the IDRiD dataset. On comparing the best results of this research with previous state of the art techniques, EfficientNetB5 outperformed those existing methods.

articleTitle: Financial Reporting and Decision-Making in Engineering Sector: A Bibliometric Review of Scopus Database
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Decision Aid Sciences and Applications (DASA)
abstract: With a focus on documents indexed in the Scopus database, this bibliometric research explores the academic literature regarding financial reporting and decision-making in engineering sector firms. The study highlights major research areas, important works, authors, and methods used in the related literature. By examining a sizable dataset of relevant research (598 documents), this bibliometric provides researchers and policymakers with a valuable landscape of the current state of research in this area. Our main results are as follows; 1915 documents have been published in this area from 2014 to 2024, by adding some limitations, our final sample was 598 documents, the publication trend in this area seems to be positive with years. Moreover, the USA has the biggest number of published documents in this area.

articleTitle: Medical Image Segmentation With U-Net for Breast Cancer and Lump Type Prediction
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Decision Aid Sciences and Applications (DASA)
abstract: Today, it is known that, like other types of cancer, breast cancer cases are increasing every year. It is an indisputable fact that early diagnosis and correct diagnosis, which medical literature pays particular attention to, have positive effects on patient health in this field. Therefore, it is a great necessity to identify breast cancer cases correctly and not to confuse malignant masses with benign masses. At this stage, a study was carried out to support the physician's decision, and segmentation was carried out on images containing potential breast cancer with the U-Net model. In addition, a two-class classification model is proposed to determine whether ultrasound images containing masses are benign or malignant. While the detection rate of the current model for benign masses is 99.9%, it reaches 86.6% for malignant masses. In addition, various data augmentation techniques were used hybridly to increase malignant mass images containing fewer samples, and the overall prediction success was increased to 91.13%.

articleTitle: A Monte Carlo Tree Search for the Optimisation of Flight Connections
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Decision Aid Sciences and Applications (DASA)
abstract: In 2017, Kiwi.com proposed the Travelling Salesman Problem 2.0. Despite some similarities with the classic Travelling Salesman Problem (TSP), the problem is more complex. It can be characterised as an asymmetric, time-constrained and generalised TSP. Moreover, infeasibility further complicates the challenge, as no flights may be available between certain airports on specific days. Exact methods often fail in solving these <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\mathcal{N} \mathcal{P}$</tex> -Hard problems. Therefore, alternative approaches, such as heuristics, are typically favoured. A Monte Carlo Tree Search (MCTS) is implemented to tackle Kiwi's problem, an algorithm traditionally used in board games but adapted here for air travel optimisation. The MCTS has been chosen for its proven effectiveness in handling complex and high-dimensional search spaces.

articleTitle: AI-Based Voice Agent for Automated Sales Calls
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Decision Aid Sciences and Applications (DASA)
abstract: This paper presents an AI-based voice agent designed to enhance customer engagement in automated sales. Operating continuously, the agent leverages the power of Large Language Models (LLMs) to interact with potential customers, persuading them to purchase products or schedule appointments with human representatives. Initial performance evaluation gives extremely positive results highlighting the agent's potential to revolutionize sales interactions and improve operational efficiency. These are demonstrated by a conversion rate of 8%, significantly higher than industry averages of 2-5%, high ratings for friendliness, clarity, and realism in customer satisfaction surveys, and an average of 1.7 seconds reaction time during conversation.

articleTitle: Implementation of User and Article Module Design and Testing on Innovation Dashboard Backend Using PHP Laravel and RESTful API
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Decision Aid Sciences and Applications (DASA)
abstract: Innovation and research are important factors in improving the competitiveness and quality of educational institutions, including universities. Lecturers are not only required to be actively involved in teaching and learning activities, but also in research and community service. However, currently there is no platform that can integrate data related to lecturers' research at Telkom University, which causes data management to be ineffective. Therefore, this study aims to build and test the backend system of a research and innovation management application with a focus on user and article modules using PHP Laravel and RESTful web service. This system is expected to facilitate the management and archiving of lecturers' research in an integrated manner, improve data quality, and become a platform that can be accessed by the public to increase the credibility of Telkom University. System testing will be carried out using unit test and stress test methods to ensure the functionality and reliability of the system being built.

articleTitle: A Data-Driven Workload Prediction Model for Cloud Computing Using Machine Learning
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Decision Aid Sciences and Applications (DASA)
abstract: Cloud computing (CC) technology is widely pay-per-use to provide efficient services to the user. Therefore, it is frequently used in business management because it is cheaper, scalable, and flexible but has some limitations. However, workload prediction is a challenging and complex problem. To address this issue, a data-driven workload prediction model inspired by a decision tree-based model of Machine Learning has been proposed using the benchmark dataset Google Cluster Workload Traces 2019. It is a large benchmark dataset used to analyze or predict workload behavior, resource allocation, or system performance. The main aim is to optimize user satisfaction and profit for cloud service providers and minimize the scalability of resources. The proposed model has been assessed using different evaluation parameters like RMSE, MSE, MAE, R-squared, training time, model size, and prediction speed. The results of this study show that the proposed model performs effectively and outperforms the contemporary model.

articleTitle: E-Mail Spam Detection Using BERT and LSTM
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Decision Aid Sciences and Applications (DASA)
abstract: The quick advancement of today's digital world and our daily reliance on the internet have a big impact on our lives. Especially in these days when automation is very easy, fraud and fraudulent activities against users have become quite common. One of the most common examples of these activities is fraud attempts through spam e-mails. Spam e-mails aim to hijack people's information, spread malware and defraud people by playing with their perceptions. Various spam detection methods and algorithms have been developed to prevent these problems. In this study, two models are proposed to detect spam e-mails using natural language processing (NLP) and deep learning methods: LSTM (Long Short Term Memory) and BERT (Bidirectional Encoder Representations from Transformers). As a result of the studies on the Enron e-mail dataset, the BERT model showed 98.93% accuracy and 98.87% f-score performance. The LSTM model showed 97.47% accuracy and f-score performance. With these results, it is seen that the BERT model detects spam with higher accuracy despite the complexity in language structures.

articleTitle: Exploring Integration AI-Powered in Supply Chain Management
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Decision Aid Sciences and Applications (DASA)
abstract: This study aims to examine the integration of AI implementation in Supply Chain Management. In this era, AI has become a transformational force in all sectors, especially in SCM. With AI capabilities, it is possible to assist SCM operations in a company. However, there are still many studies that need to be reviewed in this regard. This study examines the literature study method approach. This method uses relevant studies to analyze. The results of this study indicate that the success of AI integration in Supply Chain Management (SCM) depends on organizational readiness, data quality, human resource skills, and management support in investing in technology and training. The main challenges in AI integration include technical difficulties, limited expertise, and data security issues. AI provides significant advantages in increasing efficiency, decision-making accuracy, and supply chain visibility. Industries such as e-commerce, manufacturing, food, and technology implement AI to improve inventory management, accelerate response to demand, and support operational sustainability and competitiveness.

articleTitle: The Impact of the Green Human Resources Management Model on the Administrative Decision-Making Process Applied to Pharmaceutical Companies
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Decision Aid Sciences and Applications (DASA)
abstract: Recently, the efforts of various public and private Egyptian pharmaceutical companies to adopt green human resources management practices have increased to keep pace with the rapid and successive changes occurring in the labor market, which have a direct impact on the administrative decision-making process by Egyptian pharmaceutical companies, and here comes the role of pharmaceutical companies in Paying attention to the process of making administrative decisions, which leads to preserving the environment and its available resources and reducing the negative effects resulting from industrial operation. In this context, the aim of the current research was to systematically analyze the scientific literature related to the Green Human Resource Management (GHRM) model and administrative decision-making Process (ADMP) in pharmaceutical companies to achieve sustainable competitive advantage. It became clear that the Green Human Resource Management model has a positive impact on the administrative decision-making process in companies. The research relied on the descriptive analytical approach to determine the framework to develop the proposed framework to clarify the relationship between the Green Human Resource Management model and administrative decision-making in companies. The analysis of the literature in the field of Green Human Resource Management and administrative decision-making was also used to answer the main question of the research, which is what is the impact of the Green Human Resource Management model on the administrative decision-making process in Egyptian pharmaceutical companies.

articleTitle: Platform Dynamics and Regional Variations in Thailand's Online Rice Market: A Comparative Analysis of Consumer Behavior on Shopee and Lazada
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Decision Aid Sciences and Applications (DASA)
abstract: This study investigates the dynamics of online rice sales in Thailand across two major e-commerce platforms, Shopee and Lazada, in response to an anticipated increase in domestic rice demand. The commoditization of agricultural products in e-marketplaces has heightened the need for competitive differentiation strategies. Despite the established influence of pricing and promotional strategies on consumer purchasing behavior, a gap exists in understanding region-specific consumer responses to these factors in Thailand's online rice market. This research collected data from 560 rice vendors (343 on Shopee and 217 on Lazada) through an automated web scraping process during September 2024, encompassing key variables such as price, discount rates, sales volume, and customer ratings. The analysis classified rice products into three categories-jasmine rice, white rice, and glutinous rice-reflecting the dominant market segments. Descriptive statistics and ANOVA were applied to evaluate variations in customer behavior and pricing strategies across geographic regions and platforms. Results indicate that Shopee holds a significant market share, particularly in the Northeastern region, though consumer satisfaction as measured by ratings was found to be higher on Lazada. Notably, Shopee displayed a positive correlation between price and sales volume (p = 0.002), while no such correlation was observed on Lazada. Furthermore, correlation analysis revealed that customer ratings and discount prices had limited impact on sales volume, with the number of units sold serving as the primary determinant. ANOVA findings highlighted significant differences in units sold, discount price, and sales volume across customer segments, suggesting that diverse, region-specific pricing and promotional strategies may optimize sales effectiveness. This study contributes valuable insights into the nuanced purchasing behaviors within Thailand's e-commerce rice market and underscores the need for platform-specific and regional approaches to maximize vendor success.

articleTitle: Assessing the Dynamics of ERM and Sustainability Disclosure in Enhancing Firm Value: Insights from IDX80 Listed Companies
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Decision Aid Sciences and Applications (DASA)
abstract: Investment activities undertaken by investors require various pieces of information about the company selected as an investment opportunity. In addition to financial information, non-financial information can serve as an important indicator for investors in evaluating the company. Thus, non-financial information contributes to shaping perceptions of the company's performance and growth potential. Firm value reflects how valuable a company is in the eyes of investors, highlighting the significance of firm value to investors. The aim of this study is to assess the effects of enterprise risk management (ERM) and sustainability disclosure on increasing firm value. The sample includes companies listed on IDX80 on the Indonesia Stock Exchange from 2020 to 2023. Using a purposive random sampling approach, 39 companies were chosen, resulting in a total of 156 observations. Data were gathered through content analysis, and multiple linear regression analysis was used to investigate the relationships. The results indicate that both ERM and sustainability disclosure positively influence firm value when considered together; however, individually, both factors demonstrate a negative impact on firm value. This research significantly contributes to the field of accounting science, particularly for corporate insights. Where companies can consider the disclosures made, if the disclosures made will burden the company then it can be reconsidered. Especially if the disclosures are related to risk where this will worsen the company's image if the company has a high risk.

articleTitle: Assessing Student Comprehension and Implementation of Design Thinking in Mechanical Engineering Education
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Decision Aid Sciences and Applications (DASA)
abstract: This paper investigates how the integration of fundamental principles of mechanical engineering within students' learning in the context of drawing, manufacturing process, and fabrication methods influences the understanding and practical application of design thinking principles among first-year students. The program interlinks theoretical education with work in laboratories on issues dealing with orthographic and isometric projections, metal forming, casting, machining, and welding. The students' improvement is evaluated by Pre-Intervention, Mid-Intervention, and Post-Intervention Surveys. These surveys also monitored shifts in student knowledge, technical skills, and design thinking. The results have indicated a significant gain over the course of the intervention in the student's ability to navigate the idea-to-product continuum, in the students' skill with AutoCAD, and in the competencies associated with manufacturing and fabrication processes. Such research exemplifies how a structured curriculum effectively incorporates theoretical teaching with hands-on experience for improved engineering education to equip students better for the challenges faced in the industry.

articleTitle: Classification of Skin Lesions using Squeeze and Excitation Attention based Hybrid Model of DenseNet and EfficientNet
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Decision Aid Sciences and Applications (DASA)
abstract: Skin cancer, like all other types of cancer, is a health problem where early diagnosis saves the patient's life. Successful detection of skin lesions in dermoscopic images enables this process to be managed more quickly. Deep learning architectures have advanced significantly in recent years, particularly in the classification of medical images. For the multi-class classification of skin lesions, a hybrid model was developed in this study utilizing the convolutional neural network architectures of DenseNet and EfficientNet. In addition, SE (Squeeze and Excitation) attention mechanism is integrated into both models. Experimental results show that the inclusion of SE attention mechanism provides a noticeable improvement in classification accuracy. This study not only contributes to the development of effective skin lesion classification systems, but also It also provides valuable insights into the synergistic effects of combining neural network architectures with attention mechanisms.

articleTitle: An LSTM-Based Approach for Anomaly Detection in Bolt Thread Rolling Process
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Decision Aid Sciences and Applications (DASA)
abstract: Bolted fasteners are used in machine tools, bridges, transportation machinery, power plants and other mechanical structures. The most common use of such elements is in the automotive industry, where there are thousands of threaded connections in the assembly of a passenger car. In the production of these elements, the thread rolling method is used for threading and this method is used in 90% of threaded connections. A wide variety of defects occur during threading operations. The cost to the industry due to lost time and materials is directly related to the percentage of rejected products, making it crucial to find an effective way to address these defects. In this paper, a method using a long short-term memory (LSTM) approach is proposed to detect defects in the thread rolling process that lead to defective bolt production. The proposed approach collects time series data from the machine with a strain sensor during the thread rolling process. Then, the obtained signals are taught by an automatic LSTM-based encoder for the robust case and anomalies occurring in defective cases are detected.

articleTitle: The Study of Critical Success Factors for Small and Medium Size Craft Beer Brewery in Northern Thailand: A Fuzzy AHP Approach
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Decision Aid Sciences and Applications (DASA)
abstract: This paper investigates the critical success factors (CSFs) influencing the growth and sustainability of the craft beer industry in Chiang Rai, Thailand. Using the Fuzzy Analytic Hierarchy Process (Fuzzy AHP), the study identifies and ranks key factors across four dimensions: Innovation, Community, Social, and Engagement. The findings highlight the significance of resource availability, local identity, community networks, and social responsibility as essential drivers of success for craft beer businesses. The study also addresses the challenges faced by the industry, such as restrictive government regulations, and limited consumer awareness. Furthermore, it discusses the role of logistical strategies, including cold transportation and the integration of local ingredients, in maintaining product quality and distinctiveness. The high cost of craft beer relative to local incomes presents an additional challenge. The study contributes valuable insights into the strategic elements needed for developing Thailand's craft beer sector, providing a foundation for future studies on regional industry dynamics.

articleTitle: Enhancing Emotion Recognition Performance Using EEG Signals with Deep Learning Algorithms and Hyperparameter Optimization
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Decision Aid Sciences and Applications (DASA)
abstract: Emotions play a crucial role in understanding human nature and enable us to experience and feel what we go through. Humans express their behavioral characteristics through emotions. In addition to or as an alternative to facial image-based emotion recognition, the EEG (Electroencephalogram) method is also employed in emotion recognition tasks. In this study, a novel deep learning approach has been developed to enhance emotion recognition performance using EEG signals. We applied hyperparameter optimization on SEED-IV, DEAP, and DREAMER datasets using our proposed Special Convolutional Model (SCM) and two-dimensional LSTM models. The SCM model achieved an accuracy rate of 64.35% on the SEED-IV dataset, outperforming similar studies in the literature. The two-dimensional LSTM model, on the other hand, achieved a notable accuracy of 58.8%. The success of the SCM model is attributed to hyperparameter optimization performed using the RMSprop optimizer. In tests conducted on the DREAMER dataset, the accuracy rate, which was 28% in the WEKA environment, was increased to 44% through optimization. This study demonstrates the effectiveness of optimizations in deep learning models for enhancing EEG-based emotion recognition performance. The developed approach allows for a deeper understanding of EEG signals and surpasses existing methods in the literature.

articleTitle: Using the 360-Degree Method to Evaluate Overall Performance and its Impact on the Overall Quality of University Education
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Decision Aid Sciences and Applications (DASA)
abstract: The study aimed to identify the use of the 360-degree method to evaluate overall performance (self-evaluation, downward evaluation, upward evaluation, horizontal evaluation) and its impact on the overall quality of university education resources in Egyptian universities. The study sample consisted of (357) individual faculty members, and (342) (a single member of the administrative body in Egyptian universities. The study relied on the descriptive analytical approach, and used two survey lists to identify the opinions of the study sample. The results of the study reached a statistically significant positive relationship at the level of (0.01) between the dimensions of using the 360 degree method to evaluate overall performance and the overall quality of university education in Egyptian universities there is a statistically significant positive impact at the level of (0.01) for the following dimensions of using the 360 degree method to evaluate overall performance: (downward evaluation, horizontal evaluation, self-evaluation) on the overall quality of university education in Egyptian universities and the absence of a statistically significant impact for the upward evaluation dimension on the overall quality of university education in Egyptian universities. The study recommended paying attention to the strong positive relationship linking the dimensions of using the 360 degree method to evaluate overall performance and the overall quality of university education, and The necessity of paying attention to the overall quality of university education by making optimal use of the resources available in universities, building and strengthening human and social relations, and establishing an accurate information system for managing overall quality, and The necessity for Egyptian universities to rely heavily on the use of the 360-degree method to evaluate overall performance, and to move away from traditional and routine methods.

Author Keywords: the overall quality of university education

articleTitle: Internship Management System (Analysis, Design, and Implenetation)
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Decision Aid Sciences and Applications (DASA)
abstract: This research has developed an internship management system (ISM) at the university level that plays a crucial role as an intermediary platform between internship stakeholders, which are interns, academic supervisors, and field supervisors. The system development life cycle methodology was followed to develop the internship system, which consists of four phases, i.e., planning, analysis, design, and implementation. This study shows three phases, which are analysis, design, and implementation phases.

articleTitle: Design and Implementation of Flutter Based Multi-Platform Docker Controller App
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Decision Aid Sciences and Applications (DASA)
abstract: This paper focuses on developing a Flutter application for controlling Docker resources remotely. The application provides a user-friendly interface for executing various Docker-related commands on the server where the Docker engine is installed. The application uses the SSH protocol to establish a secure connection with the server and execute the commands. Further, an alternative approach is also explored, which involves connecting the application with the Docker engine using HTTP. This proposed Docker controller application provides a significant advantage for managing Docker resources remotely, which is highly beneficial in DevOps fields. It provides a user-friendly interface to manage containers, making it easy to create, start, stop, restart, and remove containers. It abstracts away the complexities of working with Docker commands, allowing users to interact with containers more intuitively. It can be used to manage a number of docker engines from one place making it easy to control and monitor all the docker resources. Its performance, security, and scalability are evaluated using various testing techniques, and the results are found satisfactory. Further improvements may include enhancing the application's features, optimizing the performance, and exploring other possible approaches for establishing the connection between the application and the Docker engine.

articleTitle: AI-Driven Innovations: Transforming Data Support and Environmental Management for the Future
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Decision Aid Sciences and Applications (DASA)
abstract: This paper presents the evolving role of artificial intelligence (AI) in improving internal control and management processes. AI-driven technologies, including Generative Adversarial Networks (GANs) and ontologies, in addition to enabling data-supported decision-making, and empowering local governments to execute administrative tasks more efficiently and effectively. The study explores the wide range of opportunities that AI offers, highlighting the potential for optimizing internal workflows. Besides, it delves into key challenges, models, and methods for fully integrating AI into organizational processes, providing actionable insights for achieving streamlined, data-driven management systems.

articleTitle: Enhancing Financial Decision-Making at ALBA Company: Leveraging Financial Statement Analysis for Improved Investment Returns
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Decision Aid Sciences and Applications (DASA)
abstract: Financial statement analysis (FSA) serves as an essential tool for informed management decision-making in organizations. This study aims to determine how ALBA Company can leverage FSA to improve financial and investment decisions while reducing low investment returns. Research methodology: Descriptive statistical analysis methods for presentations are used to analyze the financial ratio utilizing data from ALBA Company's annual report. The study determines that financial statement analysis is sufficient for informed decision-making, and organizations should prioritize utilizing FSA to effectively leverage this tool. Moreover, a range of ratios ought to be employed while evaluating a company's financial accounts. The FSA should be utilized judiciously in diverse decision-making processes beyond investment activities. Limitations: Only FSs released by ALBA Company between 2018 and 2023 are included in the analysis. Contribution: The article assists various investor types in making important investment decisions. The study recommended to design a sufficient timeframe for the gathering financial data and prepare appropriate analysis and employ ratios to assess a firm's financial and/or operational success.

articleTitle: Open Vehicle Routing Problem with Time Windows in a Real Case Application
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Decision Aid Sciences and Applications (DASA)
abstract: The vehicle routing problem is a complex yet crucial issue for companies' logistical optimization. Commonly, it is one of the most interesting problem as it is encountred frequently in real life while subjecting to different constraints to optimize various criteria. In this paper, we are interested in the Open Vehicle Routing Problem (OVRP) with a homogeneous fleet of vehicles and time windows constraints. It is proved to be strongly NP-hard. We propose a Mixed Integer Linear Programming (MILP) which is runned by CPLEX solver to obtain optimal solution for small sized problems. However, for large sized instances, we develop an innovative K-means based-algorithm. Then, the computational results prove its performance by testing real world instances.

articleTitle: Sustainable Decision-Making for Sustainable Development Policy: Future Prospects, Opportunities and Challenges
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Decision Aid Sciences and Applications (DASA)
abstract: This paper investigated various methodologies and frameworks that facilitate sustainable decision-making. It emphasized the importance of multiple-criteria decision-making (MCDM) theories, explored the life cycle sustainability assessment (LCSA), and examined ethical considerations in decision-making, ensuring that decisions are operative and ethically formulated. It discussed the practical challenges of implementing these frameworks. Moreover, it identified opportunities for improvement. The paper examined multiple case studies to offer valuable insights into the practical application of sustainable decision-making frameworks. Sustainable decision-making for sustainable development policy across various regions and countries was also investigated. The paper concluded with detailed recommendations to improve sustainable decision-making processes for policymakers and industry leaders, contributing to more successful and sustainable practices across various sectors.

articleTitle: Towards a Decision Model for Innovation Self-Efficacy: A Catalyst for Creative Behavior
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Decision Aid Sciences and Applications (DASA)
abstract: This study aims to identify the impact of self-efficacy for innovation on the creative behavior (exploring opportunities, generating, promoting and implementing the creative idea) at the ministry of works in the Kingdom of Bahrain. Two hundred and seventy-eight employees were surveyed through a simple random sampling method. The analysis is based on the outcomes of the questionnaire survey that was given to a representative sample of employees at the ministry in question. The researchers hypothesized that there is a significant impact of self-efficacy for innovation on the creative behavior (exploring opportunities, generating, promoting and implementing the creative idea) at the ministry of works in the kingdom of Bahrain. Findings revealed that this hypothesis was accepted. Moreover, the results indicated that there were no significant differences with regard to the impact of self-efficacy for innovation on the creative behavior with its dimensions in question at the ministry in question due to the demographic (gender, age, qualification, years of experience and position).

articleTitle: Route Compactness in Routing Problems: A Comparison of Exact Approaches to Solve a non-Linear Model
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Decision Aid Sciences and Applications (DASA)
abstract: The compactness of routes in distribution planning is a criterion that has been under explored in logistics literature, despite its notable impact on the practical implementation of routing plans, such as in solid waste collection. This article addresses this gap by introducing a bi-objective model to optimize the vehicle routing problem with time constraints, focusing on minimizing travel times and enhancing route compactness. Experimental tests on small-scale instances were performed using two exact multi-objective solution methods: the weighted sum and the augmented E-constraint methods. The results provided insights into the trade-off between the two objectives while assessing the computational efficiency of both solution approaches.

articleTitle: Virtualization Techniques for Secure Cloud Architectures: An Analysis of Risks and Countermeasures
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Decision Aid Sciences and Applications (DASA)
abstract: This is a fascinating perspective that is simplifying the way consumers engage with computing and related functions. The structure of the cloud is not something that one may describe as a start; however, it was working on a different technology that was based on the many services that it offered. It also has application software for the users to access for such tasks as word processing. Additionally, cloud computing allows customers to take advantage of cloud computing infrastructure by designing and deploying their applications on the cloud. It is capable of providing resilient distributed file system storage designed for storing data that usually gets dispersed across various geographic regions. Virtualization technology is one of the core offerings provided when one is using the cloud. The concept is the ability of physical servers to host multiple virtual machines. This has worked well and has been of great benefit to the users while on the cloud. In this essay, a review of the evidence from the existing research literature on cloud virtualization is provided. This investigation was performed through a literature review of some related works on cloud virtualization. Some of the literature reviews done were undertaken in a credible manner. This paper identifies the present conditions of cloud virtualization trends and assists in the directions of subsequent studies. The main focus of this work is to pose the following question: what is new and how is the cloud virtualization developing? The reviewed works include journal publications and conferences as well as white papers and magazines that have published good works. Therefore, at the end of this review, the trends in cloud virtualization as discussed should have been able to come out. This will be of help to the potential user and even the cloud providers.

articleTitle: Deep Learning-Based Fault Diagnosis in Photovoltaic System
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Decision Aid Sciences and Applications (DASA)
abstract: This study presents a methodology for diagnosing faults in photovoltaic (PV) systems using Convolutional Neural Networks (CNNs). By leveraging CNNs' ability to extract intricate features from PV data, including voltage, current, irradiation, and temperature, the proposed approach enables the accurate identification of various fault types such as short circuits, open circuits, wear, and shading. The contribution of this paper enhances PV system performance and reliability through early fault identification and a comprehensive framework for fault analysis. By effectively distinguishing between normal operating conditions and different fault occurrences, this methodology supports a more sustainable and efficient solar energy future. Through data preprocessing, optimization of the CNN architecture, and incorporation of a multi-class classification layer, the model achieved a high accuracy in fault detection, with an average detection and classification accuracy of 99.7%. The rigorous validation and testing employed in this study affirm the effectiveness and reliability of the CNN-based approach. Overall, this methodology offers a promising strategy for improving fault diagnosis in PV systems, advancing the reliability and efficiency of solar energy applications.

articleTitle: Solar Energy Systems: Driving Urban Sustainability through Innovative Strategies and Impacts
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Decision Aid Sciences and Applications (DASA)
abstract: The concept of access to solar energy is an abstraction that must be generalized to urban fabric within cities in presence of modern, high-rise buildings that are increasing daily, with two different effects: first is their response to solar radiation due to height, and second is their effect on neighborhoods in blocking those rays from them. Cities are not directional and buildings are fixed, not responding to rhythms of their surroundings. Research aims to demonstrate importance of interaction between buildings and their environmental surroundings in an effort to achieve sustainable urban development by providing electrical energy from sunlight throughout year and adopting it in facades to achieve a balance between obtaining lighting on one hand and saving energy in cooling. The concept was applied to a local example, which is “Bawabat Al-Iraq” project in city of Baghdad, to provide solar energy throughout year, and measures taken in this regard, relying on field data taken from integrated photography and data from official weather bulletins. Research concluded that urban planners and architects must take into consideration “solar architecture” as one of most important principles for achieving urban sustainability.

articleTitle: Effective Marketing Strategies to Improve Sales Performance in the Manufacture Industry
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Decision Aid Sciences and Applications (DASA)
abstract: This study explores the impact of work experience, sales training, and customer relationship on sales performance at PT YZX, a leading global manufacturer in the energy and infrastructure sector. The growth of PT YZX is one of the manufacturing companies whose operations are thought to affect Indonesia's economic expansion. Data was collected from all 35 salespeople in the company using the saturation sampling method. The analysis was carried out using Structural Equation Modeling (SEM) using the SmartPLS program. According to the findings, work experience and customer relationship significantly improved sales performance. Simultaneously, work experience, sales training, and customer relationship affected sales performance. These findings highlight the importance of retaining experienced employees and strengthening customer relationships as key strategies to improve sales performance at PT YZX. This study provides insight for companies to focus on developing work experience and customer relationship quality to achieve optimal sales results. Therefore, PT YZX's marketing strategy could involve enhancing customer relations and work experience.

articleTitle: Decision Making in Precision Agriculture Using IoT and Machine Learning: A Focus on Rice Diseases
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Decision Aid Sciences and Applications (DASA)
abstract: Rice is one of the staple foods consumed by billions, which makes it extremely susceptible to diseases that can decimate yields and quality. Precision agriculture uses the Internet of Things (IoT) and machine learning (ML) to enhance its capability in real-time disease monitoring and decision-making. Sensor data from paddy fields can be aggregated into machine learning models to guide early detection of diseases, such as rice blast, bacterial blight, and sheath blight. The paper presents an IoT-based approach that utilizes environmental sensors to capture critical parameters such as humidity, temperature, rainfall and soil moisture. This data is further processed using several machine learning algorithms, including Decision Tree, Random Forest, Support Vector Machine, XGBoost, LightGBM, Artificial Neural Network (ANN), Logistic Regression, and K-Nearest Neighbors for disease prediction and decision support. XGBoost was the best of all of them. Results show improved accuracy in the detection of diseases using XGBoost Algorithm and timely intervention, which could boost rice productivity. The implications of such work are therefore as immense, ranging from sustainable farm practices and reduced pesticide application to reducing the cost of disease control. Thus a Precision Agriculture based decision support system is proposed which will help the farmers take necessary action prior disease dispersion.

articleTitle: Ethical and Legal Issues of Regenerative Medicine in the Uae
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Decision Aid Sciences and Applications (DASA)
abstract: Decision-making in regenerative medicine involves navigating a complex landscape of ethical and legal issues. These challenges impact healthcare providers, researchers, and patients, requiring careful consideration to ensure responsible practices. This review is a comprehensive overview of regenerative medicine, particularly in the context of stem cell research and its ethical and legal implications in the Middle East, especially the UAE. Indeed, in the UAE, the ethical and legal issues surrounding regenerative medicine significantly influence decision-making among healthcare providers, researchers, and patients. As the country seeks to position itself as a leader in medical innovation, these challenges must be addressed to ensure the responsible development and application of regenerative therapies.

articleTitle: Large Language Models for Decision-Making Enhancement in Tourism Package Customization
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Decision Aid Sciences and Applications (DASA)
abstract: The tourism industry faces significant challenges in providing personalized travel recommendations that cater to diverse traveler preferences and needs. This paper presents an approach utilizing Large Language Models (LLMs), specifically the open-source LLaMA model, to enhance decision-making in tourism package recommendations. By integrating a comprehensive database of attractions, amenities, and activities, the proposed system generates tailored suggestions based on user profiles, including demographics, interests, and travel duration. The application of few-shot learning techniques in prompt engineering allows the model to effectively interpret user inputs and produce relevant recommendations with minimal examples. This research aims to demonstrate how LLMs can serve as powerful decision aids in logistics within the tourism sector, ultimately improving user satisfaction and streamlining the travel planning process.

articleTitle: An Alternative Design for the Hidd Intersection Using Flyovers to Reduce Congestion
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Decision Aid Sciences and Applications (DASA)
abstract: This study focuses on reducing congestion at the Hidd Intersection, located along the Shaikh Khalifa bin Salman Highway in the Kingdom of Bahrain, which is one of the two main arterial roads in the country. The highway connects to the King Fahad Causeway, serving travelers from Saudi Arabia. Additionally, the junction serves drivers accessing the Hidd District and nearby areas, including Arad, Galali, Amwaj, and Bahrain Airport. Due to its critical location, the intersection experiences significant traffic volume, resulting in frequent delays and congestion. This project proposes implementing two flyovers to replace traditional traffic lights. A comprehensive traffic analysis has been conducted, including traffic counts performed by the Ministry of Works, Bahrain, along with other data collection and analysis methods. This includes reviewing previously proposed designs for the intersection addressing similar issues. The design adheres to the standards set by the American Association of State Highway and Transportation Officials (AASHTO). The highway design is modeled in Autodesk Civil 3D and includes two flyovers in different directions. Although some traffic in various directions will continue to use the existing traffic lights, the implementation of the flyover design is expected to reduce delay times by approximately 50%. The project will be further developed and modified in certain areas to maximize its effectiveness. Hidd Intersection.

articleTitle: Mqtt Routing Optimizing Based Intrusion Detection for Internet of Things Using Hybrid Machine Learning
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Decision Aid Sciences and Applications (DASA)
abstract: With the advent of the Internet of Things, a world was born in which everything could be uniquely identified and monitored, tracked, and managed by computer programs. Items can self-configure using a predefined communication protocol. Other software programs can be linked to operate together using Message Queue Telemetry Transport Protocol (MQTT) or MQSeries components. Business integration software and middleware are common terms for this category of applications. With its suggested lightweight, easy-to-implement, and lowbandwidth system for billions of smart items, the MQTT protocol offers a wide range of potential applications, including home automation. In order to enhance the power savings in MQservice routing, we presented an intelligent assistant for optimizing routing model. For Internet of Things (IoT) purposes, it introduces an optimal routing model based on optimized hybrid machine learning-based anomaly detection (OHMLA). In order to extend the reach of a network, the offered approach allows Internet of Things devices to make efficient use of energy. To further enhance Intrusion Detection identification and get optimum network selection routes, the moth Salp Swarm technique (SSA) technique is used for the optimized hyperparameters. The model is capable of accurately detecting attacks that result in network congestion, causing delays in connection response and data transfer in IoT network.

articleTitle: Deep Learning-Based Visual Question Answering for Medical Imaging: Insights from the PathVQA Dataset
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Decision Aid Sciences and Applications (DASA)
abstract: Extracting information from medical data and making the correct diagnosis based on this information is critical in medical decision support systems. Interpretation of complex medical images requires a deep medical knowledge. Traditional methods have performance limitations in such data-intensive analyses and are insufficient in terms of obtaining accurate results. In this study, we present an effective solution to obtain fast and meaningful information from medical images and develop a Medical Visual Question Answering (MedVQA) system. With this system, it is aimed to produce correct answers by making sense of the questions directed to the contents of medical images by using deep learning-based models trained on the Path Vqadataset. In the training process of the model, transfer learning techniques and Attention mechanisms are used to better analyze the complex structure of medical terminology. With this proposed solution, it is aimed to accelerate the diagnostic processes of healthcare professionals and to provide automatic understanding of visual information. As a result of the experiments, it was observed that the MedVQA model developed as a result of the training on free-form question-answer pairs on the PathVQA dataset performed 58.63% with BERT+VGGI9 and 60.130/0 with BioBERT+VGGI9. For the question-answer pairs in the Yes-No form, 91.80% and 92.17% accuracy was obtained, respectively. Our study showed a significant performance improvement compared to existing approaches and demonstrated that MedVQA models can be effectively used for deep learning-based extraction of meaningful information from medical images and extraction of features of textual data with natural language processing models. Our study aims to contribute to healthcare professionals to obtain more accurate and faster solutions by using decision support systems with an innovative approach in the field of medical image analysis.

articleTitle: Efficient Hyper-Parameter Tuning for the Kappa Regression Algorithm
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Decision Aid Sciences and Applications (DASA)
abstract: The Kappa Regression algorithm has been shown to provide great performance results, but hyper-parameter tuning can, at times, be computationally intensive. The algorithm in-cludes a single parameter for each feature and a global parameter is required when features are combined. For each feature, one can perform a grid (linear) search, but this can be inefficient if the range of parameter values is large. However, we have found, experimentally, that the prediction error is a convex function of the parameter value. Although we have not shown this analytically, we have demonstrated this property over a wide range of datasets. Using this property, we use a modified Golden Section Search algorithm to find the unique optimal parameter value. In order to initialize the algorithm, we need function values for two points such that the optimal parameter value lies somewhere in between. The left point (with a parameter value of zero) is easy to compute. However, the rightmost point of the algorithm is taken as twice the rough estimate of the optimal parameter value, which is computed using various statistical properties of the dataset. We demonstrate the efficiency of the approach using several datasets.

articleTitle: The Impact of Machine Learning in Strength Prediction of Reinforced Concrete Beam-Column Joint
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Decision Aid Sciences and Applications (DASA)
abstract: The most crucial part in Reinforced Concrete (RC) structures that is a key part in integrating structure's overall stability is beam-column joints (BCJ). If BCJ regions experienced shear failure, that could cause structure collapse. Recently, Machine Learning (ML) techniques have been playing a role in the prediction of shear strength of RC BCJ. Many researchers recently used ML different techniques in civil engineering applications generally. Shear strength prediction of RC BCJ is one of those ML applications in engineering. This paper shows different literature reviews for the impact of ML techniques in shear strength prediction for RC BCJ.

Index Terms: Least Absolute Shrinkage And Selection Operator

articleTitle: PlantNet-Lite: A Lightweight CNN Approach for Plant Disease Recognition
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Decision Aid Sciences and Applications (DASA)
abstract: Plant diseases like rust and powdery mildew pose serious risks to agriculture worldwide and can have a devastating effect on harvests if they are not identified in time. While powdery mildew damages plants with white or gray powder-like spots, rust causes pustules on leaves and stems that hinder photosynthetic activity. These illnesses have the potential to spread quickly, resulting in large crop losses, upsetting food supply systems, and hurting farmers' bottom lines. Recent developments in deep learning have made it possible to automatically diagnose diseases using pretrained models such as VGG19 and MobileNetV2, which are crucial for early identification. Nevertheless, these models frequently necessitate significant computational resources, rendering them unsuitable for implementation in settings with limited resources. A lightweight convolutional neural network (LCNN) for effectively identifying plant diseases from leaf photos is presented in this paper named PlantNet-Lite. PlantNet-Lite preserves competitive accuracy while lowering computing complexity. In testing, it outperformed more complicated models in terms of efficiency and resource utilization, achieving 96.88% test accuracy. PlantNet-Lite is appropriate for use on mobile devices and in settings with constrained processing resources due to its lower size and quicker inference time. This study opens up possibilities for more improvement and scalability in practical agricultural applications and shows how LCNNs can offer a balanced solution for plant disease diagnosis by combining high accuracy with useful efficiency.

articleTitle: Exploring the Impact of Decision Models on FinTech Adoption: An Empirical Study
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Decision Aid Sciences and Applications (DASA)
abstract: The research addresses the integration of decision-making models in the usage of FinTech with emphasis on user trust, financial literacy and regulation. A positivist research approach is taken in this study and a survey that is detailed and structured and distributed to 210 respondents in Jordan with experience in FinTech was employed. Key findings showed that user trust, financial literacy, and regulation factors were important for the adoption of Fintech solutions. Regarding the factors affecting the adoption behaviour of Fintech, it was established that user trust had the most affect, whereas more literacy and a proper regulatory environment were next. This study adds a new perspective to the existing literature by developing a thorough model that accounts for the decision-making process of FinTech. Fintech providers as well as the policy makers will find this research worth reading and beneficial in facilitating the uptake of these modernized banking systems.

articleTitle: The Positive Impact of Hiring Female Personnel in the Logistics Sector in Saudi Arabia: A Qualitative Approach
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Decision Aid Sciences and Applications (DASA)
abstract: This research tries to explore the benefits of hiring female workforce in Saudi logistics industry from both organizational and economic perspective. The study uses qualitative research interviews with female logistics workers, managers and policymakers to explore how gender diversity may influence operational practices by defining the relation between lower performance products and service quality in organizational culture of Saudi Arabia as well improve organisational policies towards a diversified workforce aligned with Saudi Vision 2030. Female employees bring significant benefits like better problem-solving skills, enhanced collaboration and operational advantages but many face difficulties with their career advancement or on biases at work. Finally, we provide recommendations for policy and practice to continue support progress toward improving female participation within the sector.

articleTitle: A Survey on Security Issues and Challenges in Cloud Computing
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Decision Aid Sciences and Applications (DASA)
abstract: Cloud computing has revolutionized how organizations and individuals handle their data, providing flexible, cost-effective solutions for storing and accessing information. However, with these benefits come significant security challenges. This paper surveys the major security risks in Cloud computing presents various challenges, including data breaches, insider threats, and insecure interfaces, which can leave users vulnerable to attacks. We also explore concerns around data privacy, particularly with regulations and the complexities of storing data across different countries. As cloud technology evolves, new threats and trends, like the impact of artificial intelligence and the future potential of quantum computing, add further layers of complexity. This paper provides an overview of these issues while also offering practical strategies for improving cloud security, including encryption, access controls, and the importance of understanding the shared responsibility between cloud providers and users. Addressing these challenges is essential for ensuring that cloud computing continues to be a safe and reliable option for the future.

articleTitle: NeuroNet: An Attention-Driven Lightweight Deep Learning Model for Improved Brain Cancer Diagnosis
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Decision Aid Sciences and Applications (DASA)
abstract: This paper introduces NeuroNet architecture, a lightweight deep-learning framework designed for brain tumor identification, integrating a spatial attention-driven convolutional neural network (CNN) architecture. NeuroNet aims to enhance the classification accuracy of brain tumors, specifically targeting three types: gliomas, meningiomas, and general brain tumors, using Magnetic resonance imaging (MRI) data. The framework is estimated on the Bangladesh Brain Cancer MRI Dataset, which consists of 6,056 MRI images divided into three balanced classes. Unlike traditional machine learning techniques that rely on handcrafted features, NeuroNet's architecture leverages CNN layers with a spatial attention mechanism, enabling the model to focus on critical tumor regions. This approach reduces manual intervention and enhances feature representation. The proposed model performed a high classification accuracy of 99.04%, with a weighted F1-score of 99.02%, outperforming conventional models. These results indicate NeuroNet's potential to assist medical professionals by providing an accurate and reliable diagnostic tool, thus improving brain tumor treatment outcomes. This research underscores the promise of attention mechanisms within deep learning frameworks for advancing cancer diagnosis and medical imaging.

articleTitle: Beyond the Job: Immersion's Influence on Loyalty and Engagement
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Decision Aid Sciences and Applications (DASA)
abstract: This study, aims at carrying out an investigation on the effects of job immersion on employee commitment within a governmental organization in Bahrain. In this study, the use of quantitative research, with an oriented questionnaire was conducted to a sample of 269 participants through simple random sampling.
