articleTitle: Enhancing Predictive Accuracy of LSTM Neural Networks for Diabetes Risk through K-Fold Cross-Validation: Comparison with K-Nearest Neighbors and Expert Systems
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Decision Aid Sciences and Applications (DASA)
abstract: Diabetes is a metabolic disease with a rapidly increasing prevalence worldwide. Developing accurate diabetes risk prediction methods is crucial to enable earlier intervention and optimize healthcare cost management. This study aims to enhance predictive accuracy using the Long Short-Term Memory (LSTM) algorithm in conjunction with K-Fold Cross-Validation. The dataset, sourced from Kaggle, includes 14,257 samples and various health factors. Findings indicate that the LSTM model, with K-Fold Cross-Validation, achieves 80% accuracy in predicting diabetes risk. This model outperforms the K-Nearest Neighbors (KNN) approach, demonstrating LSTM's superior ability to capture complex health data patterns. These results highlight the clinical potential of LSTM models in supporting rapid decision-making for healthcare professionals in diabetes risk detection.

articleTitle: A Robust SVM Framework for Heart Disease Detection Utilizing Advanced Feature Selection Techniques
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Decision Aid Sciences and Applications (DASA)

authors.preferredName: T N S Koti Mani Kumar

abstract: This study proposes a precise model for heart disease prediction through the utilization of support vector machine classifiers. The methodology begins with general data pre-processing the data which encompasses data cleaning which encompasses confirmation of data cleanness by clearing the data of all smoothness), handling of missing values, correcting data inconsistency where necessary, and handling of logical data errors if any. To overcome the class imbalance issue, the SMOTE technique is used here to generate a synthetic sample from the minority class to increase the ratio of the data set. The fact that there is a high variability when designing the model is also addressed whereby the IQR is used to exclude any extreme values to reduce their influence on the potential model. To improve the applicability of the selected features and also deal with the problem of multicollinearity Recursive elimination Feature (RFE) and Correlation Coefficient analysis are being applied. For the SVM algorithm tested on a SMOTE-balanced dataset with selected features, the accuracy, precision, recall, and F1 scores are 95.24%, 89.43%, 93.64%, and 88.79% respectively. This also enhances the reliability of the heart disease model and, above all significant, turns the model into a definitively clinical model that involves retrieval problems that come with computational approaches and the problem of kernels' choice.

articleTitle: Building Knowledge Graphs for Data Analysis Using Embedding and Indexing Techniques: An Agile Methodology
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Decision Aid Sciences and Applications (DASA)
abstract: Decision-making requires comprehensive and accurate information from diverse sources to ensure well-informed, data-driven decisions. Knowledge Graphs (KGs) play a significant role in this context, as they can integrate and represent data in a structured manner, allowing for a deeper understanding of the data. KGs provide semantic indicators that help discover new facts and hidden patterns that support decision-making. In this paper, we present a methodology for building a knowledge graph from distributed data using embedding and semantic indexing techniques. We adhered to agile and cost-effective principles in selecting the models and methods used to implement the methodology. We conducted testing and evaluation of the methodology's outputs, and the results were satisfactory.

articleTitle: Automated Pneumonia Detection Using a Custom Convolutional Neural Network: A Balanced Approach
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Decision Aid Sciences and Applications (DASA)
abstract: Pneumonia is a severe respiratory infection that presents considerable health hazards globally, particularly in developing nations where insufficient medical resources sometimes impede early detection. Recent advancements in deep learning, particularly convolutional neural networks, have demonstrated significant potential in the automated diagnosis of pneumonia from chest X-rays. This could be a cost-effective and accurate solution for healthcare settings that do not have many resources. In order to accurately classify pneumonia cases, this paper proposes a custom CNN model that addresses common issues such as class imbalance and overfitting. The study fixed the problem of class imbalance by making the majority class (PNEUMONIA) the same size as the minority class (NORMAL). This ensured that the training dataset was balanced, which helped the model generalize. Our suggested model has a sequential CNN architecture with four Conv layers, including ReLU activation, batch normalization, and MaxPooling layers. These are followed by fully connected layers, making feature extraction and classification work well. Dropout layers are applied in the deeper Conv and fully connected layers to prevent overfitting, ensuring the model generalizes well to unseen data. The Adam optimizer enhances the model via a binary cross-entropy loss function, while EarlyStopping and ModelCheckpoint oversee training to retain the optimal model, reducing overfitting and improving performance. The model underwent training on a balanced dataset for 20 epochs, with a maximum training accuracy of 98.03% and a validation accuracy of 99.78%. This demonstrates a significant improvement over existing models in the literature, highlighting the robustness and reliability of our approach.

articleTitle: A Deep Learning Framework for Robust Malware Detection in Wireless Communication Networks
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Decision Aid Sciences and Applications (DASA)
abstract: Wireless communication networks are increasingly vulnerable to advanced malware attacks, posing significant risks to network security and user privacy. Traditional detection methods struggle with sophisticated malware, necessitating approaches that are more robust. This study introduces a deep learning-based detection system that leverages Convolutional Neural Networks (CNNs), Recurrent Neural Networks (RNNs), and Graph Convolutional Networks (GCNs) to analyze network traffic and detect malicious activity. Results demonstrate that these models outperform traditional machine learning in accuracy, precision, and recall, offering improved resilience against emerging malware threats. The findings underscore deep learning's potential to enhance wireless network security and pave the way for future innovations in malware detection. Our proposed models achieved up to 96.3% accuracy and 98.2% precision, outperforming traditional machine-learning approaches by a significant margin.

articleTitle: Extraction of User-Defined Information from PDF
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Decision Aid Sciences and Applications (DASA)
abstract: Exporting selected textual data from PDF formats is a challenging task due to the diverse structures of these documents. This project introduces a tool for efficient extraction of user-defined textual data from PDF documents using PyMuPDF. The system is specifically designed to handle text-based content, ensuring precision and speed for researchers, analysts, and professionals. The tool does not focus on handling non-textual elements or diverse PDF layouts, making it a streamlined solution for text-based PDF processing.

articleTitle: The Impact of AI Tools on Last-Mile Delivery in the E-Commerce Sector in Saudi Arabia
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Decision Aid Sciences and Applications (DASA)
abstract: In Saudi Arabia, the e-commerce sector has witnessed an impressive growth spurt as a result of advancements in technology and changes in consumer behavior. Last-mile delivery, the last step in the delivery process is a key yet most difficult aspect as it contributes to higher share out of total transport cost and critical function for customer satisfaction. This study explores the influence of Artificial Intelligence (AI) tools within KSA's e-commerce last-mile delivery ecosystem, particularly examining how technologies like route optimization, demand forecasting and even autonomous vehicles are changing logistics. Bearing this in mind, a third approach was adopted comprised of performing research to conduct an exploratory study based on mixed-methods: literature review; interviews with professionals from the branch and quantitative data analysis about whether AI tools significantly help improve efficiency for making deliveries as well satisfaction delivered to customers. Conclusions: The results reflect the significant competitive edge that e-commerce businesses in Saudi Arabia can harness by embracing AI strategically.

articleTitle: Trends and Challenges of E-Commerce in Nigeria
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Decision Aid Sciences and Applications (DASA)
abstract: We live in a digital world around the internet. The concept of online buying and selling has always been fasciSnating; how individuals in different locations can seamlessly engage in commerce across borders. The purpose of this study is to uncover the common trends and challenges presented by e-commerce in the Nigerian market, drawing insights from two diverse markets: The United States and South Africa. This study also provides strategic recommendations for overcoming these hurdles such as reducing the data cost, providing appropriate internet technology, investing in infrastructure, and enacting adequate laws and regulatory bodies. The study concludes that although there is an ongoing exciting journey of digital transformation in Nigeria, we still have a long way to go to be on par with other countries like the United States and South Africa. This study will contribute to providing a guide for policymakers in Nigeria for future policy directions on e-commerce.

articleTitle: Using Machine Learning for Predicting Business Failure: A Systematic Literature Review
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Decision Aid Sciences and Applications (DASA)
abstract: One of the pioneer topics in the finance industry is the prediction of bankruptcy using machine learning (ML) methods. Bankruptcy prediction is an essential indicator for various organizations, including banks, corporations, countries, and many more. These financial organizations identify specific strategies when bankruptcy prediction is determined. Therefore, financial institutions must ensure the accuracy of the models used. The ML methods have proven the relevance and robustness of the models applied in predicting the bankruptcy of organizations within different regions of the world. This Systematic Literature Review (SLR) covers 38 papers on bankruptcy prediction using ML. This study explores ML advancements in predicting business failure in Eastern and Central Europe and Gulf Cooperation Countries (GCC) regions. In addition, this paper aims to examine the technical issues and pitfalls concerning predicting models applied to bankruptcy. The third purpose is to validate the superior power of ML in achieving forecasting goals on the topic. These studies have resulted in a spectacular performance of models produced by ML methods in the context of bankruptcy. However, some issues related to data and model setting affect the quality and performance of the models, such as selecting variables, imbalanced data, and outliers. In addition, the findings demonstrate that it's essential to keep in mind and consider that the characteristics of some nations have an impact on how the study field covered in this article evolves. Moreover, imitating other models without considering the nations' specificities may not lead to the best findings.

articleTitle: Smart Water-Powered Renewable Energy System with IoT Integration
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Decision Aid Sciences and Applications (DASA)
abstract: An advanced hybrid renewable energy collecting and storage system prototype that utilizes water flow as its primary power source. Additionally, the system incorporates an energy monitoring system based on the Internet of Things (IoT) technology. The device effectively harnesses energy from the movement of water, storing it for future use in low-voltage applications. It demonstrates a maximum daily energy capture capacity of about 100Wh. The energy monitoring system, based on the Internet of Things (IoT), enables the real-time and remote monitoring of energy harvesting and usage. We thoroughly assessed the energy harvesting component across different situations to identify the crucial parameters that impact energy output. The results of our study demonstrate that several elements, including the spatial separation “between the energy harvester and the water source, Water flow” speed, sensor orientation, and sensor density, all play significant roles in determining the quantity of energy collected. This research shows that it is possible to integrate IoT technology with hydropower renewable energy systems. It provides significant perspectives on enhancing energy extraction efficiency in practical scenarios.

articleTitle: Data-Driven StrategicWorkforce Planning in UK SMEs: A Comparative Analysis
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Decision Aid Sciences and Applications (DASA)
abstract: Amidst escalating digital competition, small and medium-sized enterprises (SMEs) face a vital need to strategically manage human resource management (HRM) for sustainable growth. The adoption of data-driven strategic workforce planning is crucial for SMEs, facilitating informed decisions that enhance operational efficiency. Drawing from secondary data obtained through a governmental survey involving over 2000 SMEs across various sectors in the UK, this study endeavors to deepen our comprehension of the determinants and challenges associated with the adoption of data-driven workforce planning (DDWP) in SMEs and its consequential impact on organizational performance. The study endeavors to construct a framework anchored in the technology-organization-environment (TOE) model, subsequently validating this framework across three prominent industries within the UK SME landscape to substantiate hypotheses derived from the extant literature. The discussion encompasses an exploration of the challenges inherent in implementing DDWP within SMEs, followed by an assessment of how these challenges influence the adoption of DDWP. Subsequently, the study delves into an evaluation of the impact of DDWP on performance, concluding with an examination of the framework's applicability across industries. The results illuminate that drivers influencing the level of adoption of DDWP in SMEs similarly impact selected industries. Moreover, the findings underscore that the level of adoption of DDWP exerts a palpable impact on organizational performance, enhancing overall business efficiency. The outcomes of this study furnish valuable insights and practical recommendations for HR professionals, policymakers, and researchers, delineating strategies to elevate business performance and efficiency through the transformation of workforce planning into data-driven workforce planning.

articleTitle: Sustainable Microplastic Filter Development for River Conservation: A Case Study in Yogyakarta
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Decision Aid Sciences and Applications (DASA)
abstract: Indonesia, a maritime nation with 70% of its territory comprised of water, faces significant environmental challenges due to population growth and human activities. Plastic waste, particularly microplastics, poses a critical threat to aquatic ecosystems and human health. This study aims to develop innovative water filtration technology to address microplastic contamination, employing a research and development (RnD) approach to create and evaluate the effectiveness of the product. The research focuses on developing advanced filtration systems to mitigate microplastic contamination in the rivers of Yogyakarta. The filter design is inspired by the structure of baleen whales, combining Rapid Sand Filtration (RSF) and Granular Activated Carbon (GAC) methods with a backwash system. The study was conducted on four major rivers, such as Code, Gajahwong, Manunggal, and Winongo, where the average microplastic density reached 18,400 particles/m<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">3</sup>. Results indicate that the filtration system effectively reduced microplastic contamination by 75.4% with backwashing and by 71.7% without it. Notably, the Code River exhibited the highest reduction at 88.5% with backwashing. Additionally, the system improved water clarity and eliminated odors. This approach presents a promising solution for enhancing river water quality and safeguarding public health.

articleTitle: Dental Diagnostics with Deep Learning: A VGG16-Based Approach for Classifying Segmented Dental Radiographs
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Decision Aid Sciences and Applications (DASA)
abstract: This research focuses on creating a deep learning architecture to categorise dental radiographs into categories such as Cavity, Fillings, Impacted Tooth, Implant, and Normal. Considerable preprocessing was carried out on the Dental Radiography dataset sourced from Kaggle. The dataset was pre-processed by segmenting individual teeth to allow the examination of specific dental conditions. The underlying architecture is a VGG16 convolutional neural network that has availed transfer learning in order to enhance the feature extraction capability. The dataset was divided into training, validation, and test sets, ensuring sufficient representation across all classes. In such a situation, it was able to obtain an overall accuracy of 96.52% on the test set with most classes having high precision and recall along with F1-score. Key findings give evidence of the effectiveness of deep learning for automation of diagnosis from radiographic images, while the VGG16 architecture is found particularly effective. Consequences implied by this research are that AI models can contribute a lot to dental professionals by making preliminary diagnoses faster and more accurately, hence improving diagnostic efficiency and patient care. This study thus holds importance in the sense that this will be one contributing factor to the emergent field of AI-assisted dental diagnostics, overcoming class imbalance problems and showing a possible clinical integration of deep learning models for better diagnosis.

articleTitle: Autonomous Bat Echolocation Monitoring System with Machine Learning for Real-Time Pest and Biodiversity Management
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Decision Aid Sciences and Applications (DASA)
abstract: The preservation of biodiversity and the mitigation of agricultural pests are crucial components of sustainable agriculture. This study presents the Autonomous Bat Echolocation (ABE) Monitoring System, a sustainable approach to biodiversity preservation and pest control in agriculture. The system combines auditory sensors, low-power devices, and deep learning algorithms to monitor bat activity by detecting and classifying species based on their echolocation calls. The integration of the BatDetect2 model allowed real-time processing on low-power devices within our monitoring stations, enabling efficient and continuous monitoring of bat activity. By establishing a network of these stations, the system provides real-time detection as an early warning for potential pest infestations in agricultural fields. Overall, the ABE Monitoring System is a scalable, eco-friendly tool that helps in biodiversity monitoring and supports sustainable agricultural practices, aiding farmers in pest prediction and management.

articleTitle: Fine-Tuning Whisper for Speech Translation: A Case Study on Translating Darija to Arabic
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Decision Aid Sciences and Applications (DASA)
abstract: The task of translating Darija, a dialect of Arabic, into Modern Standard Arabic (MSA) presents significant challenges due to linguistic variations and the lack of representation in major models. Traditional speech recognition and translation systems, like Whisper, are generally trained on more standardized languages and often struggle with dialects like Darija. To address this issue, we fine-tuned the small version of Whisper on the Darija-C corpus for speech-to-text translation into MSA. Our approach involved adapting Whisper's translation capabilities by fine-tuning the model with 5000 training steps and evaluating its performance using the BLEUmetric. The fine-tuned model achieved a BLEU score of 0.65, reflecting a marked improvement over the baseline. This research demonstrates the effectiveness of fine-tuning models for dialectal translation tasks, offering insights into how underrepresented dialects like Darija can be better supported by advanced speech translation systems.

articleTitle: Image Classification of Corn Leaf Diseases Using CNN Architecture ResNet-50 and Data Augmentation
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Decision Aid Sciences and Applications (DASA)
abstract: Corn is a crucial crop in global food production. Despite its ability to thrive in various weather conditions, it is susceptible to diseases, particularly affecting its leaves. Corn leaf diseases have detrimental effects on harvest yields, leading to losses for farmers. This research employs a deep learning approach using Convolutional Neural Network (CNN) ResNet50 architecture and data augmentation to classify images of corn leaf diseases. Factors such as data splitting ratios, learning rates, and model optimization are explored, while data is enriched through augmentation techniques such as rotation, shifting, and flipping. Training data indicates that the use of data augmentation influences the model's accuracy in classifying corn leaf disease images. The RMSProp optimizer provides the highest average validation accuracy in Non-Augmentation training. Meanwhile, evaluation results from the confusion matrix show that applying data augmentation with a 90:10 data split, Nadam optimizer, and learning rate of 0.0001 yields the highest accuracy of up to 94.36%. However, assessment of the model's ability to classify images reveals that configurations utilizing data augmentation, a 90:10 data split, Nadam optimizer, and a learning rate of 0.001 demonstrate optimal performance with precision reaching 94.50%.

articleTitle: Integrating Sustainable Behavior Into Construction Risk Management: Modeling Human Related Factors And Attitude
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Decision Aid Sciences and Applications (DASA)
abstract: This study aims to examine human-related elements and the impact of contractors' risk attitudes on construction risk management, while also addressing the moderating effect of sustainable behavior. This study used descriptive and inferential statistics to examine data collected from 317 contractors in Nigeria's construction business. We gathered the data using a convenience sample technique and analyzed using the “partial least-squares structural equation modelling” (PLS-SEM) technique. However, the findings demonstrated that acknowledged human-related factors have a positive impact on risk management in the construction sector. Additionally, researchers found that these factors positively influenced the risk attitudes of contractors. As a behavior, sustainable practices moderate the association between human-related factors and contractor risk management. However, eliminating risk is impossible and requires meticulous management. The approach's final innovative feature is the incorporation of sustainable behaviors in construction risk management.

articleTitle: Enhanced Nanoparticle Classification Through Optimized Artificial Neural Networks
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Decision Aid Sciences and Applications (DASA)
abstract: This study investigates the effectiveness of Deep Learning techniques in classifying nanoparticles, with a par-ticular focus on how the depth of neural networks influences model performance. Artificial Neural Networks (ANN) were utilized in simulations, exploring configurations ranging from a single hidden layer to four hidden layers to identify the optimal architecture for nanoparticle classification using MATLAB- NN Toolbox. Evaluation metrics include Mean Squared Error (MSE), Root Mean Squared Error (RMSE), the Correlation Coefficient (R), and the Coefficient of Determination <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$(R^{2})$</tex>. Notably, the minimum value of the MSE achieved was <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$5.6814 \times 10^{-13}$</tex> with the Bayesian Regularization (BR) technique, while the maximum values of Rand <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$R^{2}$</tex> were 0.9989 and 0.9977, respectively, with the Levenberg-Marquardt (LM) technique. The results offer insights into model robustness and contribute to selecting an optimal algorithm for analyzing polymeric nanoparticles. This study highlights the potential of ANN to advance precision in nanomaterial classification tasks, supporting further development in this field.

articleTitle: The Role of Sustainable Human Resource Management in Enhancing Organizational Agility (Articles Review)
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Decision Aid Sciences and Applications (DASA)
abstract: Organizational agility, the ability to swiftly adapt to internal and external changes, is essential for sustaining long-term success in today's dynamic global environment. Achieving agility requires practices that drive transformation, growth, and innovation, influenced by factors such as globalization, technological change, and competition. Human resource management (HRM) plays a critical role in fostering agility, with Sustainable Human Resource Management (SHRM) practices identified as key to developing a resilient, adaptable workforce. While extensive literature explores the link between organizational agility and its outcomes, research on the intersection of SHRM and agility-especially in the public sector-remains limited. This review synthesizes existing research to examine how HR practices enhance organizational agility and their application in the public sector, emphasizing the importance of sustainability and adaptability in a post-pandemic context. The review also identifies research gaps, particularly regarding the mechanisms through which SHRM contributes to both short-term agility and long-term organizational sustainability.

articleTitle: Efficient Zone Routing through K-Nearest Neighbours Optimization in Wireless Sensor Networks
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Decision Aid Sciences and Applications (DASA)
abstract: Wireless Sensor Networks faces significant challenges due to limited energy and computational resources, requires efficient routing protocols to optimize network lifetime and performance. Traditional Zone Routing Protocol (ZRP) employs mixed routing approach to minimize overhead by partitioning the network in various zones, and utilises the proactive routing approach within zones and follow the reactive routing among zones. However, inefficient zone formation increases routing overhead and reduce scalability, limiting the protocol's effectiveness in dynamic environments. This paper addresses these limitations by integrating the K-Nearest Neighbours (KNN) algorithm into ZRP, optimizing zone creation based on node proximity to enhance the routing efficiency and network organization. The proposed KNN-ZRP approach aims to create more cohesive and strategically formed zones, thus reduces the number of zones needed and improves the communication efficiency. Through extensive simulations, the paper presents a comparison among the performance of traditional ZRP with the KNN-enhanced ZRP across metrics such as zone count, routing overhead, and average distance to the nearest neighbour. The result shows that the KNN-ZRP approach achieves a significant reduction in routing overhead and prolongs network lifetime, with results showing up to a 30% reduction in zone numbers and improved resource conservation. This approach demonstrates substantial improvements in network scalability and efficiency, making it highly suitable for deployment in resource constrained WSN environments.

articleTitle: Balancing Act: Legal and Political Dimensions of Engineering Decision Making
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Decision Aid Sciences and Applications (DASA)
abstract: Engineers often make decisions that profoundly impact society, with consequences ranging from saving lives to jeopardizing property. This study examines the complex interplay between the regulatory framework and the politics that shape these technological practices. Through an extensive literature review and real-world case studies, the findings of the study highlight the importance of understanding the legal constraints and political dynamics of the whole game for engineers, and efficient accounting decision-making has been further emphasized and incorporated. However, the political considerations in a case can affect the interpretation and implementation of these legal systems, as various stakeholder groups try to sway policymakers' navigation of this Law-politics interface, which poses enormous challenges for engineers who have to balance technical, ethical, and practical considerations with evolving regulations and psychological pressures. This study highlights the importance of engineers' engagement in the legal and political contexts of their profession; if the engineering profession is to foster its potential to deliver solutions that serve the public interest more through this holistic understanding, they will get it.

articleTitle: Role of Cloud Computing in Big Data Analytics: A Scalable Data Analysis Perspective
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Decision Aid Sciences and Applications (DASA)
abstract: The focus of this study is the role of cloud computing in triggering big data revolution, especially regarding scalabil- ities and efficiency boosts that are brought about by exascale systems. Along with increase in volume and variety of big data, conventional data processing infrastructure appears incapable to properly handle the huge amount of data. Cloud computing, which is a scalable environment and flexible services, is a solution in doing so but big data combined with it becomes problematic in terms of data security, real-time processing and cost man- agement as well. Based on the an in-depth literature review, well-established models and intelligent computing techniques, this project is focused at the teamwork between existing clouds and exascale platforms which tries to address these problems. Resulting in the establishment of such frameworks and strategies that enhance the efficiency and effectiveness by putting priority on the strengths of these technologies.

Author Keywords: Cloud Computing Big Data Analytics Scalability Data Privacy Real-time Processing Data Security Computational Efficiency Cloud Architecture Data Management Cost Optimization

articleTitle: Sustainable Energy Decision-Making with an RAG-LLM System
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Decision Aid Sciences and Applications (DASA)
abstract: To reach the ambition of a net-zero economy by 2050, the UK aims to improve energy efficiency in all homes by 2035, targeting reductions in energy consumption and household expenses. Small and Medium-sized Enterprises (SMEs) play a critical part in this evolution but frequently face challenges in navigating the complex and fast-changing Energy sector to access essential information. Required data spanning regulatory updates, market trends, renewable energy production, and climate patterns is dispersed across multiple sources, creating inefficiencies and raising costs for SMEs pursuing sustainable Energy goals. This study addresses this information gap through a prototype Information System (IS) that consolidates diverse regulatory and environmental topics as a proof-of-concept. The proposed Energy Question Answering (QA) Assistant, based on the Large Language Models (LLMs) and Retrieval-Augmented Generation (RAG), integrates information from government, industry, and environmental sources. Using open-source technology, this tool delivers SMEs timely insights into Sustainable Energy Initiatives (SEIs) and regulatory frameworks, supporting cost-effective and informed decision-making that aligns with the UK's sustainability targets.

articleTitle: The Impact of Prosocial Motivation on Organizational Citizenship Behavior
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Decision Aid Sciences and Applications (DASA)
abstract: Among employees at the Ministry of Information in Bahrain, focusing on its five dimensions: conscience, sportsmanship, civic virtue, courtesy, and altruism. Using a descriptive analytical approach, data were collected via a questionnaire distributed to 269 employees, achieving a response rate of 88.84% with 239 completed surveys. The findings revealed a statistically significant positive effect of prosocial motivation on all OCB dimensions, with notable differences linked to demographic factors such as age, educational qualification, years of experience, and job level. Sportsmanship emerged as the most influenced dimension, followed by altruism, courtesy, conscientiousness, and civic virtue. The study suggests that managers should encourage employees to view challenges as opportunities for problem-solving and to focus on proactive measures to support colleagues. It also recommends that human resources reassess planning according to employees' workload and urges staff to adhere to break times.

articleTitle: Artificial Intelligence Tools for Generating Design Alternatives for Interior Spaces-Literature Review
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Decision Aid Sciences and Applications (DASA)
abstract: This paper explores the significant impact of artificial intelligence (AI) in the field of interior design, with a particular focus on its ability to generate a variety of innovative design possibilities. With the evolution of the design landscape, the integration of artificial intelligence technologies has led to a significant transformation, challenging traditional methods and providing designers with a powerful set of tools to enhance their creative processes. This paper addresses how these algorithms are able to independently create a variety of design options, reshaping the visualization phase and enhancing a more dynamic and iterative design process. The study delves into the various ways artificial intelligence impacts interior design, emphasizing its ability to analyze large datasets, recognize trends, and create unique design solutions. Additionally, it explores the ethical considerations and challenges associated with integrating artificial intelligence into the creative sector, and provides insights on how designers can thoughtfully leverage these technologies while preserving the essence of creativity in their design work. Research deepened our understanding of how artificial intelligence is reshaping design choices for interior spaces, paving the way for a future where imagination and smart algorithms collaborate to expand the horizons of interior design.

articleTitle: Applying Machine Learning to Detect Fraud of Financial Statements: A Systematic Literature Review
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Decision Aid Sciences and Applications (DASA)
abstract: The application of machine learning (ML) approaches to financial statement fraud detection is reviewed in this systematic literature review, highlighting the pressing need to improve fraud detection mechanisms in the financial markets. The primary objective of this study is to compile the body of current research, discover gaps in the field, and recommend future directions for research. Using the systematic literature review (SLR) approach, the study carefully reviews relevant primary literature to determine which algorithms for machine learning work best for fraud detection. The evaluation cautiously selects research from numerous databases, highlighting machine learning's promise and ability to detect fraud in financial statements. Findings show that complex machine learning techniques—in particular, deep learning methods and ensemble learning models—significantly improve the accuracy of fraudulent activity detection by recognizing intricate patterns and abnormalities that conventional techniques might miss. Despite these advancements, the review identifies a need for more inclusive datasets and the integration of non-financial data to augment the models' predictive power. The paper emphasizes the uniqueness and significance of utilizing machine learning (ML) in identifying financial fraud and advocates for additional research and development in integrating various data formats to enhance fraud detection models.

articleTitle: Security Technology Evaluation Criteria Model for Telemedicine Consultation System: A Literature Review
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Decision Aid Sciences and Applications (DASA)
abstract: The increasing number of patients in hospitals, the need for telehealth among the elderly, and the impact of the pandemic highlight the need for telemedicine services. Among them, the telemedicine consultation system (TCS) is the medium for doctors to communicate with patients in the telemedicine system. However, due to the problem of safety technology, it has not been widely applied. This literature review conducts a comprehensive search using keywords in authoritative index databases such as SCI and Scopus, aiming to find out the existing security problems and solutions of TCS, and establish security technology evaluation criteria for TCS in identity authentication, system authorization, data privacy protection and data transmission security. At the same time, a TCS technology evaluation criteria model is established to classify the security level of the system.

articleTitle: The Effect of Leadership Storytelling on Employer Branding for Engineering Organizations: Conceptual Paper
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Decision Aid Sciences and Applications (DASA)
abstract: Organizational storytelling is a crucial aspect of employer branding, as it directs the cultures and behavior of an organization, reflecting the employer brand. Leadership has a distinct impact on organizational culture, making leadership storytelling essential. It impacts on employee emotional responses, such as pride, commitment, motivation, and loyalty, which are reflected in employer branding. However, research on the effects of leadership storytelling is underrepresented in the study of narrative techniques leading to employer branding. This paper aims to connect research on employer branding and leadership storytelling by breaking new conceptual ground with an innovative framework. Three main connections are argued: the direct impact of leadership storytelling on employer brand strategies, the storytelling of leadership reflects and directs organizational culture, and the storytelling of leadership impacts organizational identity, serving as a precursor for employer branding. The paper emphasizes that the employer brand reflects character, and leaders should develop stories associated with character and share them with employees and candidates throughout the employment life cycle.

articleTitle: Corporate Governance and Non-Financial Risk Disclosure: Insights from Companies Listed on the Bahrain Bourse
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Decision Aid Sciences and Applications (DASA)
abstract: This study examines the connection between corporate governance mechanisms and the non-financial risk disclosure (NFRD) in non-financial companies listed on the Bahrain Bourse (BHB). It analyzed data from 19 companies over a five-year period (2018–2022), focusing on board characteristics such as size, independence, nationality, ownership, and meetings in addition to control variables. The research employed a descriptive approach and multiple linear regression to evaluate hypotheses. The principal findings demonstrate that the dimensions—nationality and ownership—of board members correlate favorably with the extent of NFRD. Conversely, factors like board independence, number of meetings, and attendance rates do not show a significant relationship with disclosure levels. The study recommends enforcing compliance with the Bahraini Corporate Governance Law and suggests increasing the representation of foreign board members and implementing employee stock ownership plans to enhance governance and transparency.

articleTitle: The Impact of Innovation in the Space Sector on Entrepreneurship: An Empirical Investigation on Oman
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Decision Aid Sciences and Applications (DASA)
abstract: The purpose of this research is to investigate the impact of technology advancement, strategic investments, and innovation driven government policies and initiatives on entrepreneurial endeavours, entrepreneurial venture growth, and entrepreneurship success in Oman's space sector. The study used a quantitative research methodology to collect and analyse data from employees of Oman space entrepreneurship companies. The findings show that all three independent variables have a significant impact on the dependent variables, implying that technological advancements, strategic investments, and supportive government policies are important drivers of entrepreneurial endeavours, venture growth, and entrepreneurship success in the space sector. These findings emphasize the necessity of creating a synergistic environment that combines advanced technologies, strategic financial assistance, and innovation-friendly laws in order to develop a successful entrepreneurial ecosystem in Oman's emerging space sector. This study provides useful information for policymakers and business executives looking to boost the sector's growth and competitiveness.

articleTitle: Leveraging BIM for Decision Support and Logistics Optimization in Bahrain's Engineering Application
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Decision Aid Sciences and Applications (DASA)
abstract: The construction industry in Bahrain is incurring significant delays due to several deficiencies such as rework and material handling, which result from miscommunication, coordination, and relocation among on-site parties. The industry needs a comprehensive communication and coordination tool to avoid these deficiencies. Building Information Modeling has demonstrated promising capabilities in enhancing communication and coordination through 3D visualization. Many of the technological breakthroughs of the past decades have stymied full deployment of Building Information Modeling. This overview presents research on the largest impediments, namely process development, disparate systems integration, and modification management, from several disciplines and considers approaches for their resolution. These include process and technology acceptance models; service-oriented architecture, middleware, and semantic web infrastructures; and novel design and facilitation approaches. It also discusses the unique contributions that Building Information Modeling and recommended research contributions from each respective technology domain can make to the overall problem.

articleTitle: Diabetes Prediction using Deep Ensemble Network
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Decision Aid Sciences and Applications (DASA)
abstract: Timely diabetes detection is crucial for effective management and minimizing complications. This research presents a novel framework for early diabetes diagnosis, combining DeepEnsembleNet's capabilities with a hybrid optimization strategy. The methodology begins with robust data preprocessing, addressing missing values and outliers through advanced statistical techniques. A comprehensive feature extraction process uncoveres key insights, leveraging statistical measures and correlation analysis. Feature selection is optimized using Hybrid Immunity League Championship Algorithm (HILCA), a tailored approach integrating bio-inspired optimization techniques. The DeepEnsembleNet architecture seamlessly integrates multiple neural network types to accommodate diverse data modalities. Extensive experimentation and hyperparameter tuning have yielded promising results, demonstrating the model's potential for accurate early diabetes detection. By concurrently optimizing feature selection and hyperparameters, this hybrid approach enhances overall performance. This innovation holds significant promise for improving diabetes treatment outcomes and enhancing patient quality of life.

Author Keywords: Feedforward Neural Networks and Cross validation

articleTitle: Blockchain-Enabled Real-Time Intrusion Detection Framework for a Cyber-Physical System
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Decision Aid Sciences and Applications (DASA)
abstract: In today's world, Cyber-Physical Systems (CPS) are facing growing risks from cyberattacks. In this paper we propose an idea of blockchain-enabled CPS framework to enhance our Cyber Physical system security. The framework we are aiming uses blockchain for immutable data storage and AI-driven intrusion detection. It aims to detect threats in real time and trigger automated responses in conditions of any unnoticed activity detected. This system and framework goal is to ensure data integrity, availability, and rapid threat mitigation. This paper outlines the design principles, architecture, and workflow of the proposed framework. We also discuss the potential of combining blockchain and AI for Cyber physical system security, addressing challenges like real-time performance, decentralized storage, and automated responses.

articleTitle: Data-Driven Approach to Coastal Water Quality Management: Enhancing Sustainable Decision-Making for Engineering and Development Initiatives
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Decision Aid Sciences and Applications (DASA)
abstract: This paper is part of undergraduate coursework addressing the ecological impacts of urbanization and industrialization, with a focus on water pollution and diminishing water resources in Bahrain coastal areas. The study analyzes water samples from Tubli Bay, Al-Hidd Walkway, and Busaiteen Beach using methodologies such as pH testing, turbidity assessment, conductivity measurement, Total Solids (TS), Total Suspended Solids (TSS), and Total Dissolved Solids (TDS) analysis. Key parameters, including pH, temperature, and turbidity, were assessed against international standards from the World Health Organization and the U.S. Environmental Protection Agency. Results indicated pH levels ranged from 7.15 to 7.44 and turbidity from 20.7 NTU to 22.1 NTU, suggesting suspended particles from sediment runoff and anthropogenic activities. Elevated TDS and conductivity measurements reflect significant salinity in the coastal areas studied. The objectives include monitoring water quality, evaluating compliance with regulatory standards, and assessing pollution impacts on aquatic ecosystems.

articleTitle: Assessing the Effects of Blackhole Attacks on MANET Reliability and Security
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Decision Aid Sciences and Applications (DASA)
abstract: Mobile Ad Hoc Networks (MANETs) are characterized by some important attributes, including infrastructure, mobile, and dynamic nature, which makes them have vast applications in different areas of computer networks. The black hole attack falls among the strongly criticized security threats within the framework of the MANETs. This deceptive behavior captures data packets from a source destined for the malicious node and then declines them when they are received. This paper comprehensively reviews prior studies done to analyze and mitigate black hole attacks in MANETs. Besides this, we will conduct a comparative analysis of the research above projects. The present paper extends prior work by actually performing the black hole assault simulations in a MANETs environment. This is done with the aid of the NS2 simulator and the Ad Hoc On-Demands Distance Vector (AODV) routing protocol. In this study, the black hole attack is analyzed and the consequences of the attack are assessed in terms of the system performance and security. We analyze crucial parameters like end-to-end latency, PDR, packet drop, and throughput to evaluate the consequences of this assault. From our results derived from the analysis of our simulations, we aim to present substantial points to do with the impacts of blackhole attacks on MANETs. In this way, our goal is to participate in the perpetually evolving efforts aimed at enhancing the security and reliability of such dynamic networks.

articleTitle: Object Tracking in Surveillance System Using Particle Filter and ACF Detection
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Decision Aid Sciences and Applications (DASA)
abstract: This paper presents a study on object tracking in surveillance systems using Particle Filter and Aggregate Channel Features (ACF) detection to address the challenges of accurately tracking multiple objects in dynamic environments. Object tracking is a crucial component in computer vision, with applications spanning from surveillance and security to autonomous navigation and robotics. In this work, we leverage Particle Filter, a robust Bayesian-based filtering algorithm known for its effectiveness in non-linear and non-Gaussian conditions, to track objects consistently over time. The ACF detection method is employed for its high precision in identifying objects across various frames, thereby enhancing initial detection accuracy. Performance testing is conducted across four datasets, using key metrics such as precision, Multiple Object Tracking Precision (MOTP), and Multiple Object Tracking Accuracy (MOTA) to evaluate effectiveness. The results show that while Particle Filter combined with ACF detection achieves consistently high precision (95-99%) and stable MOTP rates (69-79%), challenges arise in maintaining uninterrupted tracking accuracy, as evidenced by lower MOTA scores (3.1-7.2 %) and a significant rate of false negatives, especially in complex scenarios with occlusions. These findings suggest that although Particle Filter and ACF detection are effective for initial detection and data handling, enhancements or hybrid methods may be required for applications demanding high accuracy in continuous multi-object tracking.

articleTitle: Optimal Board Characteristics for Making Effective Decisions Affecting Financial Performance: An Examination Study
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Decision Aid Sciences and Applications (DASA)
abstract: This This study aims to test the relationship between the characteristics of the board of directors (BOD) and financial performance (FP) in the financial sector listed on the Bahrain bourse. To achieve the objectives of the study, all companies in the financial sector listed on the Bahrain bourse were studied, and the study sample consisted of 20 companies. The annual financial reports of companies have been relied on to extract data that helps test the relationship between the characteristics of the BOD and FP. The results of the study showed that there is no relationship between the characteristics of the BOD and the return on equity (ROE), and in light of the findings of the study, the study recommended several recommendations, most notably: keeping the size of the BOD at the minimum stipulated by the Bahraini corporate governance, as this limit enables the BOD to properly perform its supervisory activities. And conducting many studies because they are important for the decisionmaking process of the BOD and shareholders. The BOD should improve the quality of its strategic decision-making by establishing frameworks designed to prioritize long-term profitability and sustainability. By aligning board-level strategic decisions with performance targets, businesses may construct insight-driven, comprehensive, and responsive strategies that promote constant financial well-being.

articleTitle: Stochastic Pickup and Delivery Problem: A Bibliometric Review of Research Using VOSviewer
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Decision Aid Sciences and Applications (DASA)
abstract: In this paper, we utilize the bibliometric review software VOSviewer to investigate the extent of existing research and emerging trends associated with the Stochastic Pickup and Delivery Problem (SPDP), a significant challenge in efficient logistics and transportation. We retrieved articles published between 1983 and 2024 from two databases: Scopus and Web of Science. Our analysis identifies key authors, influential publications, and collaborative networks shaping the SPDP research landscape. The results indicate that the stochastic approach is becoming increasingly critical within the field of operations research, highlighting the importance of addressing relevant practical issues. Additionally, new research trends and collaborative associations are unveiled, serving as a valuable guide for studies focused on optimizing logistics systems under uncertainty. This analysis provides insight into the SPDP research corpus, underscoring the relevance of this problem in enhancing the efficiency of transportation systems in uncertain environments.

articleTitle: Business Model Design with Design Thinking and Business Model Canvas Approach in Metaverse Showroom PT. XYZ
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Decision Aid Sciences and Applications (DASA)
abstract: From market research and forecasts conducted by Adroit Market Research at the end of 2021, it has produced rapid growth rates in the global Metaverse market, including Southeast Asia. PT. XYZ has the Metaverse Showroom, a new experience in shopping for physical and digital products in the virtual world, providing information, product simulation, and direct service interaction on automotive products such as cars or other vehicles. The Metaverse Showroom was formed based on benchmarking from other global Metaverse platforms, which have yet to be adapted to the market in Indonesia. Therefore, a business model is needed that suits the needs of the people in Indonesia. In this study, the business model was designed by targeting Generation Z, who had previously entered the Metaverse as respondents. The method used is Design Thinking, which consists of 5 stages: Empathize, Define, Ideate, Prototype, and Test. In addition to Design Thinking, researchers use the Business Model Canvas (BMC), Customer Journey Map (CJM), and Service Blueprint (SB). Research results that need to be added to this research include community space features for automotive enthusiasm and interactive features that are integrated with the NFT system and collaborate with Brands. The researcher pours this into BMC along with eight other blocks. Then 3 CJM proposals have their personalities: users who want to find product information or intend to buy these products, users who wish to do NFT Hunting, and users who want to have a community in Metaverse showrooms. In operating the business model, customer actions range from seeking information to how aftersales are carried out. Then in its implementation, there are five internal units: the marketing team, admin, platform, avatar, arcade, and partners. Several support processes, namely, marketing analytics, and login page systems to push notification tools and services, support it.

articleTitle: Landslide Susceptibility Mapping in Gilgit-Baltistan: Leveraging Machine Learning for Risk Assessment
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Decision Aid Sciences and Applications (DASA)
abstract: This study examined the challenging issues of landslide detection along Gilgit-Baltistan's Karakoram Highway (KKH), where seismic activity and a dearth of data were significant issues161 characters. The study selected support vector machine (SVM), random forest (RF), and XGBoost algorithms to balance algorithm performance with ease of implementation. Finally, the study assessed the performance of the algorithms by fine-tuning them and optimizing their parameters. This was done by evaluating metrics such as the Area Under the Curve (AUC) and accuracy. Surprisingly, this comprehensive approach resulted in an average accuracy of 90% for all algorithms. These findings provide valuable insights for improving disaster prevention strategies and guiding land-use planning efforts along the KKH highway.

articleTitle: Tort Liability for Engineers: Bridging Law and Practicality
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Decision Aid Sciences and Applications (DASA)
abstract: This paper addresses the challenge of reconciling engineering decision-making with the complexities of tort law, particularly negligence. It focuses on how tort liability can be made practically understandable for engineers, who often struggle to navigate legal obligations due to the contrasting nature of legal and engineering mindsets. By examining key legal cases and principles, the study offers a simplified, actionable framework that engineers can use to predict and mitigate liability risks. The goal is to bridge the gap between legal theory and engineering practice, providing engineers with clear, practical guidance on how to avoid legal pitfalls while maintaining professional responsibility.

articleTitle: Beyond the Code: A Meta-Analysis of Cultural and Societal Factors in Engineering Ethics
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Decision Aid Sciences and Applications (DASA)
abstract: Since concerns in the ethical issues of engineering projects can cause harm, both to the public and the environment, the topic has received many attentions. This meta-synthesis will seek to pull together current knowledge to illuminate the ethical issues which are encountered within engineering projects including: the moral obligation of engineers; conflict of interest; safety; and environmental concerns. Due to the relative unavailability of important theoretical studies on ethical issues and decision-making in engineering profession, this study uses findings from substantial quantitative studies, qualitative case analytical studies, and formal or standard theoretical studies in various fields of engineering to analyze common ethical issues, and assess the roles of regulatory frameworks, corporate governance, and code of conducts as agents in ethical decision processes. Results show that these engineers are restrained by code of technical professionalism, but their principles of ethics are limited by extraneous factors such as financial viability and/or company dictates. The author then discusses the implications of the findings to practice and suggests ideas for implementing ethical education to engineering and for strengthening the function of professional engineering institutions in the ethical development of engineers.

articleTitle: Optimal Algorithm for Managing on-Campus Student Transportation
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Decision Aid Sciences and Applications (DASA)
abstract: This study analyzed the transportation issues at the University of Bahrain Sakhir campus, where a bus system with an unorganized and fixed number of buses allocated each semester was in place. Data was collected through a survey, on-site observations, and student schedules to estimate the number of buses needed. The study was limited to students who require to move between buildings for academic purposes and not those who choose to ride buses for other reasons. An algorithm was designed to calculate the optimal number of buses for each time slot, and for each day. This solution could improve transportation efficiency, lower costs, enhance students' mobility experience, and decrease CO<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</inf> emissions. A series of recommendations were provided to university officials including the need for further research to examine creating new routes and implementing express buses.

articleTitle: Brand Advocacy Research: A Performance Analysis Between 2007 and 2024
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Decision Aid Sciences and Applications (DASA)
abstract: This study intends to give a complete performance analysis of brand advocacy research, showing its publication pattern and most influential publications. The analysis, which uses data from the Scopus database, combines performance analysis and science mapping tools. The inclusion requirements were that the sources be peer-reviewed academic publications written in English and published between 2007 and May 14, 2024. The stringent screening method reduced our dataset from an initial 214 documents to 167 highly relevant publications. The data show considerable growth in brand advocacy research, particularly after 2020, with a large rise in publications in 2023. Notable authors include Nour Adham Abdelrazek, S B Abdinagoro, and Allam Abu Farah. The study's conclusions for managers include the necessity for strong digital engagement strategies, the integration of CSR activities, and an emphasis on emotional and relational components of customer behaviour to increase brand advocacy.

articleTitle: Analytical Study of the Features and Parameters of Off-Angle Iris Image vs. Deep Learning Model
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Decision Aid Sciences and Applications (DASA)
abstract: This paper presents an analytical study and a technique for extracting the features of a common case of images of the iris called off-angle iris which was taken for persons identification systems. The main problem when using biological iris measurements to identify the persons is the difficulty of identifying and extracting features of the iris. This problem is increasing when dealing with off-angle iris and it leads to decreased system accuracy and increased system rate error. In return, all the transfer learning techniques face difficulties in the case of heavily degraded data and partially occluded, and off-angle. A new method has a whole new methodology to deal with the image as it is without transformation processes. A new algorithm has been included for extracting features of the iris through the pupil switching points. The most discriminating points of the iris depend on the biological human eye statistics and analytical study. It has been trained and tested on the common images of the off-angle iris database so-called: “CASIA Iris 1.0”. It has been implemented in the MATLAB environment. The results showed the efficiency of this technique, high precision and more importantly low failed acceptance rate. It emphasized that it is adaptive as well as efficiency improvement of the system.

articleTitle: A Deep Reinforcement Learning-Based LSTM-Enhanced A3C Model for Predicting Bacterial Gill Disease in Aquaculture Water
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Decision Aid Sciences and Applications (DASA)
abstract: Aquaculture, a rapidly growing industry that plays a crucial role in global food security and contributes significantly to the economies of many countries, faces substantial challenges in managing aquatic diseases. Among such diseases is Bacterial Gill Disease (BGD), which may cause severe economic losses if not detected early and promptly treated. This paper introduces a novel deep reinforcement learning approach, the LSTM-Enhanced Asynchronous Advantage Actor-Critic (LE-A3C) model, which was proposed to predict BGD by analyzing multivariate water quality indicators. The approach integrates LSTM's sequential learning capabilities with the advantage-based optimization and the asynchronous parallel learning approach of the A3C algorithm. This could remarkably capture complex temporal dependencies as well as water quality patterns, which allows the proposed LE-A3C to identify early warning signs for outbreaking potential BGD outbreaks. The asynchronous learning in A3C would enable multiple water quality scenarios to be explored and optimized concurrently; this actually accelerates learning and increases its robustness in real-time predictive tasks. This boosts the speed and accuracy of detecting diseases and, therefore is a highly efficient tool for aquaculture systems. The proposed LE-A3C model was implemented on the “Ponds data” dataset, and experimental results clearly demonstrate its superior performance compared to existing models, achieving a predictive accuracy of 97.50%. In comparison with the existing models M-DQN achieved an accuracy of 88.52%, the M-GRU model reached 78.92%, and the S-LSTM model recorded 74.31 % accuracy.

articleTitle: A Bibliometric Review of the Integration of Healthcare 4.0 Technologies in the Hospital Sector
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Decision Aid Sciences and Applications (DASA)
abstract: This paper provides a bibliometric review of the integration of Healthcare 4.0 technologies in hospital management. Analyzing 198 studies, the review identifies key trends, system configurations, and best practices in deploying digital healthcare tools such as the Internet of Things (IoT), artificial intelligence (AI), and telemedicine. The research indicates that publications in this domain grew significantly between 2014 and 2024, peaking in 2022. This review highlights the transformative potential of these technologies to optimize resource management, improve patient outcomes, and enhance healthcare efficiency. Despite progress, challenges such as data privacy and system integration remain unresolved. This study offers valuable insights into future research and practical applications of healthcare 4.0 technologies in hospitals.

articleTitle: The Effect of Digital Marketing on Reducing Reverse Logistics Costs in Saudi Arabia's E-commerce Market: A Qualitative Study
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Decision Aid Sciences and Applications (DASA)
abstract: As the e-commerce market in Saudi Arabia rapidly expands, so to do reverse logistics costs as a result of high return rates. This study specifically considers how digital marketing can help minimize these costs in the form of product returns and refers to techniques like correct descriptions, out-of-the-box promotions, post-purchase interaction etc. The research is qualitative in nature, the data collection had been executed with semi-structured interviews within logistics and e-commerce marketing professionals in Saudi Arabia. Digital marketing, we can logically infer from the study has a huge bearing on customer expectations and in turn redemption rates which ultimately leads to better return rates and reduced reverse logistics costs. Finally, the paper ends with a few ideas on how digital marketing might tip logistics performance and profitability in favour of e-commerce In Saudi Arabia.

articleTitle: Leveraging Conflict Management Strategies in Petrochemical Engineering Companies to Foster Managerial Creativity
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Decision Aid Sciences and Applications (DASA)
abstract: The research aims to examine the impact of organizational conflict management strategies' impact (collaboration, competition, and compromise) on managerial creativity in one of the Petrochemical Engineering Industries Company in Bahrain. In order to respond to the research questions and evaluate the hypotheses, the study uses a descriptive analytical technique. A total of (214) questionnaires were electronically distributed to the research sample. With 206 employees answering in total, the response rate is high (96%). Multiple and simple regression analyses were used in the data analysis process to test the study hypotheses. The main Findings show that organizational conflict management strategies impact managerial creativity in the research organization. Furthermore, the research concludes that the research organization's employees have a high level of creativity. Also, findings revealed a clear diversity in the use of the three organizational conflict management strategies by the company's management, through which they contribute to the continuous support of employees such as finding the solutions to problems, creating a competitive and stimulating atmosphere that contributes to increasing of productivity and maintaining the establishment of relationships between all parties involved in the conflict.

articleTitle: The Impact of the Work Environment in the Organization on Job Security for Employees: An Applied Study on Al-Rawabi Private School in the Kingdom of Bahrain
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Decision Aid Sciences and Applications (DASA)
abstract: The present study investigates the influence of work environment factors—including incentives and rewards, work relations, and working conditions—on job security at Al-Rawabi Private School in Bahrain. A structured questionnaire was employed to survey a sample of 160 employees. SPSS was employed to analyze the data, which included Pearson correlation and regression analysis, in order to ascertain the relationships between variables. The results indicate that job security is most significantly influenced by work relations, incentives and rewards, and working conditions. The critical role of these factors in assuring employee stability is underscored by the model explains 75.5% of the variance in job security. According to the research, it is imperative to improve working conditions, ensure an equitable distribution of rewards, and enhance work relations in order to promote job security. The study provides valuable insights into the literature, particularly in the educational sector, and offers actionable recommendations for improving the work environment to increase employment security in similar institutions. The results' generalizability may be impacted by the focus on a particular institution, which is one of the limitations.

articleTitle: Development of A Webmail and Integration With Spam Detection System Using Bi-LSTM Method
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Decision Aid Sciences and Applications (DASA)
abstract: Email spam is a significant issue for email users as it is not only disruptive but also poses a threat to data security through phishing and malware attacks. Therefore, an effective and efficient spam detection system is required. This study developed a spam detection system using the Bi-directional Long Short-Term Memory (Bi-LSTM) method, aimed at classifying emails as spam or not spam with high accuracy. This topic is important due to the increasing volume of spam emails threatening users' privacy and security. Currently, built-in spam filters, such as those in Gmail and Outlook, still lack accuracy, particularly in avoiding important emails being mistakenly categorized as spam. The spam detection system developed using Bi-LSTM involves several key stages, such as data collection, preprocessing to clean the data, feature extraction, and email classification. Bi-LSTM was chosen for its ability to process text sequences bidirectionally, enhancing spam detection accuracy by considering the context of words in the email. System testing showed that the Bi-LSTM method achieved an accuracy rate of 99.90% in detecting spam emails. This result indicates that the system is effective in identifying and classifying emails as spam or not, with good potential for integration into various email platforms.

articleTitle: A Comprehensive Review of Technology Acceptance Models in the Context of Digital Government Services
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Decision Aid Sciences and Applications (DASA)
abstract: The adoption of digital government services is crucial for realizing the benefits of public sector digitization. Despite the widespread implementation of digital initiatives, low adoption rates remain a significant challenge in many countries. To understand the factors influencing public acceptance of digital services, researchers have employed various technology acceptance models, including the Theory of Reasoned Action (TRA), Theory of Planned Behavior (TPB), and the Unified Theory of Acceptance and Use of Technology (UTAUT). However, these models, originally developed for commercial and private-sector contexts, often fail to account for the unique factors influencing digital government service adoption, such as public engagement, transparency, and trust. This paper provides a comprehensive review of the existing technology acceptance models and explores their application within the digital government domain. We analyze their strengths and limitations, particularly in addressing the complexities of public sector adoption. The review highlights critical gaps in the literature, particularly regarding the role of user experience, public trust, and the impact of emerging technologies like artificial intelligence and personalization in the adoption of digital services. These insights form the foundation for proposing a new, more comprehensive model tailored to digital government, setting the stage for future research and practical applications.

articleTitle: Performance Analysis of Energy and Secure Efficient Routing for Wireless Sensor Networks
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Decision Aid Sciences and Applications (DASA)
abstract: Wireless Sensor Networks (WSNs) are essential for various applications, but their architecture makes them vulnerable to attacks. While traditional security methods like authentication and encryption offer some protection, they often fall short against specific node attacks. This paper introduces the Secure Energy Aware Routing (SEAR) strategy, which uses trust-based assessments to exclude malicious nodes while optimizing energy consumption. SEAR factors in node trust, hop time, and residual energy to ensure reliable data transmission through trustworthy nodes. MATLAB simulations on networks of varying sizes (100–500) compare SEAR with existing methods (EAD and EASER), demonstrating SEAR's superior performance. Results show significant improvements in packet delivery ratio (13-16%), network throughput (19–24 %), energy consumption (32-36<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">%</sup>), packet loss (16-190/0), and end-to-end latency (21-26<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">%</sup>), proving SEAR's effectiveness in enhancing WSN security, energy efficiency, and performance.

articleTitle: Financial Sustainability in the Spotlight: Unraveling the Impact of Financial Independence, Debt Ratio, and Capital Expenditure
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Decision Aid Sciences and Applications (DASA)
abstract: The study investigates how financial independence, debt ratio, and capital expenditure affect the financial sustainability of local governments in Aceh Province, Indonesia. The results of this study indicate are intended to guide policymakers in districts and municipalities in Aceh, helping them develop strategies that promote financial sustainability without compromising future fiscal health or the quality of public services. The study analyzed data from 23 districts and municipalities in Aceh Province over a five-year period (2018–2022). The researchers employed panel data regression analysis using Eviews (version 12) and SPSS (version 23) software. Data sources consisted of local government financial reports that had been audited by the Supreme Audit Agency (BPK) and the BPS-Statistics Indonesia (BPS). The main findings show that financial independence is positively correlated with financial sustainability. In contrast, debt levels and capital expenditure show a negative impact on the economic sustainability of local governments.

articleTitle: Hybrid Deep Learning Architecture with Attention Mechanisms for Enhanced Plant Leaf Disease Detection and Classification
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Decision Aid Sciences and Applications (DASA)
abstract: Plant leaf diseases pose a major challenge in agriculture, requiring early detection to prevent losses and ensure food security. In this study, a hybrid deep learning model is proposed to improve the classification of 35 plant leaf disease categories. The framework integrates two pre-trained Convolutional Neural Network (CNN) models—DenseNet121 and MobileNetV2—along with a custom model, all enhanced by attention mechanisms for better feature extraction. Fine-tuning was performed using attention modules and global average pooling layers, followed by fully connected layers with Swish activation, dropout, batch normalization, and L2 regularization. The model was trained on the New Plant Diseases Dataset from Kaggle and achieved higher accuracy, precision, recall, and Fl-score compared to baseline models. Grad-CAM (Gradient-weighted Class Activation Mapping) was used to identify the most influential regions in the leaf images, improving the model's explainability and reliability. This hybrid approach shows promise for practical application in agricultural disease detection systems.

articleTitle: Bayesian Regression for Predicting Subscription to Bank Term Deposits in Direct Marketing Campaigns
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Decision Aid Sciences and Applications (DASA)
abstract: In the highly competitive environment of the banking industry, it is essential to precisely forecast the behavior of customers in order to maximize the effectiveness of marketing initiatives and improve financial consequences. The purpose of this research is to examine the efficacy of logit and probit models in predicting term deposit subscriptions using a Portuguese bank's direct marketing data. There are several demographic, economic, and behavioral characteristics in the dataset that affect the probability of subscribing. To increase model performance and provide an unbiased evaluation, the target variable was balanced, considering the inherent imbalance in the dataset. The two model's prediction abilities were evaluated using Bayesian techniques and Leave-One-Out Cross-Validation (LOO-CV). The logit model performed better than the probit model in handling this classification problem. The results highlight the relevance of model selection when dealing with complicated decision-making processes in the financial services industry and imbalanced datasets.
