abstract: This study examines whether financial restatement significantly affects the correlation between financial performance and firm value of companies listed on the Indonesia Stock Exchange. Furthermore, this study investigates the moderating role of auditor competence on the relationship between financial restatement and firm value. The sample was 300 non-financial companies that have undertaken to present financial restatement from 2018 until 2023. To examine the hypothesis, we employed multiple regression and moderated regression analysis. The research results show that financial performance positively and significantly impacts the company's value. The restatement of financial statements positively and significantly impacts company value. Furthermore, financial restatement moderated the effect of financial performance on company value in companies listed on the Indonesia Stock Exchange. The latest results show that auditor competence strengthens the influence of restatement on firm value.

articleTitle: Gamification as a Practice of Performance Improvement: The Role of Innovative Behavior
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Decision Aid Sciences and Applications (DASA)
abstract: Gamification has generated a lot of attention and controversy in organizations as many see it as a powerful tool to motivate individuals and increase activity in business. Not much research has been carried out in the context of gamification applied to the automotive sector in Indonesia. This research aims to try to understand the influence of gamification strategies on employee performance through individual innovative behavior among Mitsubishi dealer employees in Indonesia. A quantitative approach was chosen and applied in this study. Partial Least Square - Structural Equation Modeling (PLS-SEM) was applied as a data analysis technique supported by the Smart-PLS 4 computer software program with a sample size of 120 respondents. The findings of this study indicate that the gamification program has not been able to fully have a positive impact on employee performance, in this case the level of individual employee innovative behavior plays a full mediation role in making gamification in the workplace have a positive impact on improving employee performance. The novelty of this research is that it explores one specific outcome of gamified competition based on affordance theory. It analyzes the role of innovative behavior as a mediating factor and expands the scope of gamification literature by focusing on a workplace context driven by workplace design that incorporates competition through gamification.

articleTitle: Effects of Job Characteristics on Organizational Identity in Higher Education Sector in the Kingdom of Bahrain
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Decision Aid Sciences and Applications (DASA)
abstract: This research examines the factors affecting organizational identity (OI) in higher education sector in the Kingdom of Bahrain. More specifically, it tries to explore the influence of Job Characteristics (JC) on Organizational Identity (OI). a self-administered questionnaire was directed to academic and admin staff in the higher education sector in the kingdom of Bahrain. (118) academic and admin staff at higher education institutions in the Kingdom of Bahrain were surveyed through a simple random sampling method. The researchers hypothesized that there are significant impacts for Job Characteristics (Skill Variety, Task Identity, Task Significance, Autonomy, Feedback) on Organizational Identity for the employees in higher education. The findings revealed that this hypothesis was accepted for the effect of (JC) as a whole on (OI). According to the five dimensions of (JC), the results revealed that both of task significance and feedback are the only two dimensions that affect the organizational identity of workers in the sector in question. These results are discussed and several conclusions and implications were drawn, as well as more recommendations and future researches were suggested.

articleTitle: The Future of Engineering: Adapting to Legal and Political Changes
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Decision Aid Sciences and Applications (DASA)
abstract: Navigating the Changing Landscape of Engineering: Legal, Political, and Technical Perspectives Engineering practice is largely driven by legal, political, and technological developments This paper examines the impact of these changes on the engineering profession. Engaging in intellectual property rights litigation can be time and resource-intensive, highlighting the importance of clearly communicating IPR ownership at the beginning of a project. The regulatory environment, including health and safety legislation, is heavily influenced by technology, requiring engineers to build “navigational capital” to successfully navigate these environments Political changes such as geopolitics and globalization also strongly influence engineering practices, requiring strategic changes. Meanwhile, technological advances offer opportunities for productivity, safety and environmental improvements, but implementing these innovations also requires thinking about change If they are to navigate this evolving landscape, engineers must acquire social skills, such as fact systems, and delegitimize opponents and Emphasizes the importance of actively adapting and innovating in response to dynamic legal, political and technological forces doing their job.

articleTitle: Hotel Booking Cancellation Prediction Using Applied Bayesian Models
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Decision Aid Sciences and Applications (DASA)
abstract: This study applies Bayesian models to predict hotel booking cancellations, a key challenge affecting resource allocation, revenue, and customer satisfaction in the hospitality industry. Using a Kaggle dataset with 36,285 observations and 17 features, Bayesian Logistic Regression and Beta-Binomial models were implemented. The logistic model, applied to 12 features and 5,000 randomly selected observations, outperformed the Beta-Binomial model in predictive accuracy. Key predictors included the number of adults, children, stay duration, lead time, car parking space, room type, and special requests. Model evaluation using Leave-One-Out Cross-Validation (LOO-CV) confirmed strong alignment between observed and predicted outcomes, demonstrating the model's robustness. Special requests and parking availability were found to be the strongest predictors of cancellation. This Bayesian approach provides a valuable tool for improving booking management and operational efficiency in the hotel industry.

articleTitle: Monitoring Packaging Defects in a Logistic Company for the Determination of Type-II Errors
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Decision Aid Sciences and Applications (DASA)
abstract: In the logistics sector, defects in packaging can seriously impact product quality, increasing the chances of damage during transit and potentially putting consumers at risk. As a result, poor packaging quality can lead to more product returns, recalls, and waste, which may result in decreasing customer loyalty and the company's reputation. This study introduces an extended <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$c$</tex> control chart with picture fuzzy sets (PFSs) for monitoring packaging quality in the logistics sector. This proposed approach monitors packaging processes in logistics while accounting for uncertainty, demonstrating how fuzzy logic can handle and model this uncertainty effectively. By representing process uncertainty with PFSs, a more sensitive and accurate control chart is achieved. Based on that, the study aims to help packaging operators in the logistics sector identify problems early and intervene with corrective actions as needed, using the proposed extended methodology. The effectiveness of the proposed approach is demonstrated with an illustrative example. Also, to show the performance of it, average run lengths for both in-control and out-of-control scenarios are calculated. Based on the results, the proposed approach increases in overall efficiency and product reliability by reducing type-II errors and allowing better representation of the problem environment under uncertainty.

articleTitle: Building the Future of Public Services: Introducing the Digital Government Services Acceptance Model (DGSAM)
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Decision Aid Sciences and Applications (DASA)
abstract: Adopting digital government services is essential for public sector digitization, yet low adoption rates persist. Traditional models like TAM, TRA, TPB, and UTAUT, designed for commercial use, often overlook key factors in digital government adoption, such as public engagement, transparency, and trust. This paper reviews these models, analyzing their strengths and limitations in the public sector context, highlighting gaps related to user experience, trust, and emerging technologies like AI. These insights lay the groundwork for proposing a new model tailored to digital government adoption.

articleTitle: Advancing Energy Efficiency in Residential Construction: Building Envelope Optimization in Hot-Arid Climates
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Decision Aid Sciences and Applications (DASA)
abstract: The efficiency of a building's envelope significantly influences its ability to conserve energy and minimize carbon emissions, especially in residential structures. This research investigates how different envelope design features affect energy use in an arid climate. A residential house in Bahrain served as the case study, with simulations conducted using IESVE energy modeling software. The analysis explored the influence of various envelope components and operational variables. Among the strategies assessed, incorporating 50 mm of expanded polystyrene insulation into external walls emerged as the most effective method for reducing energy demand in Bahrain's climate. Furthermore, the findings demonstrated that the g-value of windows has a greater effect on reducing solar heat transfer compared to the U-value.

articleTitle: Enhancing User Satisfaction: How Does the ISS-ECM Model Drive the Continued Use of Travel Apps?
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Decision Aid Sciences and Applications (DASA)
abstract: Travel apps are crucial for travelers who want to plan, reserve, and manage their trips easily and efficiently. This study decisively explores Indonesia's most popular travel applications, examining the powerful impact of the Information System Success Model and the Expectation Confirmation Model on users' intentions to persist in using these apps. This study effectively combines both models and highlights how information, system, service quality, expectation confirmation, and user satisfaction influence continuance usage intentions. Data was thoroughly collected from 240 respondents who actively use travel apps in Indonesia, and the analysis was conducted using SEM with SmartPLS software. The results demonstrate that information quality, system quality, service quality, and expectation confirmation significantly boost user satisfaction. Furthermore, user satisfaction is pivotal in driving the intention to continue using these applications. These findings firmly emphasize the critical importance of enhancing the quality of information, systems, and services to ensure sustained engagement with travel applications.

articleTitle: Integrating Machine Learning and Sentiment Analysis: A Comparative Study on Mental Health Classification from Social Media Data
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Decision Aid Sciences and Applications (DASA)
abstract: The present research paper categorises the different statuses of mental health, employing various techniques of machine learning. It also looks into the emergence of problems due to class imbalance and increases the feature overlapping in any multiclass dataset. The dataset contains 52,681 entries compiled painstakingly from Reddit, Twitter, and Kaggle. There are seven predefined statuses: Normal, Depression, Suicidal, Anxiety, Stress, Bipolar, and Personality Disorder. In the dataset preparation, comprehensive preprocessing techniques involved text cleaning, tokenization, stemming, and TF-IDF vectorization. The following step was to resample and address class imbalance using methods like random over-sampling. Finally, this paper developed, trained, and evaluated three machine learning models: Decision Tree, Logistic Regression, and XGBoost-XGB-with hyperparameter optimization through GridSearchCV. Performance metrics compared for the models are accuracy, precision, recall, F1-score, and confusion matrices. XGBoost performed the best with an accuracy of 82%, outperforming precision and recall in most classes. This was followed by Logistic Regression at 78% and Decision Tree at 67%, which didn't do too well in predicting the minority class. Again, the results show that the ensemble methods, like XGBoost, are powerful when handling these kinds of imbalanced data with complex multiclass problems. Valuable insights provided by this study will help develop intelligent mental health tools, thereby facilitating timely intervention and care. Future studies will employ advanced techniques, such as transformer-based models, multi-modal integrations of data, and domain-specific embeddings, to further improve the accuracy of classification and contextual understanding. This work establishes a robust framework for advancing mental health analysis by machine-learning methods.

articleTitle: Decision-Making Dynamics: Analyzing the Economic Influence of Sports Tourism on Bahrain's Growing Industry
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Decision Aid Sciences and Applications (DASA)
abstract: Tourism in Bahrain will rise in 2022 and reach 10 million visitors, even forecasting that tourism can improve Bahrain's growing tourism industry. This study aimed to discover the Sports Tourist contribution to the Kingdom of Bahrain's economy by analyzing this sector's Capabilities and Opportunities. The methodology employed in this study was a quantitative method based on the analysis and standard estimation by building traditional models to measure the impact of tourism activity. This impact was represented by two variables: tourism revenues (TR) and the number of visitors (NV), and their effects on some variables of the Bahraini macro-economy. These variables were represented by Gross Domestic Product (GDP), Domestic consumption (DC), Domestic investment (DI), Domestic saving (DS), Exports (DX), and Imports (DM). The study utilized both linear and logarithmic functions to analyze the data for the period spanning from 1995 to 2020. The study also estimated the expected values and drew their course for the period between 2022 and 2027. Findings refer that sustainable tourism must include tourism planning, development, and management in heritage areas within protection or sustainable development strategies. Tourism should be planned and managed sustainably for economic uses optimal for the natural and human environment in the heritage area. Information and studies should be available on the nature of tourism and its impact on the population and the cultural environment before and during development for the local community so that it can participate and influence the overall development trends-practical recommendations introduced in this narrative.

articleTitle: The Impact of Burnout and Stress on Employee Productivity at Batelco in the Kingdom of Bahrain
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Decision Aid Sciences and Applications (DASA)
abstract: The present study investigates the impact of psychological stress and burnout on employee productivity at Batelco in the Kingdom of Bahrain. The research examines the relationships between these variables by employing a descriptive-analytical methodology to acquire data from 169 employees using a structured questionnaire. The findings indicate that there are substantial negative correlations between employee productivity and both exhaustion and psychological stress. This underscores the urgent necessity for organizational interventions to alleviate these factors. The investigation employed a cross-sectional design, utilizing descriptive-analytical methodology. We distributed a structured questionnaire to 169 Batelco employees to collect data. The questionnaire assessed employee productivity, psychological tension, and burnout. Research employed SPSS to analyze the data and assess the relationships between the variables. The results indicate that fatigue and psychological stress significantly reduce employee productivity. The research demonstrates that it is imperative to mitigate psychological tension and exhaustion in order to optimize employee productivity at Batelco. Promoting a supportive work environment and implementing targeted wellness programs can ultimately enhance organizational performance by mitigating these negative effects.

articleTitle: WebMail Development and Implementation of Email Spam Detection Using Convolutional Neural Network (CNN) Method
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Decision Aid Sciences and Applications (DASA)
abstract: Email spam poses a significant issue in the digital era, disrupting user experiences and potentially threatening security. This study investigates the performance and effectiveness of the Convolutional Neural Network (CNN) method in detecting email spam, leveraging its ability to extract and analyze patterns from textual data. The model's performance was evaluated through confusion matrix metrics, including precision, recall, and Fl-score. in addition, a webmail application was developed to integrate the CNN spam detection model, providing users with essential email functionalities. This application allows users to send, receive, and manage emails via SMTP for email transmission and IMAP/POP3 for retrieval. Developed with a front-end using HTML, CSS, and Bootstrap, and a backend in PHP and JSON, the webmail system stores all email data in an SQL database. Python was utilized to implement and train the CNN model, which automatically filters incoming emails, classifying them as either spam or non-spam before they reach the user's inbox. The results demonstrate that the CNN model achieved a high accuracy of 99.80% with the Adam Optimizer, indicating its robust capability in accurately detecting spam emails.

articleTitle: Crisis Management and its Impact on the Quality of Administrative Decisions Case Study of Greater Amman Municipality/Jordan
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Decision Aid Sciences and Applications (DASA)
abstract: The study aimed to identify crisis management and its impact on the quality of administrative decisions in the Greater Amman Municipality, with its dimensions (early warning stage, prevention and preparedness stage, damage containment stage, activity recovery stage, and learning stage). The study also sought to ensure the consistency of these practices with the objectives of the Greater Amman Municipality. The researcher used the descriptive analytical approach, and selected the study population from the employees of the municipality who hold administrative and supervisory positions, totaling 112 individuals. A comprehensive survey method was used due to the small size of the study population, and a questionnaire was utilized as a tool for collecting information from the respondents. A total of 112 questionnaires were distributed, through the electronic link have been fully retrieved and are valid for analysis. The study concluded with several findings, most of notably a high degree of agreement among the respondents regarding the alignment between the stages of crisis management and the quality of administrative decisions in the Greater Amman Municipality. The study recommended the importance of establishing a specialized administrative unit for crisis management.

articleTitle: Enhancing Decision-Making Through Non-Financial Risk Disclosure in Bahrain's Companies
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Decision Aid Sciences and Applications (DASA)
abstract: This study aims to evaluate the degree of disclosure on non-financial risks (NFR) among non-financial firms listed on the Bahrain Bourse (BHB). This study includes all non-financial firms listed on the BHB to achieve its aims. The study employed content analysis, utilising a sample of 19 companies and 95 observations from 2018 to 2022. The study relied on the descriptive method to assess the level of NFR disclosure. The key findings show a decline in the level of disclosure regarding non-financial risks. The most revealed components of NFR were empowerment risk elements, followed by strategic risks. The study found that the materials sector disclosed the highest number of items, followed by the industrial sector, the communication services sector, real estate firms, consumer discretionary, and consumer staples. This study has implications for legislative bodies in the Kingdom of Bahrain, as it aims to enhance the principle of transparency and reduce information asymmetry, by encouraging greater voluntary disclosure overall, with a specific focus on NFR disclosure.

articleTitle: Empowering Smart Homes with Fog Computing for IoT Connectivity
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Decision Aid Sciences and Applications (DASA)
abstract: Innovative grid technology leverages Information and Communication Technology (ICT) to enhance energy efficiency and mitigate losses. This paper introduces a “novel three-tier hierarchical framework for smart homes within the Internet of Things (IoT)” ecosystem, addressing the current shortage of intelligent solutions that underutilize IoT advantages. Our framework's primary objective is to elevate smart homes to the microgrid level, enabling the seamless integration from the microgrid's renewable distributed energy sources and attaining maximum energy efficiency. In addition to traditional data processing, we propose the application of fog computing in smart homes. Through a rigorous simulation using real smart meter datasets, our study demonstrates that fog computing, mainly when using predictive filtering, may drastically cut down on the amount of data being sent and the load on the home's network. This innovation holds immense potential for revolutionizing energy management and resource allocation in the context of smart homes, thus contributing to a sustainable and efficient future. This research represents a critical step towards harnessing the power of IoT and fog computing in smart grids and homes, offering a promising path towards more intelligent, eco-friendly, and energy-efficient living spaces.

articleTitle: Perceptions of Virtual Environments in Arab States: Unveiling the Nexus of Money Laundering and Terrorist Financing
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Decision Aid Sciences and Applications (DASA)
abstract: This study utilizes some sociological methods and primary marketing research to explain the differences in public attitudes in various Arab countries towards the usage of artificial intelligence (AI) in the fight against disinformation, with a focus on ethical and legal aspects. In other words, the impression is created that the current study seeks to measure possibilities of potential harm and effective usage of sources of information, illusionary though, of AI in relation to information and security problems. This study also investigates the already existing conditions that shift social media users' attitudes towards the use of AI tools for the purposes of countering misinformation by using the quantitative approach. Also, the research aims at classifying and identifying the legal public and illegal hate speech on social media platforms using AI tools. The significance of this research is that in engaging policy makers and other stakeholders, their attitudes regarding the combating of misinformation using AI technologies are gauged, thus seeking to draft policies on the use of AI technologies with the emphasize that ethical and legal considerations are critical in this area.

articleTitle: Machine Learning for Predicting Employee Attrition: A Bibliometric Analysis
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Decision Aid Sciences and Applications (DASA)
abstract: The escalating phenomenon of employee attrition poses significant organizational stability and growth challenges, making its prediction a focal area within human resource management and organizational studies. This research provides a comprehensive bibliometric analysis of research trends, collaborations, and impacts in predicting employee attrition using machine learning (ML) algorithms from 2010 to 2023. Drawing on data from the Scopus database, this study maps the intellectual landscape by examining publication patterns, global collaboration networks, author contributions, and keyword cooccurrence. The findings reveal a marked increase in research activity, particularly in recent years, driven by advancements in ML techniques and the growing availability of workforce data. The United States, India, and China lead in research output, while strong international collaborations reflect the field's interdisciplinary nature, integrating insights from management, psychology, and data science. This review identifies critical journals and influential articles, highlights emerging themes such as industry-specific applications and advanced ML models, and provides a roadmap for future research. The novelty of this study lies in its systematic mapping of the research landscape, offering actionable insights for researchers, practitioners, and organizational leaders to enhance predictive capabilities and improve employee retention strategies.

articleTitle: Modeling Green Hydrogen Supply and Demand Dynamics in India Using System Dynamics
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Decision Aid Sciences and Applications (DASA)
abstract: Study develops a System Dynamics (SD) model to predict the effects of subsidies on the price and supply of Green Hydrogen (GH) while estimating demand based on varying production costs and prices up to 2030. SD leverages feedback system theory for modelling and simulation, making it ideal for analyzing complex systems like GH production, which represents the cleanest industrial method for hydrogen fuel. In response to global sustainability concerns, the Indian Government has launched the “National Green Hydrogen Mission.” This model provides insights into key factors affecting GH production, such as capital costs and construction timelines, and assesses their influence on the market's demand-supply gap. It also explores how different subsidy structures could shape the future of the GH market in India. Findings indicate that maintaining hydrogen plant construction times under two years is critical for achieving government targets. Moreover, implementing aggressive, short-term subsidies proves more effective in boosting hydrogen production than offering lower subsidies over extended periods. These insights can significantly guide industry decision-makers in strategizing and developing effective policies for GH's market success.

articleTitle: An Efficient and Secure Framework for Smart Healthcare Using IoT and Machine Learning
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Decision Aid Sciences and Applications (DASA)
abstract: The healthcare systems worldwide are challenged with the increased demand for rapid and efficient patient care. In this context, an advanced solution is required to meet the growing needs. This paper presents an intelligent healthcare framework integrating IoT devices with machine learning algorithms to enable real-time predictive patient monitoring. It comprises a four-layer architecture: data acquisition from IoT sensors, data preprocessing, analytics for predictive modeling, and an application layer for user interactions. Validated with data from the MIMIC-III and PhysioNet datasets along with 12 months of IoT sensor data from a university medical center, the framework achieved 96% prediction accuracy with precision, recall, and ROC AUC scores of 0.95, 0.96, and 0.98, respectively. The system had a great response time of 200 milliseconds. It has greatly improved early detection by 36.9% and reduced false alarms by 68%. False alarms decreased from 25% to 8%, and response time was reduced from 45 to 12 minutes, or 73.3 %. Resource utilization analysis reflects optimal performance since the analytics layer hit a spike at 45% CPU utilization, thereby pointing out optimal load management. Patient satisfaction also rose to 22.7%, increasing from 75% to 92%, reflecting the framework's impact on care quality. All these results render the framework an effective and scalable solution that optimizes healthcare resources while improving care for the patient.

articleTitle: Analysis of Electronic Commerce for the Promotion of Sustainable Development in Nigeria: Addressing Challenges and Envisaging Future Prospects
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Decision Aid Sciences and Applications (DASA)
abstract: Internet adoption has touched all parts of life, including e-commerce, at a remarkable speed. E-commerce may boost Nigeria's economy, create jobs, promote financial inclusion, and assist local enterprises. E-commerce has many benefits, but its usage for Nigeria's sustainable growth remains predominantly low. The study adopts a traditional literature review and desktop content analysis approach and examines e-commerce for sustainable development in Nigeria, including challenges, potential, and prospects. The findings reveal that despite advances, infrastructural deficiencies hamper Nigerian e-commerce growth, particularly, frequent electricity outages and logistics, data and privacy concerns, digital inequality, high cost of data and security, environmental effects, legal and regulatory uncertainty, and poor road networks and lack of awareness and ignorance of e-commerce existence. The study concludes that Nigeria can maximise e-commerce for sustainable development by improving electricity outages, digital skills, financial inclusion, legal and regulatory framework efficiency, environmental impact, and building online trust and confidence.

articleTitle: Artificial Intelligence in Account Management: Innovation, Challenges, and Strategic Outlook
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Decision Aid Sciences and Applications (DASA)
abstract: This article presents the growing role of artificial intelligence (AI) in account management, through highlighting its increasing significance in computing and financial administration. AI is rapidly becoming a transformative tool across various sectors, and its application in tax administration presents both opportunities and challenges. The article explores AI-driven business opportunities, growth trends, and strategic planning within the field. in addition to address the critical technical, ethical, and legal considerations, including intellectual property rights, that must be navigated to ensure responsible and effective implementation.

articleTitle: Early Detection of Long COVID Symptoms from Social Media Using BERT
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Decision Aid Sciences and Applications (DASA)
abstract: The complex variability of Long-COVID symptoms often hampers effective disease management. These symptoms can persist long after infection and are often unrecorded in medical records, particularly in mild cases that do not require hospitalization. Social media texts offer diverse sources of information on emerging health conditions. Leveraging these data enhances our understanding of Long-COVID, making Natural Language Processing (NLP) techniques essential. This study introduces an NLP that uses BERT-based models to detect Long COVID symptoms in social media posts. Data from social media platform Twitter were collected using the keyword #LongCovid, followed by a multi-stage preprocessing process that included text cleaning and lexicon-based text filtering. Three models-BERT, BioBERT, and Bio+Clinical BERT-were fine-tuned and evaluated based on their F1 scores. The experimental results demonstrate that the general BERT model outperformed the domain-specific BioBERT and Bio+Clinical BERT models, achieving the highest F1 score in multi-label text classification with an F1 score of 89.90%. This finding highlights BERT's suitability for processing informal language on social media platforms and suggests that general-purpose language models may be more effective for health surveillance on these platforms than models pretrained on medical data. Our study contributes to academic understanding by demonstrating effective symptom identification for health monitoring, particularly of Long-COVID symptoms, from social media data.

articleTitle: Measuring the Variation of an Industrial Staple Manufacturing Process under 3-Dimensional Uncertainty Functions
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Decision Aid Sciences and Applications (DASA)
abstract: In the context of industrial staple manufacturing, maintaining high-quality standards is essential to ensure product consistency and dependability. Traditional statistical quality control (SQC) methods, such as <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\overline{X}-s$</tex> control charts, are often employed to monitor and control these processes. However, these methods may fall short in handling uncertainty and imprecise data observed in real-world manufacturing environments. This study introduces a novel approach by integrating picture fuzzy sets (PFSs) into <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\overline{X}-s$</tex> variable control charts (VCCs) to enhance their sensitivity and robustness in detecting variations in the manufacturing process. Since PFSs, characterized by membership, non-membership, and hesitancy functions, provide a more comprehensive framework for representing uncertainty, we aim to establish a more sensitive method for quality control, accommodating both quantitative measurements and qualitative judgments by incorporating it. The proposed picture fuzzy <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\overline{X}-s$</tex> control chart is applied to monitor mass variations in industrial staples, demonstrating their effectiveness in distinguishing in-control and out-of-control states, thereby offering a more flexible and informative approach to process monitoring and decision-making.

articleTitle: IoT Enabled Water Flow Management and Monitoring System for Hydroelectric Power Generation
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Decision Aid Sciences and Applications (DASA)
abstract: Water energy sources play a crucial role, particularly in providing electrical energy through hydroelectric power. Both the water flow rate and the water head determine the potential energy available from water. The hydroelectric system's energy generation directly depends on the water flow rate. A lower flow rate means less water is available to generate energy, even if the head is high. It is essential to increase the potential of the water flow so that it can generate enough electricity. Traditionally, the flow rate is restricted due to the limited capacity of single penstock. This work addresses this issue by introducing multiple penstock-based water flow management systems. Also, conventional water flow monitoring systems often face limitations, like relying on manual measurement, as it only provides periodic data, making it difficult to respond quickly to changes in flow conditions. IoT-based flow sensors leverage IoT technology to monitor water flow and transmit flow data in real-time, enabling operators to detect fluctuating flow conditions and implement timely adjustments to processes, therefore enhancing the overall efficiency. This work aims to design and develop an IoT-enabled prototype hydroelectric power generation system using multiple water flows for enhancing power generation efficiency. The prototype indicates the use of multiple pipes as penstocks in a dam. Additionally, if generating a significant amount of electricity is not required, the water flow can be discontinued, thereby automatically closing each pipeline. This work uses flow sensors, Kitsware software, Arduino IoT Cloud, and an LCD display to generate flow measurement data every ten seconds from multiple pipelines. Moreover, the system automatically generates Excel data and graphically represents multiple water flows, enabling the user to compare the water flow data. The completed work resulted in a hydropower system demonstrating enhanced output and effective compatibility with IoT for remote access.

articleTitle: Development of SecureNet Analyzer for Comprehensive Threat Detection
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Decision Aid Sciences and Applications (DASA)
abstract: SecureNet Analyzer is a familiar web application security analysis solution that provides an All in 1 scan type like IP, URL, Document Scan as well as Website Scan Space. Since the combination of diverse scanning features is performed through a single integrated interface, the platform allows users to search for security risks in digital assets and obtain clear, specific recommendations for effective problem-solving. In terms of the front end, the system is developed such that an operative of average security experience or training can easily operate. In addition, SecureNet Analyzer solutions can be easily integrated into a range of security contexts and then easily developed and adapted when needed to meet the needs of an organization or project. This flexibility makes it one of the security blocks that form the bedrock of security in any given digital setting. Through SecureNet Analyzer, the user can develop measures that will check their system as well as work towards preventing threats from developing in the first place, protect their assets from risks of copy by malicious people over the internet. Because of its ability to offer broad analysis on security the software is highly convenient when working in the digitally complex world of today.

articleTitle: The Impact of Digital Banking Innovations on Supply Chain Integration in the E-Commerce Sector in Saudi Arabia: A Qualitative Approach
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Decision Aid Sciences and Applications (DASA)
abstract: The enhancement of technology and the commitment to e-commerce under Saudi Arabia Vision 2030 drive progress in this realm. Thanks to digital banking innovations - fintech, blockchain and open banking solutions in particular that enable greater transparency, efficiency and security of supply chain integration - the industry experience rapid growth. In this paper, we investigate some examples of these innovations that are emerging in supply chain management and discuss whether they can benefit small or medium-sized enterprise (ISMEs). Drawing from industry background data collected and fresh research, we show in this report how these technologies have enabled the big leaguers inside large corporations to way more effectively extend their supply chain while smaller businesses continue to get curb stomped. The paper also considers the regulatory space; most notably the Saudi Arabian Monetary Authority and its open banking objectives. In this regard, we propose policy recommendations and future research areas in order to address these challenges better so that the adoption of digital banking technologies is extended.

articleTitle: Digital Transformation and Competitive Strategies: Insights Into Innovation, SMEs, and AI Startups
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Decision Aid Sciences and Applications (DASA)
abstract: This literature review examines the role of digital transformation in developing competitive strategies across diverse organizational contexts. With the advent of the digital era, organizations increasingly leverage digital technologies to enhance their competitiveness and adapt to evolving market dynamics. Through an analysis of recent research papers, this review explores key themes, including integrating traditional and digital strategic tools, the impact of digital competencies on open innovation, the competitiveness factors influencing AI technology-based startups, and the development of transformational digital strategies in SMEs. Findings highlight the importance of strategic decision-making, technological flexibility, collaboration efforts, and responsible management practices in navigating the complexities of digital transformation. Identified research gaps underscore the need for further exploration into areas such as the balance between responsiveness and responsibility, the integration of sustainability principles, and the adoption of innovative approaches to drive strategic change. Future research should delve deeper into factors such as motivation, global environment, and demographic variables to enhance our understanding of the evolving landscape of digital transformation and its implications for organizational competitiveness. This research contributes to the existing literature by providing insights into the evolving landscape of digital transformation and its implications for organizational competitiveness, thereby informing strategic decision-making and facilitating the adoption of effective digital strategies among diverse organizational contexts.

articleTitle: Design and Implementation of User Interface and User Experience in Digital Kanban Applications for Automotive Electrical Assembly Process with User-Centered Design Method
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Decision Aid Sciences and Applications (DASA)
abstract: The Kanban system is a methodology used to manage and track workflows to optimize production efficiency. This study investigates issues identified through observational analysis and retrospective reviews only to reveals many data abnormalities such as redundancy and loss of Kanban cards. These issues stem from non-real-time data consumption and prolonged Stock Transfer Order (STO) processes, which impede the achievement of production targets. The research aims to develop a software interface solution utilizing a User-Centered Design (UCD) approach, assessed through Usability Testing (UT) and the System Usability Scale (SUS). Evaluating usability to encompasses the aspects of Effectiveness, Efficiency, Memorability, Error, and Satisfaction. The results showed an Effectiveness of 93.3% with an increase of 3.03% on the second test, while Efficiency was recorded at 151.83 seconds to complete all the task and 70.23 seconds on the second test, a decrease in time across all the task resulting in a great Memorability while having the Error rate low at 17.8<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">%</sup> and 3.9% on the second test. Therefore, having the SUS to yield a score of 8.41, with a grade of A, indicating that it is acceptable and categorized as excellent.

articleTitle: Heuristic Iteration Approach for Load and Voltage Optimization in Single-Phase Distribution Systems at Three-Phase Transformers
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Decision Aid Sciences and Applications (DASA)
abstract: Load and voltage imbalances in single-phase low-voltage distribution systems are persistent challenges that often lead to increased neutral cur-rents, power losses, and equipment degradation. This paper introduces the Heuristic Deviation Percentage Iteration (HDPI) method as a novel approach to ef-fectively mitigate these issues. The HDPI method leverages 24-hour load data to iteratively redistribute imbalances between phases, achieving significant re-ductions in neutral currents and power losses while improving phase balance. A case study conducted on a distribution network in Indonesia demonstrates the method's effectiveness, achieving a reduction in phase imbalance from 13.44% to 3.75%, reducing neutral currents by up to 68%, and decreasing power losses by 45%. The methodology is computationally efficient, cost-effective, and designed for seamless integration with existing infrastructure, making it suitable for deployment in developing regions. This paper also explores the potential for integrating real-time IoT-based dynamic balancing solutions to enhance scala-bility and adaptability in complex grid systems. These findings underscore the HDPI method's potential to serve as a practical, scalable, and economical solution for improving the operational reliability and efficiency of distribution networks worldwide.

articleTitle: Multi-Stage Stochastic Models for Hydropower Generation in a Target-Priority Reservoir with Quasi-Dependent Inflows
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Decision Aid Sciences and Applications (DASA)
abstract: In this paper, we investigate the water reservoir operation problem under conditions of stochastic water inflows and exogenous operational constraints. The objective is to maximize the firm energy level while maintaining several operational reliabilities satisfied at a high level. A multistage stochastic programming model is formulated to specify release policies that are adapted to the uncertainty in the problem for shorter time periods. The model is designed to be flexible enough to be a planning or an operational tool. It is then solved by using stochastic dynamic programming (SDP) formulations with custom tailored algorithms that exploit the problem structure for a more efficient solution. The results and the simulation analysis show that the model solutions provide high levels for operational reliability while generating an optimal level of firm energy. The optimization-simulation framework provides energy authorities with tractable, yet efficient, models for short term water release schedules.

articleTitle: Impact of Image Pre-Processing on Skin Cancer Classification Melanoma Through Deep Learning
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Decision Aid Sciences and Applications (DASA)
abstract: Melanoma is a type of cancer that originates from melanocytes, which begins when melanocytes grow uncontrollably and form malignant tumors. Although rare, melanoma is highly lethal, causing 75% of deaths from skin cancer, despite accounting for only 4% of skin cancer cases. Therefore, an automated approach is needed to classify this disease. In melanoma classification, hair on the skin can interfere with image analysis by obstructing the details and shapes of the skin areas that need to be identified. To address this issue, a preprocessing scheme using the skin hair removal method is employed, which utilizes morphological features to recognize and remove hair contours, then restore the lost details with inpainting techniques. However, this process typically reduces the image quality and makes it slightly blurry. Therefore, this study also proposes the use of CLAHE (Contrast Limited Adaptive Histogram Equalization) preprocessing to enhance the sharpness of image details. The test results show that the developed model can effectively distinguish between normal skin and melanoma. The accuracy of the images after preprocessing is higher compared to the original images. The testing was evaluated based on accuracy, precision, recall, specificity, and F-score. For the original images, the accuracy for the ResNet-34 architecture is 94% and for EfficientNet-B0 it is 98.6%. Meanwhile, for the images with CLAHE preprocessing, the accuracy for both ResNet-34 and EfficientNet-B0 architectures reached 100%.

articleTitle: Integrated Weather Station with Air Pollution Station Prediction Using Convolutional Long Short-Term Memory (ConvLSTM) Method
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Decision Aid Sciences and Applications (DASA)
abstract: A major problem now facing Indonesian society is the increasing levels of air pollution and the deteriorating air conditions due to pollution. This pollution not only damages the environment and affects the climate, but can also have adverse effects on public health, such as respiratory diseases. This condition emphasizes the importance of measuring air pollution levels in various regions. This research aims to combine weather data and pollution data to predict air pollution levels. To get accurate data on weather conditions and pollution, a sophisticated technology is needed to support this research. The utilization of the Internet of Things (IoT) is one of the solutions used in this research and allows for efficient merging of weather and pollution data through the creation of IoT-based weather stations. The data will be analyzed using a quantitative approach, emphasizing the creation and application of the Convolutional Long Short-Term Memory (ConvLSTM) model. This model is particularly effective in understanding both the spatial and temporal aspects of the data. By using this approach, it is anticipated that predictions of air pollution levels will become more accurate and efficient than with traditional methods. Additionally, it aims to support informed decision-making for pollution control and raise public awareness about preventing air pollution.
